Title: The Edinburgh Revue Is All at Sea
Description: The Edinburgh Revue – the Titanic of comedy. Stately, sophisticated and with an iceberg in it. As the ship goes down, the orchestra plays one last tune. And that tune is sketch comedy. An hour of our finest material curated from across the year and put in a boat.
Artist: The Edinburgh Revue / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: In the heart of the Royal Mile, the Canons’ Gait Bar, Restaurant, ground floor and basement Cellar Bar – the original Free Fringe Venue for PBH’s Free Fringe Comedy.  Children welcome before 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access to bar 15 steps to performance area

Title: Sounds from Gold Coast
Description: African rhythms and harmonies in gospel arrangements performed by Ghanaian a cappella sensation. Passionate singing accompanied by dance steps and anecdotes will take you on an unforgettable journey into the heart and soul of the African continent. Alabaster Box comes to the Just Festival with its unique a cappella style of Christian music dubbed Afropella. It inculcates mouth-made sounds of African rhythms and harmonies with a message that employs African cultural symbols as tools to render the Christian faith. Passionate singing, brief African dance steps and anecdotes that link African cultural symbols to the Christian message.
Venue description: Just Festival events aim to challenge perceptions, celebrate differences and promote respectful dialogue. The conversations, talks, exhibitions and performances which constitute Just’s annual programme are designed to engage with topical local, national and international questions of social justice, equality and identity, including prejudice against race, ethnicity, class and economic status. Just explores these issues by creating safe spaces for dialogue and exchange between affected groups.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Gavin Webster: I Am Stand-Up Comedy
Description: What type of comedian are you Gav? Hard-hitting? Are you one of these edgy types that says the unsayable or a modern consumer complaints comedian? Maybe you’re surreal and are only capable of looking at things obtusely. What about one of those observational comedians that tell lovely stories about their knockabout lives. Shut up man, listen, I Am Stand-Up Comedy! 'Wonderfully surreal rants... few stand ups will be as palpably funny as this' ***** (Herald). ‘Simply a pleasure to spend time in his company’ **** (Comedy.co.uk). www.gavinwebster.co.uk
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Gavin Webster / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner from Stand 1, our little sister club is in its 19th year hosting the latest comedy talent. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area. For customers with access needs, the first floor is accessible by a steep flight of steps only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Stand 2 access is by a flight and a half of very steep stairs - 13 steps in total. We can assist as appropriate but this is our least accessible venue. Entry to venue via 16 North St. Andrew Street. Regretfully, staff are unable to assist electric wheelchairs

Title: All Hail the Poetry King!
Description: Award-winning silliness for all the family from one of the nation's most successful spoken word artists. Packed full of stinky pirates, deadly pugs and quick-fire raps, you'll never look at poetry in the same way again. Packed full of audience interaction and with a narrative that's shaped by the decisions of audience members, will you have what it takes to overthrow your Poetic Overlord? Viva la revolución! 'The English teacher you wish you had' (Fest). 'Emphatic, playful... terrific' (Guardian). 'He's not even a real King!' (Sam, aged 9).
Venue description: Having undergone a £1Million refurbishment Bourbon celebrates a unique bar/restaurant and nightclub space. The multi-purpose venue, open 7 days & nights a week during the Edinburgh Fringe, hosting a variety of PBH Free Fringe shows everyday.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Approx. 15 steps into the main bar. Once inside performance spaces are fully accessible

Title: David Callaghan: One for Sorrow, Two for Joy; Shoes
Description: A new stand-up show from David Callaghan. 'One of my highlights of the Fringe' **** (Scotsman). 'Far more original than many big comedy names' **** (EdFestMag.com). 'He really hits the mark, and scores' **** (TheReviewsHub.com). 'Callaghan does an excellent job... very funny routines' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Smart, rich, hilarious storytelling, underpinned by some fantastic jokes, give the really gifted comedian a rightful place as one of the freshest emerging talents' (Narc Magazine).
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Life on Venus
Description: True Arrow presents a series of scenes which readjust the balance of male to female dialogue by putting women front and centre with a multi-rolling cast of four women and one man. Come and celebrate everything girly, pink and ever so slightly catty.
Venue description: Located seconds from the Royal Mile and part of our 10 space strong Royal Mile performance hub. Two intimate spaces host an array of new and established work from small scale theatre to spoken word, sketch, stand-up and chat. Also the home of 'YourSpace' the festivals very own production house for performers.  For more info on Shows and YourSpace see : www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: I Ran With the Gang: The Story of Alan Longmuir, the Original Bay City Roller
Description: Returning for its fifth year, the smash-hit, sell-out show returns to Edinburgh! Written and directed by award-winning playwright Liam Rudden and featuring the hit Bay City Rollers songs Bye Bye Baby, All of Me Loves All of You, Keep on Dancing, Summerlove Sensation, Saturday Night, Give a Little Love and Shang-a-Lang. So, don your tartan and get ready to run with the gang! It's shang-a-lang-a-tastic! Rollermania is back! 'Fantastic night of nostalgia!' (Edinburgh Evening News).
Venue description: An intimate venue on the first floor of Le Monde with 100 seats. Up Close and Personal performances in a fabulous air conditioned venue with full bar and restaurant facilities. Located on George Street in the heart of the New Town, very close to Assembly Rooms and St Andrew's Square.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are a few steps outside the venue to negotiate before reaching the main areas. Our team will be pleased to assist where possible

Title: Allan Taylor
Description: Allan Taylor is the consummate professional who has taken songwriting to a high level. Poetry with music: over 40 years touring worldwide, more than 150 artists have recorded his songs. He has recorded more than 20 albums and continues to tour throughout Europe, performing at major arts centres and festivals. His songs encapsulate the realism of otherwise unsung heroes and their uncharted lives. 'Beautifully crafted, worldly-wise songs' (Scotsman). As Allan says before each show: 'Sit back and enjoy the journey'.
Venue description: The venue is on the ground floor of a classic 200 year-old Georgian townhouse looking north across the Forth from Calton Hill
Venue accessibility: The venue does not have a lift. The basement bar is essentially inaccessible to wheelchairs. First level dressing rooms are accessible only by stairs. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Royal Terrace is up a gradient from the top of Leith Walk/London Road. The basement entrance is accessed by stone steps down from street level. The main entrance to the building has four stone steps up from the pavement

Title: TwentyTwelve – Free
Description: Colin's life has been a series of well-meaning mishaps and misunderstandings. He'd somehow managed to get by without too much drama... that was until 2012 when it all came crashing down. What happened? Come and find out.
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: The Lost Matriarch 2
Description: Chuckle award runner-up (1998) Berlinda will take you on a journey to The Lost Matriarch, leaving behind all you have ever known about gender. In the upside-down world of TLM2, women are fasculine and men are meminine. Yes you heard correctly. Ladies dominate building sites, pay for lap dances and give their daughters guns to play with. But men are fed up with paying more for a haircut, they want change! How long can these inequalities last? How can anyone express their true sexentity? Who am I? Will Berlinda ever tell a funny joke?
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. More info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Mirth in the Morning With Rhodders
Description: Want some comedy with your coffee? Start the day with stand-up comic, radio host and oddball Rhodders, for an hour of Mirth in the Morning. Brought to you by Reading’s Stand and Deliver Comedy Club, you can expect today’s best mix of comedic acts. You’ll see everyone from seasoned comics to the freshest up-and-coming talent. You never know who might turn up! 'Rhodders is without doubt one of the freshest, most original and funny comedians working the circuit at the moment' (Matt Fox, Director of the Swindon Fringe Festival).
Artist: Stand and Deliver Comedy / Free Festival
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Cosmic Comedy Berlin
Description: Come and join us for a wunderbar time at Cosmic Comedy Berlin. Laugh your lederhosen off at a wide range of topics by some of the best comics from the Berlin English comedy scene. They will be sharing humorous stories of living, working and partying in one of the most popular cities in the world. Find out what makes Berlin so special and distinct. We will also be having international guests popping in and giving everyone a Super-Überraschung. You don't have to be German or Berliner to find it funny, just be able to laugh!
Artist: Dharmander Singh / Neil Numb / Free Festival
Venue description: One of Edinburgh's flagship free venues, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, there are free shows all day, and a free nightclub until 5am across our 5 floors of rooms and bars. Come an explore!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: Aidan Greene: Stutter Island
Description: Award-winning comedian Aidan Greene never liked horror films. Until he realised he was living in one. But is he the hero or the monster? Come learn why monsters aren’t always what you think, how speaking Irish can become illegal, and why sticks and stones can break bones but words can break your spirit. Stutter Island is unlike any place you’ve been before. 'Aidan Greene stands alone as one of the most remarkable stand-ups working today' (TheCatLaughs.com).
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: Departure Date
Description: David is bumbling his way through life when suddenly he discovers he only has one day left to live! With nothing left to lose he arranges a date with the girl of his dreams. As time is running out, will he find the courage to seize his last chance for love? With the help of his self-absorbed sister, a drunken best friend and an aggressive prostitute what could possibly go wrong? A laugh-out-loud story of desire, desperation and despair. Told with acidic wit, big heart and a wry smile.
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Great stylish on site bars too. For more info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Power, Fame and Sex
Description: As old as humanity itself. As well known as gods. Pillars of our society. But what happens if they are forced to face each other, society’s judgments and – worst of all – themselves? Three powerful personifications trying to show society who and what they really are while getting tangled up more and more in their complicated relationships with each other and their own inescapable natures.
Warnings: Adult themes, strong language
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The pedestrian route available from the Royal Mile is wheelchair accessible

Title: Davey Reilly: Disposable Camera
Description: A stand-up show about a stolen camera, what was on it and what it represents. Davey Reilly presents a new hour of comedy exploring curiosity, potential and Russian spies. Davey has been described as 'the future of Irish comedy' by Rich Hall, a 'liberal cuck' by countless members of the far-right online, and has appeared on RTÉ, BBC, MTV, and Facts, among others. 'It’s amazing to watch a one-man comedy gig achieve what often takes a whole cast, elaborate set and theatrical conceit' (Meg.ie).
Warnings: Accessibility: Two sets of stairs to reach venue.
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: Wings
Description: Eva is a stand-up comedian. James is head-writer for hit sitcom Flat Pancake. Their relationship is hilarious. So hilarious that it's falling apart. And there's nothing funny about that. Today, Eva has the gig of all gigs, and James has to stop her, because this time all the jokes are about him. 'Go see this play whenever and wherever it is performed' (BrumRadio.com). 'An innovative and charming piece that guarantees the audience laughs and silliness' (Redbrick.me). A comedy about love. A love story about comedy. The most you’ll laugh while having your heart broken. Or vice versa.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue with five rooms of free shows running throughout the day and night, all located around a vibrant and buzzing courtyard in the middle of Cowgate. With a huge drinks selection, a wide bar menu, and a courtyard full of street-food tents and cocktail huts. Shows run from 10am to 2am, with music through until 5am.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Mark Simmons – One-Linererer
Description: Following last year's Amused Moose: Best Show nomination for One-Linerer, Mark Simmons presents the hotly anticipated One-Linererer. This is a show for people who like jokes. Lots of jokes. Rob Brydon Tour support 2018 and featured in Dave's Top 10 Jokes of the Fringe. As seen on BBC Three's One for the Road. 'Master of one liners' ***** (One4Review.co.uk). 'A talented comic with an artisan's grasp of joke-writing' **** (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Afternoon Concerts at 3.30
Description: Performers: Theresa Burton (recorder), Aisling Kenny (soprano), Ursula Schlapp (viola da gamba), Katie Johnston (cello), Ailsa Aitkenhead (piano), Annemarie Klein (recorder), Dorien Schouten (harpsichord), Roxburgh Quartet, Turadh, Sean Webster (baritone), Ingrid Sawers (piano), Fyrish Quartet, Tatiana Plavans (viola), Simon Smith (piano), Hans Gál Trio, Musica Mundana, Emily Mitchell (soprano), Geoffrey Tanti (piano). Instrumental: music by Brahms, Schumann, Hans Gál, Leighton and Alkan; baroque concerts; a modern/traditional programme by Turadh. Vocal: cantatas by Telemann; songs by Schumann and Poulenc; settings of poetry from Houseman’s A Shropshire Lad.
Venue description: St Michael and All Saints (Scottish Episcopal) welcomes all to participate in its services, which are in the Anglo-Catholic tradition. The church choir is one of the best in Edinburgh, and you will be able to be an observer or participant in our Sunday High Masses during the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Rosie Sings – Facts About Love!
Description: Rosie shares Facts About Love from her own life. Through songs and banter Rosie talks dating apps, turning 30 and why she can't wait to get married to Batman. 'The voice of an angel, mouth of a sailor' (Jamie Anderson). 'Stunning beauty, irrepressible panache and elegance' **** (Mark ‘Divine’ Calvert). 2017 Audience reviews: 'Really funny and engaging show, what an amazing voice and well written songs and jokes' ***** (Ben Hartley). 'I was laughing, nearly crying and came away from it singing the songs for the rest of the day' ***** (Lara Fabiani).
Warnings: Strong Language
Venue description: Finger's Piano Bar is an institution established in the early 80s. During the Free Fringe shows Finger's turns into one of the best cosmopolitan venues in Edinburgh. An experience not to be missed! Opening hours 2pm till 5am. No disabled access. Age restriction 18+.

Title: Simon Kempston
Description: Following previous five-star reviews, this unique talent returns to perform thought-provoking, evocative, original songs in a wonderfully intimate setting. His beautifully crafted folk-tinged material showcases his incredible, distinctive and intricate fingerstyle guitar work – an exciting blend of the folk-baroque, blues and classical styles, and his gently nuanced, compelling tenor vocals. An inspiring, poetic lyricist, Simon's live performances are intense and impassioned, the subject matter chiefly Scottish, yet with universal appeal. These special hometown concerts are not to be missed. 'One of Scotland's very best singer-songwriters' (Sunday Herald). 'Stunning talent' (@WeAreSTV). Beautiful tunes, infinitely talented' (BBC Radio 3).
Warnings: Age restriction is as a result of venue policy rather than anything relating to the content of the show.
Venue description: One of Edinburgh's key folk hubs, the hospitable Royal Oak is a traditional bar frequented by musicians, enthusiasts and regulars in for a blether. 18+ licence restriction.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Juliet Meyers: Year of the Dog
Description: The dog got a sitcom. She got rabies while cycling in Central America. The ongoing adventures of Juliet (writer on The Sarah Millican Television Programme and 8 out of 10 Cats) and her co-star Homer the rescue dog. Contains stand-up, stories and the actual dog as he doesn’t like being left/left out. This is a show about learning new tricks, popularity, travelling, a bit about cycling, and loving (and cursing) a dog! 'Smart and very funny!' (Independent). 'Devilish… on the edge!' **** (Scotsman). 'Quirky and original' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Insightful' (GQ). Sold-out shows 2016, 2017.
Venue description: As a brand new cocktail and coffee experience Harry’s Southside is the perfect place to spend a morning, afternoon or evening. A stylish and intimate bar (formally known as the Meadow Bar & Southside Social) Harry's is Edinburgh's first social enterprise bar.  So come in, pull up a chair and give back to your community and others across the globe while enjoying great free Fringe shows.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. 1 steps into the venue from pavement

Title: Sameer Katz: Treesonous Thoughts
Description: Tired of watching middle-class white boys try to be funny? Come watch a middle-class brown boy (who grew up in a white society) try to be funny! After performing alongside the Cambridge Footlights, at the Comedy Store and Angel Comedy, to name a few, Sameer is bringing his third show to the Fringe! He provides his hilarious take on race, society and little things you never noticed. Amused Moose National New Comic Award semi-finalist 2018. 'We were blown away' (WolfsonHowler.co.uk). 'Very accomplished ad libs' (NottsComedyReview.wordpress.com). 'What a soothing voice' (Barry Ferns, Angel Comedy).
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Eliza's Big Adventure!
Description: Oh no, Eliza the explorer has been kicked out of her kingdom! She needs to go on an adventure to prove she is the best explorer and make it back in time for the summer celebration. Come and join her on her adventure as she dances with monkeys, makes friends with a sea princess and has a strange encounter with some aliens! Will she get back in enough time?
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue, In another unrivaled location we present the ultimate powerhouse of live performance. Part of our 8 space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter. A pulsating programme of cross genre performance art, the festival's largest programme of new writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information . Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Three ground floor theatres, lift to Grand Theatre. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. On approach there are ramps to the venue box office

Title: Punel Show
Description: Ever pundered what shows like Have I Got News For You, Mock the Week, QI or Never Mind the Buzzcocks would be like if they were just puns? Punder no longer. Darren Walsh (BBC iWonder, Dave's Joke of the Fringe) and Mark Simmons (The Mirror's Joke of the Fringe, Seann Walsh tour support) join forces to present the Punel Show: a new panel game focused on puns and general silliness. 'This is a masterclass in fast paced puns' ***** (BunburyMagazine.com).
Artist: Mark Simmons and Darren Walsh / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with a cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy, ballroom and space 3 will be used during the festival by some of the best PBH Free Fringe performers on the cabaret and comedy circuit.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Wakey Wakey
Description: Four twenty-something-year-old friends come back to their hometown to celebrate the life of Jessica, their best friend’s late wife. Tom, a vicar in training with an alcohol problem; Alexander, who for some reason is wearing a wedding dress; Alexandra, a nymphomaniac with little tact; and Trent, an immature man-child with as many manners as a teaspoon. Luke hasn’t seen his two best friends, Tom and Alexander, since marrying the love of his life, and now she’s dead. That’s fun. Hoping to give her the send-off she deserves, he invites all of his friends to support him.
Warnings: Adult themes and strong language.
Venue description: Next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall, SpaceTriplex makes up part of our fabulously smart destination hub of eight performance spaces located right at the heart of the modern fringe and offering an unmissable platform of diverse live performance. Music, Dance, Theatre, Physical Theatre, A-capella, opera, comedy and cabaret. All you need in the perfect environment.   For more information . Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Its on a flat pavement, corner of Hill Square and Nicholson Street. The venue has 3 floors all easily accessible via a lift

Title: Festival Masses
Description: Come and listen to uplifting music performed in its liturgical context by one of Edinburgh's best church choirs in the glorious setting of this church. Composers include Mozart, Morales, Gorecki, Pekiel and Haydn.
Artist: Choir of St Michael and All Saints
Venue description: St Michael and All Saints (Scottish Episcopal) welcomes all to participate in its services, which are in the Anglo-Catholic tradition. The church choir is one of the best in Edinburgh, and you will be able to be an observer or participant in our Sunday High Masses during the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Around the World with Bessy – Part One and a Half: Bessy Goes Busking!
Description: After receiving her sell-out garland in 2017, Bessy returns to the Fringe with a brand-new show. Bessy is saving up for her next big trip and decides to try busking at the famous Edinburgh Festival Fringe to earn the money for her plane ticket. However, busking isn't as easy as she thought... Come and meet Bessy and her new friends Spud 'n' Spencer Spoon, who help her out. Join in with their music and hear about their adventures in this fun, interactive, musical show!
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Accessible entry is on the left from main doors. If not taking the ramp there are a few steps from the pavement to the main door

Title: The Cutting Room
Description: An improvised comedy where a one-word audience suggestion inspires rapidly unfolding scenes. Somehow the players draw a story out of the chaos. Captivating cul-de-sac or part of the main plot? The truth is nobody knows how it will end until the final cut. An improvised comedy journey that could, potentially, go anywhere. Driven by a one-word audience suggestion The Cutting Room can take you where no one has gone before. A unique comedy experience with a different show every day.
Venue description: In the heart of the Royal Mile, the Canons’ Gait Bar, Restaurant, ground floor and basement Cellar Bar – the original Free Fringe Venue for PBH’s Free Fringe Comedy.  Children welcome before 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access to bar 15 steps to performance area

Title: It'll Probably Be Alright
Description: Dan tries to figure out when exactly one crosses the threshold into adulthood, and how long one must stay there before performing a U-turn, grabbing a milkshake and watching cartoons. Warning: this show is not suitable for those of a responsible disposition.
Warnings: Some strong language
Venue description: Situated on the bustling city centre street, at the foot of Edinburgh Castle sandwiched between the stylish West-end district and the ever popular Bruntsfield. Moriarty‘s is a place where you can relax in stylish yet homely surroundings. The carefully refurbished bar has a Sherlock Holmes theme upstairs with our focus on Craft Beers, World Lagers and Malt Whisky.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Beach Hunks: Leg Day
Description: Toned. Honed. Hunked. Chipper sketch lads Beach Hunks stride leggily to Edinburgh with a fast-paced hour of daft sketch carnage. Roll out the bunting and pray for rain as the Hunks celebrate the most special day of the year with a ceaseless parade of reprehensible characters and whip-smart gags. Limber up. Lunge forth. Whatever you do, don’t skip Leg Day.  ‘High energy physicality... had me in hysterics’ **** (Serena Bhandari). 'Bold and unusual' ****, Top 10 Shows of the Fringe 2016 (WestEndWilma.com).

Award-winning jazz vocalist, washboarder and early jazz historian Ali resurrects the original outspoken blues and jazz divas who shaped today's music via their passionate, dangerous songs. Scotland’s 'queen of vintage jazz' (OCWeekly.com) offers an authentic and fun journey back through time to celebrate these groundbreaking (yet forgotten!) first ladies of song. 'A masterclass in real grassroots jazz' ***** (Edinburgh49.org). 'Astounding vocals' ***** (San Diego Union-Tribune). 'A musical storyteller' (Scotsman). 'No other singer can deliver this kind of material with such authenticity' (BBC Jazz House).
Artist: Ali Affleck and the Gin Mill Genies
Venue description: Popular and city centre bar promoting local products as well as worldwide beers, wines and cocktails in a uniquely friendly environment. Close to The Playhouse, the Outhouse is situated down a lane off Broughton Street. We boast a beer garden, quality music, reasonable prices, showing local artists and excellent shows during the Fringe. It's a hidden gem the locals want to keep to themselves! 18+ only. Dog Friendly.

Title: A Piece of Cake!
Description: Free cakes and laughs! What could be better? This is a lovely show that's all about having a nice time and enjoying nice things! Please come along, enjoy free homemade cakes and watch some of the loveliest comedians around.
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. Title: Holt and Talbot: Mansplaining Feminism
Description: Still talking to each other after last year's Edinburgh success with Holt and Talbot Can’t Stand The Sight Of Each Other, no one is more surprised than them. Rosie Holt is unable to grasp some of the concepts of feminism but over the course of an hour, through bickering, sketches and an audacious bit of mansplaining, Christian attempts to set her straight. 'Refreshing and very funny' (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Aroused my interest from the get-go' (FringeGuru.com).
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.

Award-winning vocalist Ali offers heartfelt homage to these self-made, trailblazing and musically vital women with her acclaimed band. Scotland’s ‘queen of vintage jazz’ (OCWeekly.com). 'Stunningly expressive' ***** (San Diego Union-Tribune). ‘A musical storyteller' (Scotsman). 'No other singer can deliver this kind of material with such authenticity and so swingingly' (BBC Jazz House). 'Astounding vocals ***** (San Diego Union-Tribune). 'Vivacious stage presence' (Herald). 'Outstanding' ***** (Edinburgh49.org). Early booking is advised for this intimate performance.
Artist: Ali Affleck and the Gin Mill Genies
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, multiple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed daily programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00-05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s own programme of excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!

Title: The Second Annual Black Comedy Showcase
Description: After the success of the First Annual Black Comedy Showcase, we're back – bigger, better and blacker. Featuring the best black comics from around the globe with a different line-up every day, the show is what it would look like if MLK and Bernard Manning had a bastard love child who put on a stand-up comedy cabaret. With black bingo and a vegan meat raffle we're also helping diversity by giving a straight white male comic a chance that they rarely get. All audience members will receive a one-day not a racist pass. #blackcomedymatters
Venue description: Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. With live music six nights a week, and a host of other events constantly on the go, it's proved a firm favorite with locals and tourists for many years now. Open from 12:00-01:00 every day, apart from Sundays when we open at 12:30. No under 18's. www.bannermanslive.co.uk

Title: Red and Boiling
Description: Lesbian porn! Just kidding, for once we tell our own narrative. Drag duo, Hasadick and Rosay, will take you through a world of striking shadow puppetry using comedy and lip sync. Based on hours of interviews, they explore the lives of queer womyn and non-binary individuals from different countries, religions, ethnicities, and ages. Come laugh, celebrate and rediscover your identity with us. Every performance changes as new testimonies are shared verbatim. If you share your story with us, it might be in our show the next day. Follow our podcast #redandboiling. It’s queer and it’s magic!
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Rick Molland, resident compere of Edinburgh’s award-winning Monkey Barrel Comedy Club, presents an ever changing line-up of some of the best comics this year’s Fringe has to offer, all crammed into an hour. A little bit later, a little bit looser, even f*cking funnier. 'Rick Molland is perfect for the role of compere' (ThreeWeeks).

Soon all three are bound together by an existential crisis. Can two frogs and a metal puppet escape the restless human condition? Absurdist mask work and puppetry highlight this surreal domestic story about sex, sickness and survival.

Description: It’s April 2015 and the Baltimore Riots have only just begun. As the city fights to end police brutality, interracial couple Michael and Eva struggle to hold on to each other. Tensions mount over colonial attitudes, Freddie Gray’s controversial death and the beginnings of a monumental racial justice movement that sweeps the country. A new original play, Man Down, is a tender, sometimes uncomfortable, examination of love in the light of racial violence. Follow @ManDownthePlay #MyManDown.

Andrea leads her Love Police jazz band with sassy, sultry, silken vocals, witty lyrics and enchanting melodies to a 21st-century speakeasy world and the golden age of jazz! An award-winning Memphis, Tennessee-born, songwriter/singer/guitarist, Andrea blends musical adventure, intrigue and the sensitive wonders of the human heart. Title: Britain, Let's Talk About the Golliwogs
Description: ***** (Scotsman, 2017). Let's chat about your race relations issue. Who better with than a Samoan/Welsh comedian from New Zealand? Focusing on Britain's unique history with the golliwog, it's all about addressing the mixed-race elephant in the room... when the elephant is staring at a racially-triggering doll. Where do they come from? What do they mean? Can you own one? No, but really, can you? Following a critically acclaimed 2017 run at The Stand, James Nokise returns to Edinburgh after touring the world and is keen to chat.

Title: She Wolf
Description: Daughter, princess, wife, queen, mother, warmonger, widow and crone... monster? Queen Margaret of Anjou – the original Cersei Lannister; model for Claire Underwood; a woman so cutthroat and cold she would make Lady Macbeth sh*t her pants. Only none of that is true and the way we view women in positions of power hasn't changed much. Shakespeare wasn’t a god, he was just a man. His biases and prejudices are our biases and prejudices. Don’t miss this acclaimed comedic commentary on Shakespeare’s propaganda from award-winning comedian, actor and writer, Gillian English.
Warnings: Occasional strong language.

'Voice like Debbie Harry' (Scotsman). Since Queen's 2017 sell-out show based on Arts Council funded research, this is a fiercer, darker performance that embraces everything from Mary Magdalene via #MeToo to RuPaul. An audience-empowering ride exploring life on the front line of gender politics. Marysia's a stunning entertainer whose Singing Psychic stormed the Fringe, toured Europe, earned five-star reviews and featured at the Brit Awards.

Title: The Island
Description: The Island is an award-winning and acclaimed apartheid-era play written by Athol Fugard, John Kani and Winston Ntshona. Set on Robben Island and telling a moving story celebrating hope, passion and resilience. Two cellmates perform futile physical labour by day while rehearsing a makeshift performance of Sophocles’ play Antigone by night. The play draws parallels between Antigone’s situation and the situation of black political prisoners. Directed by Chris Weare, the production stars Siya Mayola and Luntu Masiza. Supported by the Scottish Episcopal Church.
Artist: Chris Weare, Siya Mayola, Luntu Masiza
Venue description: Just Festival events aim to challenge perceptions, celebrate differences and promote respectful dialogue. The conversations, talks, exhibitions and performances which constitute Just’s annual programme are designed to engage with topical local, national and international questions of social justice, equality and identity, including prejudice against race, ethnicity, class and economic status. Just explores these issues by creating safe spaces for dialogue and exchange between affected groups.

Bursting with emotion and explosive rhythms, this is a fiesta of pure dance, music and intensity. ***** (ThreeWeeks). Two spontaneous dancers, two passionate singers, one excellent percussionist have the audience immediately in their thrall and the show seems to end too quickly. The intimate venue only serves to enhance the immediacy of the performance – there is absolutely nothing in the way between performer and audience. An excellent Flamenco experience, generous of spirit and coming directly from the heart.

Title: Rich Wilson's Still Relevant
Description: Rich Wilson is still very much relevant, even though he's over 40. Regarded as one of the UK's finest circuit comedians, he's been making his living from comedy for 13 years even though you've never heard of him. Sell-out shows in Melbourne, Perth, Auckland and NZ and queues out the door at last year's Edinburgh Fringe. Best International Act winner (2016) and nominee (2017) at NZ Comedy Festival. 'A very very funny man' (Frank Skinner). 'Highly entertaining' (Time Out). **** (FemaleFirst.co.uk).
Venue description: Sneaky Pete's is a one room club located on the Cowgate, with guest DJs playing throughout the week as well as at weekends. Sneaky Pete's has a full schedule of PBH Free Fringe comedy every day during the Fringe from 12noon-11pm. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible

Title: Still Got It
Description: Raymond Mearns and Gary Little have Still Got It! Between them they've nearly 40 years experience in stand-up comedy and at an age where most are coasting to retirement, Raymond and Gary are just getting warmed up! This year they've joined forces to bring you a blistering hour of stand-up, brimming with great stories, awesome observations and improvisation which will leave you in no doubt why they are regarded as two of the very best headline comedians in Scotland. Gary 'runs rings round his comedy peers' (Herald). 'Raymond is an improvisational genius' (Frankie Boyle).
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving great food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Our two dedicated 50-seat performance spaces, presenting some of the best home-grown comedy at the Festival, are on the first and second floors.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Hummingbirds A Cappella: Voices
Description: The University of St Andrews' all-female a cappella group present Voices. Our human connection to music is visceral and transformational. In this show we express our individual stories and memories of that relationship through song. An anthology of contemporary a cappella, choral singing, traditional Swedish hymns and Welsh folk songs come together as The Hummingbirds showcase the incredible variety of ways that music weaves its way into our souls and hearts as told through our own voices.
Artist: The Hummingbirds in association with Mermaids
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Great stylish on site bars too. For more info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Wip It!
Description: Wip It! A split hour of stand-up, storytelling, characters, raps and musical comedy. Come and see an hour of tested and new material with two of the three Wip It! girls performing each night. All performers are members of Soho Theatre Young Company. Jen Wakefield: 'A bright talent with a proud heritage' (List). One of the List's Top Picks of the Free Fringe 2017. Kirsty Mann: Funny Women Awards finalist 2016. 'A smart character comic' (Scotsman). Isobel Rogers: 'Brilliant wit... clever songwriting... complex, funny and moving' (AYoungerTheatre.com). 'A blissful mix of satire and performance... truly unique' (Roundhouse, London).
Artist: Jen Wakefield, Kirsty Mann, Isobel Rogers / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A friendly neighbourhood bar with a great choice of craft, cask beers, wines and spirits, friendly staff and a delicious new menu. Last orders during Fringe 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-Midnight.

Title: Henry Café: Quiz Machine
Description: Henry Café, quiz host and death investigator, investigates death and hosts a quiz. To catch a killer, sometimes you have to think like a killer. Sometimes you have to host a pub quiz. Character comedy from Henry Café. 'Baffling but really kind of wonderful' **** (List). 'Hysterical and bizarre' (BarcelonaConnect.com). 'Time well spent indeed' **** (ThreeWeeks). **** (BunburyMagazine.com). **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Title: Slacker-in-Law
Description: How far would you go to impress your future mother-in-law? Returning to the Fringe following his previous sell-out run, award-winning poet/teacher/battle rapper Mark brings a show packed full of comedy, poems, rap and... pugs. Featuring an unpredictable choose-your-own-adventure poem with over 6 million outcomes and a hip hop journey through all the baddies of your childhood, he's working his ass off, but will it ever be enough? 'Precision-built to reach out to a live audience' (Guardian). 'The writing’s so sharp... absolutely priceless' (Scotsman). 'Epic' (Ice Cube). 'Surely you can do better than this...' (Sally, mother-in-law).
Venue description: Having undergone a £1Million refurbishment Bourbon celebrates a unique bar/restaurant and nightclub space. The multi-purpose venue, open 7 days & nights a week during the Edinburgh Fringe, hosting a variety of PBH Free Fringe shows everyday.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Approx. 15 steps into the main bar. Once inside performance spaces are fully accessible

Title: The Creative Martyrs: After the Apocalypse
Description: The end of the world is nigh. Too late. Boom! But the show must go on, even after the Apocalypse! Join us, plucking and strumming, singing tales of the new world in our surviving, satirical kabarett, let us rise from the rubble together... The Martyrs, with the help of the audience, seek to discover what went wrong, what we can learn and to ultimately build a new civilisation around cabaret. But do the people really want to be civilised? All with the Martyrs’ usual irreverence, music, mime and interaction.
Artist: The Creative Martyr / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Finger's Piano Bar is an institution established in the early 80s. During the Free Fringe shows Finger's turns into one of the best cosmopolitan venues in Edinburgh. An experience not to be missed! Opening hours 2pm till 5am. No disabled access. Age restriction 18+.

Title: Louise Reay: Eraserhead
Description: The first show in Edinburgh was banned... and lawyers told her to can the second show. How will the third show fare? Eraserhead is the third instalment of award-winning comedian Louise Reay’s provocative trilogy on power and oppression. It’s a free country, isn’t it? Currently facing legal proceedings, Louise explores issues of free expression, censorship and oppression in modern Britain. Adelaide Fringe Best Emerging Artist winner 2017 (weekly). Best Comedy nominee Brighton Fringe 2017. Edinburgh Fringe Groundbreaker Award nominee 2016. 'Louise Reay can legitimately claim to be unique' (Independent). 'Truly fantastic, utterly out there' (Al Murray).
Venue description: The candle in the middle of two burning ends. A patchwork quilt of fair-trade coffees, 241 pizzas & magazines will get you through the day. It all begins to unravel again with a night-time tapestry of cocktails, craft beers and fine tunes - and a huge variety of free Fringe shows

Description: It's Fringe time again and I'm back at The Beehive. Since 2012, I've been doing my thing in that wee sweaty room at the top of the stairs and it's always a blast! If you've been before you know what I mean. I'll be delivering another great night of comedy for you. Title: Coccinellidae
Description: A six-foot woman and a sex doll take on femininity. In a world where femininity obsesses over smallness in size, voice, opinion and ambition, one six-foot woman and a sex doll smash through walls and ceilings to explore how women can embrace bigness in a big physical romp. An unapologetic exploration into the apologetic world of women, a defiant call to confidence. Coccinellidae combines clown, physical theatre, audio testimonies (big testimonies) of over 100 women exploring their bigness that are woven into the live soundscape. Coccinellidae joyously challenges us to celebrate our unique bigness.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. Title: Mickey Sharma's Mixed Blessings
Description: We live in an increasingly mixed world when it comes to race, sexuality, gender and families. After realising that when it comes to dating, Mickey has a definitive bias towards white women, it was time to take a deeper look into whether it was nature or nurture. Mickey asks some tough and, at times, uncomfortable questions of himself but its all in search of the truth.

Title: Dan Simpson: Worried Face Emoji
Description: If brevity is the soul of wit, then emoji is the funniest language on the planet. Or it should be. Stand-up poet Dan Simpson taps into the ideograms and idiocy of our modern anxieties with a little 'wordplay alchemy' (FringeReview.co.uk). 'Charmingly geeky' (Scotsman). Glastonbury and BBC regular returns to the Fringe with whip-smart words and playful performance. Praise for previous Fringe shows: 'The perfect antidote to the perpetual screen-burn of our internet-obsessed age' (Scotsman). Title: Renata Rosa
Description: A rare visit to the UK for this deeply expressive Brazilian singer-songwriter and her band. Renata plays the rabeca, a fiddle from Northeastern Brazil and northern Portugal, and calls it her ‘second voice’. With it she delves into polyphonic harmonies and unearths musical influences from many sources: European, African, Arab and indigenous Brazilian. Traditions and rhythms abound in a vibrant energetic performance. Nominated for Songlines Best Artist Award 2018, Renata’s joyful voice and masterful handling of the rabeca, accompanied by lively percussion make this a performance not to be missed! Bristol Branch will support.
Venue description: Fringe Venue 197.

Title: Diamond Comedy Club
Description: The Diamond Comedy Club is bringing some of the freshest voices in stand-up comedy to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe for an unmissable late-night party! Each night, a different line-up will take to the Counting House Ballroom stage, featuring performances by some of the funniest new comedians from the UK and Canada. Past Diamond Comedy Club shows have seen performances from Norman Lovett, Daliso Chaponda and Archie Kelly. Now, for the first time, we're bringing the experience to Edinburgh! Every show is free, and every show is different, so come on down for a night to remember!
Warnings: Language and Potentially Sensitive Content
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. Title: Ashley Storrie: Adulting
Description: Scotland's favourite funny girl and viral internet sensation Ashley Storrie returns to Edinburgh with a brand-new show about not growing up. With the world most likely ending quite soon, Ashley believes we should all have a laugh and be a bit more honest particularly about the myth of "adulthood"... nobody really grows up, we're just great at pretending! 'A total revelation' (Dawn French). 'With funny witty one-liners which are as hilarious as they are true' (TheWeeReview.com). 'Breakout star of the Scottish comedy scene' (Skinny).

'Tightly written, suitably anarchic, and compulsive viewing' (TheLatest.co.uk) 'Comic brilliance!' **** (TheatreReviews.design). Title: Nick and Nina
Description: In the private visiting room of a Scottish prison, a fraught long-term friendship reaches its breaking point. Nick and Nina have been best friends since they were children, but now in their mid-twenties, life has gotten in the way – with the world constantly changing around them, how were they supposed to keep up? Neither knows that the other is struggling, and choose to cling to an image of their friend which is long outdated, until Nick's sudden arrest forces them to confront each other. They have one hour to catch up on a lifetime of secrets.
Warnings: Traumatic language - discussion of suicide/drug abuse

Title: Christian Reilly: Gig Economy
Description: Perrier Award-winning musical stand-up takes an axe to austerity and liquidates laughter deficits. 'Blisteringly funny' (Stage). 'If you're a fan of Bill Bailey or Rich Hall, you're a Christian Reilly fan already' (Guardian). 'Funniest songs I’ve heard in a long time' (Scotsman). 'Seriously funny' (Richard Herring). 'Like watching Jack Dee and Bill Bailey simultaneously... I don’t think I’ve ever come so close to hyperventilating with laughter' ***** (Student). 'Seriously catchy tunes... hysterical material' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'Amazingly high-quality' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Funny sonofabitch' (Rich Hall).
Warnings: Some adult themes and some strong language.

Under 18's, accompanied by a responsible adult, can attend suitable shows until 9pm.

Title: Eleanor Conway: Walk of Shame 2
Description: ‘…Conway is chaotic and electric’ **** (Skinny). ‘…A charm and energy you can’t learn’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). Fresh off the back of a 100-date, 10-country tour with her debut Walk of Shame, this award nominee returns with her hotly anticipated sequel about what happens when you stop chasing the ‘perfect’ version of you and realise she’s been right there all along.

Description: Billy Joel: Piano Man Live! showcases the very best of the dynamic songbook of the legendary Billy Joel. In under an hour, the five-piece band, led by sensational piano-vocalist and musical director Joe Revell, pay tribute to the iconic stadium sound of the original Piano Man. This loud, high-energy show features live brass and new arrangements of hit songs such as Movin' Out, New York State of Mind, and My Life. Don't miss out on this combination of high-quality stagecraft and impeccable musicianship.

Title: Robin Morgan: Honeymoon
Description: July: Robin gets married. Three days later: he goes away for a month, without his wife. Not exactly the ideal honeymoon, as is revealed in this follow up to the 2016 sell-out debut from The News Quiz (BBC Radio 4) writer, warm-up for The Graham Norton Show and tour support for Ellie Taylor. As seen on BBC Three. **** (Sunday Times). 'A phenomenal comic. Utterly hilarious' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Intelligent and hilarious. I highly recommend' (Joe Lycett).
Artist: So Comedy and Broken Robot Productions by arrangement with Troika
Venue description: The recently refurbished Pear Tree offers a huge selection of free shows during the day and bands indoors at night. Through the day there's also music on the outdoor courtyard stage, in a huge courtyard with outdoor bars and barbecue to enjoy your Fringe days and nights in. The venue is also linked to the Counting House which boasts four more theatres with more free shows all day and night.

Title: Burlesque
Description: Kick off your weekend as we mix you a heady cocktail of burlesque at Le Monde’s Dirty Martini Lounge. Prepare to have your thirst quenched by our line-up of international teasers. Whether you like your burlesque straight up vintage-style with a raucous bump’n’grind twist, a dash of sultry sirens, or a comedic chaser on the side, our sassy lads and lassies will leave you shaken and stirred.
Warnings: Strong language and scenes of a sexual nature.
Venue description: An intimate venue on the first floor of Le Monde with 100 seats. Up Close and Personal performances in a fabulous air conditioned venue with full bar and restaurant facilities. Title: Carmen: A Gender-Flipped Film Noir Fantasy
Description: Sultry and cool, Carmen is a gender-swapped film noir fantasy. Step into a world of drama, tension, sex and intrigue, where the struggle between good and evil is real and personal. Tough female detectives, baddies and a sultry homme fatale flirt, steal and kill in this stylish and intoxicating piece. Carmen is an improvised masterpiece, based on audience suggestions. The show is different every day and anything could happen. Come and see if the detective will solve her case, who the homme fatale seduces, and who will be left standing. A Nursery original production.
Venue description: A friendly local bar, with food and drinks available all day, and a welcoming atmosphere. The venue has been completely refurbished recently, and there's fringe shows daily in the upstairs room all day.

Title: We're Sorry Canadian Comedy Showcase
Description: This is the fourth year of We're Sorry. Showcasing Canadian talent performing or visiting the Fringe; you never know who is going to swing through. So fill your belly with poutine and bring a hockey stick for this fun show of Canuck comedians. Hosted by Evan Desmarais (@evancomedy).
Venue description: One of Edinburgh's flagship free venues, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, there are free shows all day, and a free nightclub until 5am across our 5 floors of rooms and bars. Come an explore!

Title: The Stand's Pick of the Fringe
Description: The Stand Comedy Club celebrates its 21st anniversary at the Edinburgh Fringe with the best of 20 years visiting the stage at New Town Theatre. Different line-up nightly!
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: Under new direction, New Town Theatre is heralding in a new Fringe age of outstanding Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Music and Interactive Game Play in the New Town area! Situated in the beautiful Freemasons' Hall, built in 1913 (on elegant George Street, between Assembly Rooms and the Edinburgh International Book Festival), the New Town Theatre is a must visit destination. A beautiful Fringe venue with well-equipped and comfortable theatre spaces.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Lower Hall and Studio also accessible from Rose Street North Lane. Level and Unfixed seating available

Title: The Weegies Have Stolen the One O'Clock Gun
Description: When Edinburgh’s famous One O’Clock Gun goes missing the city is outraged. When it appears to have been stolen by Glaswegians the ancient rivalry between the two cities threatens to turn ugly. Can Morningside Malcolm, the douce and respectable resident of Edinburgh’s pleasant suburbs, save the day? Of course he can! Robin Cairns returns to the Fringe with an hour of sheer entertainment. 'An absolute wee gem of a show' (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: Popular and city centre bar promoting local products as well as worldwide beers, wines and cocktails in a uniquely friendly environment. Close to The Playhouse, the Outhouse is situated down a lane off Broughton Street. We boast a beer garden, quality music, reasonable prices, showing local artists and excellent shows during the Fringe. It's a hidden gem the locals want to keep to themselves! 18+ only. Dog Friendly.
Venue accessibility: Please contact venue at info@outhouse-edinburgh to discuss specific access needs. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Title: Frank Lavender: Gotta Laugh
Description: Following his mother's tragic death (freak accident with a Bic Razor), the misogyny apologist and comedian par excellent presents his debut hour! 'Works the crowd like an Italian mama with pizza dough' (Scotsman). 'Peter Sutcliff was funnier' (Myra DuBois).
Artist: So Comedy / Broken Robot Productions / Corrie McGuire Management
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?

Title: MetaMafforphosis
Description: Maff Brown is an award-nominated comedian. He writes for Mock the Week and GQ magazine have put him in the top ten acts to see at the Fringe, twice! Come follow me on Twitter/Insta @maffbrown.

Title: Late-Night Lucky Bag
Description: Every night, a rising star of the comedy scene will curate their own night of comedy. Many acts will be making their Edinburgh Fringe debuts with these shows, including Montreal comic Jeff O'Brien whose credits include opening for Russell Peters, and Hannah Lawrence who regularly performs stand-up at the biggest clubs in Toronto. Also putting shows together are some of the UK's most exciting comedy prospects, including Lewis Costello who has supported the likes of Doug Stanhope and Ed Byrne, and rising star Hayden Allmark who is wowing audiences with his hilarious improv skills.
Venue description: Situated on the bustling city centre street, at the foot of Edinburgh Castle sandwiched between the stylish West-end district and the ever popular Bruntsfield. Moriarty‘s is a place where you can relax in stylish yet homely surroundings. The carefully refurbished bar has a Sherlock Holmes theme upstairs with our focus on Craft Beers, World Lagers and Malt Whisky.

Title: A Play, A Pie and A Pint
Description: We've all been there. The meal is over. It's time to settle up. But who had what? In this hilarious comedy from Robin Mitchell, two couples agree to split the bill, leading to confusion and laughs galore as their true personalities are revealed. In future, you'll agree to go Dutch! The 2015 Edinburgh Fringe hit returns. From the people who brought you last year's sell-out productions of Silence and Conflict In Court.
Venue description: An intimate venue on the first floor of Le Monde with 100 seats. Up Close and Personal performances in a fabulous air conditioned venue with full bar and restaurant facilities. Title: An Evening With Amanda F*cking Palmer
Description: The un-pinndownable musical force known as Amanda F*cking Palmer (Dresden Dolls, Eveyln Evelyn) returns to the Fringe, this time armed with only a piano and a ukulele. Palmer’s shows are a combination of uplifting, humorous and tear-jerking, often all in the same song. Expect special guests ranging from local musicians to celebrity friends and husbands (her author husband, Neil Gaiman, occasionally duets).
Venue description: The Queen's Hall is a 900-capacity music venue, situated on Clerk Street in the Southside of Edinburgh. Originally built in 1823 as Hope Park Chapel, it was converted to its current role in 1979. It now plays host to all types of live music, and presents approximately 200 performances every year.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is a stepped kerb from road to pavement - if a companion flags the attention of our staff, we'll be happy to assist in lifting any particularly heavy assisted mobility apparatus.

Title: Stand Up and Slam
Description: The battle is on! Six outstanding Fringe acts, one epic fight night. Who wins? You decide. The critically acclaimed showdown between poets and comedians is back for its third Edinburgh Fringe. Our resident team captains are joined by brand new guest acts every night. Pick your team, cast your vote and cheer them on to victory! ***** (TheReviewsHub.com). ***** (TheLatest.co.uk). ***** (Argus). **** (ThreeWeeks). **** (EdFestMag.com). 'A complete and utter winner' (TheReviewsHub.com). 'Witty, fast paced, and most importantly funny' (FringeReview.co.uk). 'Edgy, energetic comedy at its best' (Sunday Express).
Artist: Chatback Theatre and Comedy / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Movement nightclub is in the heart of the capital's nightlife, the club boasts a capacity just short of 500 and is one of the hot spots in its location. Every day, during the Fringe, we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe comedy. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No wheelchair accessible toilet. Level access throughout all of venue

Title: Carey Carey Quite Contrary
Description: Award-winning comedian Carey Marx is back with a new hour of hard-hitting stand-up. Taking a lesson from Donald Trump, Carey has become arrogant, certain and unapologetic. So this show is the best thing in history and sod anyone who disagrees. Writer and star of Intensive Carey, BBC Radio 4. 'Anecdotally debauched' ***** (Herald). 'A comic at his gleeful best' ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). 'Supremely crafted comedy' **** (List). 'Sharp, sweet, cheeky, cynical, romantic and rude as he ever was' **** (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: Whistlebinkies is a late night bar open until 5am during the Fringe. A popular viable alternative for any nocturnal drinkers wishing to avoid the clubs. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe comedy shows in our back room from 12noon. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There is a single step up and then 2 steps down into the bar form the Niddry street entrance. Access customer are advised to enter via Niddry street as George the 4th entrance has 15 steps down into the bar.

Title: Contini Live Lounge
Description: In the Contini Live Lounge we will be featuring an eclectic mix of genres from some of Scotland's top musicians. Whether it be the chilled sounds of singer/songwriter Kirsten Adamson, the laid back acoustic grooves of George Murray, the authentic guid folk of The Cognac Twins or the relaxed, popular covers of Mixtape, with many other artists to be announced, you are guaranteed an afternoon of beautiful music to set you up for your busy Fringe evenings.
Venue description: An independent, award-winning Italian restaurant in the heart of the New Town. Contemporary Italian food served from 8am until Late. Our family run restaurant sources the very best produce direct from Italy and around Scotland exclusively for you.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Wheelchair access ramp available, please ask our staff

Title: Ella Jean
Description: Ella Jean is no stranger to fear. 23 years old and 4200 miles from home, she's using the Fringe to cross off the last few fears on her list. She moved to London at 18 to improvise songs to audiences. She’s been on BBC Radio 3 with Abandoman, at BoomTown with Professor Elemental, and countless shows with hip hop band Unexpected Guests in London. She's dug into local music scenes from Lethbridge to Manchester, and knows how to navigate the treacherous world of comedy as a queer feminist. Her final fears include: balloons, love and your attention.
Warnings: Swearing and mature jokes.

Title: The Sound of Their Music
Description: An evening celebrating the legendary partnership of Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II. Relive the classic songs from Oklahoma!, South Pacific, Carousel, The King and I and, of course, The Sound of Music as well as items from their lesser-known works – performed by the principals and chorus of The Edinburgh Gilbert and Sullivan Society with their legendary directors, Alan Borthwick and David Lyle.

Title: Fred MacAulay and John Moloney
Description: With a friendship that has endured numerous governments, several economic downturns and expanding waist sizes, these two stand-ups join together to bring you a one-hour show which will provide a craftsman-like masterclass in stand-up comedy. Anecdotes, jokes, routines and even a song at the end. Why not do an hour each? 'Well – people do an hour in the hope of getting noticed by a TV producer. We’ve decided not to do that for a very good reason... we’ve both lost hope' (Fred MacAulay). 'A masterclass' (John Moloney).

All seating is unreserved and first come, first served.

Title: Say It Ain't Show
Description: Say it Ain’t Show is a brand-new show from Evan Desmarais about trying to adult while still being a child on the inside. It touches on expectations, passion and being okay with being overcome. This Canadian talent should not be skipped. 'Loud and in your face...' (BroadwayBaby.com). **** (GreatScott.media). **** (TheUpsideNews.com).

Title: Eddy Brimson: Fidgety Tits
Description: Some people are taking this comedy lark way too seriously. Not here. No message, no sob story, just 50 minutes of stand-up and stupidity from one of the most in-demand UK and international headline acts. Review from 2017: 'Sure fire laughs, breath-taking confidence and more. As close as you get to the perfect Fringe comedy hour' (Associated Press).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving great food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Our two dedicated 50-seat performance spaces, presenting some of the best home-grown comedy at the Festival, are on the first and second floors.

Title: Mark Watson: How You Can Almost Win (Work in Progress)
Description: Last year, Mark Watson – a man prone to considerable anxiety, with multiple phobias and a history of piss-poor self-esteem – was asked to go on Celebrity Island with Bear Grylls. It really wasn’t for him at all because his favourite things include safety, comfort, food and not being scared and miserable. But the experience changed the shambolic comedian for the better and now he's writing a sort of motivational talk about what it taught him. But still with jokes.

Description: The show isn't entirely about space, although it takes place in space. As all shows do but rarely acknowledge it. Whispers in the Cosmos is probably an existentialist quest wearing a stand up comedy costume.

Title: Nightpiece Film Festival
Description: Since 2014 we’ve platformed over 200 films giving premieres to shorts that have gone onto much bigger things in festivals across the world. Recent examples of films that began at Nightpiece include Keith Farrell's Rabbit Punch (2017), Ross Adgar's The Railway Carriage (2015) and Dan Sunley's Pieces (2016). Now in our fifth year we maintain continuity with the premiere of director Al Carretta’s 12th feature, the horror Th’dread Rattlin. Never funded or sponsored, we are a truly independent operation but we breathe indie film and present a curated selection of shorts from the UK and worldwide.
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue, In another unrivaled location we present the ultimate powerhouse of live performance. Part of our 8 space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter. A pulsating programme of cross genre performance art, the festival's largest programme of new writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information . Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Choking to Death on a Currant Bun
Description: It's like Dylan Thomas without the nice bits! Mr Brown Presents unveils its debut Fringe show all about the sordid private lives of a small town. Take a whirlwind tour around a strangely familiar dream world full of lusty policemen, kinky scrabble nights, obsessive knitting and lots of flour…

Title: India Flamenco
Description: The symbolic ritual of Indian dance is represented via a graceful routine which flows like a temple carving brought to life, then is followed by a flirtatious and celebratory gyspy dance, performed excellently by a lithe and expressively precise performer. The journey finds its destination in the fiery passion of flamenco, where the proud poise of el baile is accompanied by the impassioned singing of a male vocalist. All three dancers take to the stage in a fusion finale, in a fascinating display of the styles’ similarities and their differences. ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.
Venue description: Flamenco and world music/dance venue alongside a tasty Spanish tapas cafe/bar. The venue is located in the busy Southside area of Edinburgh, offering a programme of music, dance and story telling for adults and children. Great music, great Spanish food and a great atmosphere!

Title: Arnab Chanda: Stories from Arnab
Description: Arnab Chanda (Russell Howard's Good News, Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy, Chortle Best Newcomer Nominee 2007) quit stand-up in 2011. In his debut hour, he tells stories about what happened after that: broken dreams, death, getting alopecia and other hilarious topics. A mix of comedy and not-comedy. 'Star of tomorrow... he’s a rare talent on the UK circuit' (Herald). 'Arnab Chanda is the funniest person on earth' (Simon Amstell).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Andy Zaltzman: Right Questions. Wrong Answers.
Description: Zaltzman, host of long-running global hit podcast, The Bugle, returns to Edinburgh to (a) ask, (b) confront, (c) evade and (d) incorrectly respond to, the biggest questions facing our rightly renowned planet. He will apply his uniquely inventive satirical mind to questions such as: what on earth are we going to do about everything? And: why is the future so stroppy at the moment? Featuring the Concilicorp Arbitrax 3000, the world’s first compromise-generating robot and a talking cauliflower. 'Master satirist' (Time Out). 'Sparkling, intelligent comedy with a stupidly high joke count' (Melbourne Herald Sun).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Stand 4 is an intimate studio with exciting Fringe débuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.
Venue accessibility:
Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Staff always available to help and assist access customers where appropriate. 
Stand 3 & 4 are accessible from the pavement with steps leading to a courtyard. The venues are situated in the basement of the building. There are 15 steps in total with a 90 degree turn. Once inside the venue, Stand 4 is accessible on the flat with a right turn and Stand III has a further 3 steps

Title: A Holy Terror
Description: Joe Rooney is best known for his role in Father Ted as the rebel priest Father Damo. He has been performing stand-up for the last two decades from Moscow to Milwaukee and everywhere in between... okay, not everywhere. In his first solo Edinburgh show he talks about a passive aggressive Jesus, Catholic guilt and praying for a spider, interspersed with the occasional musical interlude. He is very good but then I would say that, because I am Joe Rooney, although not necessarily because I have my doubts.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Joe Rooney / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner from Stand 1, our little sister club is in its 19th year hosting the latest comedy talent. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area. For customers with access needs, the first floor is accessible by a steep flight of steps only.
