We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Description: Egg is a powerful and evocative new aerial theatre production from acclaimed circus theatre company Paper Doll Militia, a highly visual exploration of female fertility, sexuality and choice. Weaving together personal testimony, live original music and stunning aerial artistry, the piece takes audiences on a deeply personal and political journey, following the true story of a woman who gave her eggs to her friend to have a child. Paper Doll Militia are an Edinburgh/LA-based aerial theatre company, combining visual theatre with innovative aerial, acrobatic choreography and multimedia. Referred to as 'the sophisticated circus of now' (Edinburgh Review).

Title: Extinguished Things
Description: 'My neighbours leave their flat one morning but don't return. Al and Evie, married 40 years, no kids. I have their spare keys. I cannot resist.' Award-winning writer/performer Molly Taylor pieces together the story of two lives intertwined. Vivid and lyrical, Extinguished Things is a captivating exploration of what it means to spend your life with someone, and the nature of what you leave behind. 'Fragile and utterly beautiful… reminds us of the reason we're alive' ***** (Herald). 'A monologue of extraordinary exuberance and power' **** (Scotsman). Love Letters to the Public Transport System: Critics Circle Award, Adelaide.

Title: Never Vera Blue
Description: 'It's hard to know things, isn't it? Have you ever found that, it's really hard to know.' She's five foot ten. She's almost certain. But if she was the size she thinks she is she couldn't be here and if she doesn't even know her own dimensions, what hope is there at all? From the city to the Kent coast, from a war-torn land to the pit of the stomach, this unmissable new play follows one woman's journey to regain her identity and explores just what it means to be made to doubt yourself.

Title: Hidden Door present The Jesus and Mary Chain
Teaser: A special evening at the International Festival from Hidden Door as part of Light on the Shore with Edinburgh Gin Seaside at Leith Theatre.
Description:
Edinburgh multi-arts festival Hidden Door was instrumental in getting the long out-of-action Leith Theatre open to the public again, after years of being used as a council storage facility. So it seems only fitting that the organisers do their own one-night takeover of the magnificent venue, filling the space with film screenings, art installations and live music. 
Hailing from East Kilbride, The Jesus and Mary Chain shaped the era-defining fuzzy, shoegazey sound with their blissed-out Psychocandy in 1985, and toured it again on the album’s 30th anniversary. 
Honeyblood are a slacker-rock duo from Glasgow, celebrating girlhood through distorted guitars and woozy harmonies, and spreading a defiant message about women fending for themselves. 
Spinning Coin channel the gorgeous pastoral indie folk made famous by The Pastels and update it with their own dark, dreamy spin for modern audiences. Timings as follows:  
Doors Open 7.00 pm  
Spinning Coin 7.30 pm   
Honeyblood 8:15 pm  
The Jesus and the Mary Chain 9.30 pm  
Paradise Palms DJs 11.30 pmBar open until late!
The concert will finish by approximately 1.00 am. Please note these times are approximate and subject to change.

Subtitle: Apocalypse Now?
Teaser: While the world awaits the next moves of nations like Russia, North Korea, Iran and the USA, Rodric Braithwaite and Taylor Downing reflect on past times when the planet seemed on the edge of an apocalyptic precipice. Braithwaite’s Armageddon and...
Description: While the world awaits the next moves of nations like Russia, North Korea, Iran and the USA, Rodric Braithwaite and Taylor Downing reflect on past times when the planet seemed on the edge of an apocalyptic precipice. Braithwaite’s Armageddon and Paranoia deals with the nuclear confrontation from Hiroshima to the present day while Downing’s 1983 analyses the Soviet Union’s tense stand-off with Reagan’s America. A relevant discussion in worrying times.

Title: Waiting For It
Description: In this mystical Latin-American adventure, in a computer-dominated future, a machine creates two scientists in order to find 'it', plunging them into mythical lands to face fantastical creatures. A bird-mystic cures the audience of all their troubles in the jungle of a futuristic Latin-American continent. Audience members are invited to cross over into their world. Through mime, clown and magic-realism we reflect on what it is we spend our lives searching for.
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.

Title: Famous Puppet Death Scenes
Description: Behold: the eternal masterwork of puppetry for adults finally comes to Edinburgh! Willingly undergo a heart-wrenching parade of theatrical demises that will severely exacerbate your fear of death. All your favourite scenes are there: Edward’s Last Prance by Samuel Groanswallow, The Feverish Heart by Nordo Frot, Why I Am So Sad by Sally, and the unforgettable Bipsy’s Mistake from Bipsy and Mumu Go to the Zoo by Fun Freddy! 'Exquisite… boundless invention' (Variety Magazine). 'One of the best shows of the year… not to be missed' (Globe and Mail). 'Visually stunning and endlessly entertaining' (LA Times).
Warnings: Puppet nudity, unnecessary brutality to inanimate objects

It is a glimpse into the country through its most vital voices, through artists who take risks, who seek audiences and, ultimately push national and global conversations forward. CanadaHub is produced by Selfconscious Productions in partnership with the Canada Council for the Arts and in association with the High Commission of Canada.

Title: Best of Irish Comedian of the Year
Description: Totally sold-out shows across the globe. Three top Irish comics from the ICOTY finals. 'Sit down and roar with laughter for 60 minutes... side-splittingly funny' ***** (TheWest.com.au). 'Left my face in pain' (Sunday Times). Ireland's (possibly the world's) best compere Andrew Stanley introduces last year's winner Steve Bennett and a selection of finalists. 'It's rare to see a comic so clearly destined for the top, but with astonishingly good observational material delivered and timed to perfection, there's no doubt about the destination of the young Irishman's career' (Scotsman).

Title: Von's Midnight Madness
Description: The Antipodean madman known as Von, shall be performing his fabled loops upon his eight-string guitar and telling his extraordinary tales with a twist of adult comedy and burlesque upon the hour of midnight in the infamous Black Medicine Basement. Joining Von's array of colourful characters, he shall have local guest performers nightly, who will blow your mind with their tapestry of trickery and talent! This show will confuse, titillate and inspire! Audience participation encouraged and no two nights will be the same, so you'll have to cum at least twice!
Warnings: Nudity, male burlesque
Artist: Von Leon aka Miss Candy AppleBottom / PWYW

Lusciously lit, beautiful stone wall surroundings, peppered with plants and greenery, this is a delightful and fun cabaret space. Fully licensed bar serving quality Scottish beers, tropical spirits and exotic wines. Access from street level down stone steps straight into the action - with charming, helpful, professional staff.

Title: Bluff
Description: 'Our world is in order, a world in which there are unchangable truths that are valid to everybody.' Or maybe not? Maybe one starts to shiver at the thought that it could also be quite different. Can you feel the terryfing feeling of living in the wrong film? Step Mama Drama is based on true stories; step monsters and loving friends are included in this journey exploring the role of the stepmother often depicted as the evil stepmother or stepmonster. Allison became a stepmother 10 years ago and this new work looks at the many facets of being a step-parent or stepchild. She hopes that you will enjoy the joys and the dramas found in Step Mama Drama!
Warnings: Some adult content and themes.

Inspired by her favorite artist, award-winning musician Elsa Jean McTaggart returns with a brand-new show for 2018 – Eva Cassidy: The Story, after selling out many times in 2017. Using video, story and song, Elsa Jean McTaggart channels Eva Cassidy’s musical voice through her own. Elsa has devised this very special show to pay homage to this true interpreter of song. Title: Appropriately Inappropriate

So she gave up her dream and decided to give stand-up comedy a go. In this show, Thao shares observational humour and throws in many one-liners and funny stories. Dry, self-deprecating and politically incorrect, this is not a show for the easily triggered. A show that takes the PC out of stand-up comedy.
Venue description: As a brand new cocktail and coffee experience Harry’s Southside is the perfect place to spend a morning, afternoon or evening. We'll tell you about the city's history and especially about the characters and personalities who made Edinburgh what it is. Our guides are all local people who love our city and are only too pleased to share their knowledge and enthusiasm with you.

Warnings: Some strong language

Day-to-day life demands interaction with those who seek to attack or shame them, or are complicit in this.

Title: Alastair Savage, Scots Fiddle Old and New
Description: Alastair celebrates Scotland's magical fiddle tradition in the glorious Canongate Kirk acoustic. Joining him are long-time collaborators Euan Drysdale (guitar/piano) and Iain Crawford (double bass) alongside folk music legends Eddie McGuire (flute), Ewan Robertson (whistle) and Perthshire fiddle ace Pete Clark. Plaintive airs and swashbuckling reels combine for a colourful and moving journey of melody – ancient and modern. A festival highlight not to be missed. ‘Spectacular in simplicity, scope and delivery’ (FolkWords.com). ‘A must for aficionados, a primer for anyone with a notional interest in Scottish traditional music’ (Herald).

Title: Alastair Savage, Alone With History
Description: An afternoon concert series by one of Scotland's leading fiddle exponents. Alastair's heartfelt journey features a unique tribute to his fellow Ayrshire man Rabbie Burns alongside the magical melodies of 18th-century master Niel Gow and 19th-century virtuoso James Scott Skinner. An invigorating and soulful hour not to be missed. ‘There is a breathtaking effortlessness to Savage’s musical art: technical and intricate without ever overshadowing the music itself’ (Su O’Brien, BrightYoungFolk.com). 'Panache, grace and affection' (Jim Gilchrist, Scotsman). 'The fiddle shows both sweetness and granite strength in Savage's hands' (Alex Monaghan, LivingTradition.com).

Deeply affected by the recent demise of his cat Paul, Beaker decides to take his own life. But at the crucial moment, he receives one last urgent delivery. Anxious to complete his own "departure", Beaker is shocked when the bag begins to move...

Based on the 1991 Warner Brothers film, Dogfight takes audiences on a romantic and heartbreaking theatrical journey that stays with you long after the performance. With an impressive score and a genuine and charming soul, Dogfight is the perfect show to see this Fringe!

Becs is offered the chance to head up the party at Westminster. But her mum has early onset Alzheimers. Her best friend Nina and her teenage daughters need a bolthole. And Becs isn’t quite sure that she could do the job anyway. The party need her to go. Her family and friends need her to stay. Are women ever really free to choose?

Tom's third sell-out show sees him taking a jaunt into the unknown, with only his wit, cunning and surprising skills with a Rubik's Cube to guide him. Does it count as showing off if you thoroughly impress people with a performance packed with talents that nobody has any business learning? If so, this nerd's nerd is quite the show-off. His show is on. Come see it!

Title: The Art of Concealment

Tucked away down a small passage off Raeburn Place, this treasure trove is one of Edinburgh's hidden gems. For our 32nd festival exhibition we present The Art of Concealment: a stunning selling exhibition celebrating the art of storage around the world. Ceremonial bronze and wood boxes from the Dogon of Mali  and dowry boxes from Kerala and the Swat Valley. Moroccan, Pakistani and Indian kum kum, khajul and spice boxes.
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 149

In 1941, Ellen waved goodbye to her fiance as he left for Crete, two weeks before the German invasion of the island. Tommy's past and Ellen's present collide one night in a cellar as they shelter from an air raid. As they begin to share their stories, two ends of a single thread begin to unravel, shaping a fateful connection and a shared, incredible destiny. Two strangers, two World Wars, one connection in hope.
Warnings: Some strong language. Themes related to war.

In the face of deceit and murder, morals and loyalty are put to the test. Minotaur Theatre Company’s historical drama warns you can’t trust anyone in a police state, even the ones you love.

Expect exciting arrangements of well-loved standards, some lesser-heard gems and even a bit of history from your fresh, young(ish) hosts Tenement Jazz Band.

Showcasing the finest in traditional circus thrills and skills, Cirque Berserk! celebrates the 250th anniversary of the invention of Circus by bringing this treasured form of live entertainment bang up-to-date in a jaw-dropping spectacular created especially for the theatre. Combining contemporary cirque-style artistry with adrenaline-fuelled stunt action, this astoundingly talented international troupe includes over thirty acrobats, aerialists, dancers, drummers and daredevil stuntmen. Title: Schütz: Resurrection History
Description: Heinrich Schütz, perhaps the most highly regarded composer in 17th century Germany, wrote The Resurrection History on returning to Germany in 1623, following a period of study in Venice with Giovanni Gabrieli. This beautiful work takes biblical scenes from the period immediately following the Crucifixion, and sets them to music of intensely measured austerity and flowing polyphony. The biblical narrative is sung by a tenor soloist accompanied by a consort of viols, and the other characters in the story sing music in solo, or duet form supported by a group of continuo instruments. Directed by Les Shankland.

Dorec-a-belle recently performed on BBC Radio 4's Loose Ends show with Clive Anderson and have supported artistes including Squeeze, The Staves and Magic Numbers. From delicate to danceable, their sound will make your feet tap, skin tingle and heart swell.

Throughout August you can relax & unwind whilst enjoying some of the world’s top names in pop, jazz, folk & rock music. In the heart of Edinburgh, The Merchants’ Hall is just off Princes Street & walking distance from Waverley Railway Station.

Title: Twisted
Description: Join Aaron Ayjay as he takes a comedic and very twisted musical journey through relationships from childhood, dating, marriage, divorce and other life experiences. Aaron’s energetic and aggressive musical comedy is peppered with expletives with very dark-humoured undertones. Be it about an ex-girlfriend, ex-wife or an over friendly pet who views a human leg as fair game, his songs start with a basic theme, escalating quickly into the ridiculous, leaving the audience wondering 'who the hell pulled the rug out from under his feet at certain times in his life'. Not for the faint-hearted.

Title: Meek
Description: In a society where private lives become political and freedom of expression is not an option, Irene finds herself imprisoned. As tales of her incarceration spread overseas and her growing exposure becomes a threat, she is forced to make a brutal decision. Penelope Skinner’s (Linda, The Village Bike) new play is a haunting vision of ruthless state control, tense friendships and one woman’s determination not to be broken. Presented by the exhilarating Headlong (People, Places & Things, This House) and directed by Amy Hodge, Meek is a tale which reflects on our own fraught times.

Behind the historic buildings, find the surprising number of gardens and green nooks and crannies, all with a story to tell. You'll hear about grand gardens of the past, enjoy productive community gardens created by today's residents and take a breather in a beautiful space laid out and planted as a 17th-century Scots town garden. Lasts one hour and 45 minutes, covers up to one mile of mainly pavement walking, some slopes and cobbled surfaces. Finishes at bottom of Canongate.

Based on a series of interviews with leading experts in and on the NHS, and residencies in hospitals and surgeries, and with director Nicolas Kent, Mark uses his own demise to explore the state we’re in. What's going wrong in our NHS, how it can go right and what the future might hold for all of us.

Kia is about to find out just how big hers is. She needs help. She’s fed up with the world. She’s growing up too fast, but who can help? From One Heart to Another looks at the exciting adventures a child goes on and the lessons we remember from our childhood when we’re really challenged to question how we see life.

Soon it will see big design changes: a design dubbed The Hobbit House has won a competition to create a new outdoor concert arena to replace the Ross Bandstand, along with improved access to the Gardens and Castle Rock. He’s a hippy, a punk, a poet, a drunk, a die-hard romantic and an eternal optimist, telling it like it is. This show of simple songs that tackle big issues will make you laugh, but also make you think with no-holds-barred honesty and quick wit.

It follows the sex lives of two women of different ages, embarking on very different experiences, as the same societal ideals influence their decisions. Compelled by the recent shedding of light on sexual abuse in the media and the cancellation of compulsory consent workshops at universities, Bristol-based company Bullet Theatre boldly and unashamedly explore the experience of being female, combining unique choreography with Anna Jordan's poetic writing. This amateur production is brought to you by arrangement with Nick Hern books.

Title: Tacita Dean
Description: This exhibition by acclaimed British artist Tacita Dean takes performance as its theme. From the early Foley Artist (1996) – a celebration of the unseen sound artists of film that scripts an imaginary film entirely through the efforts of two foley artists – to the bewilderingly intricate Event for a Stage (2015), in which actor Stephen Dillane delivers (in four conjoined performances) scripts given to him, page by page, by the artist, the exhibition examines performance and its relationship to narrative, the imagination and the collective effort of artist and audience in film, theatre, drawing and photogravure.

Title: America's Diversity in Song
Description: America’s Diversity in Song. Peter Allen, baritone. Paul Machlin, piano. Broadway, jazz, folk song, classical. This appealing mix of American 20th-century song, sung by Peter Allen, whose 'rich, rounded baritone' is supported by Paul Machlin’s 'subtle coloration' (Portland Press Herald), reflects America’s broad diversity of heritages and cultures as represented by its composers. The featured works – by Copland, Kern, Ellington, Ives, Weill and Burleigh – demonstrate how this diversity enriches and strengthens America’s music. These songs will beguile listeners of every background!

Description: Ahir Shah returns to Edinburgh with a new hour of stand-up about life and what comes after, death and what comes before, and Bohemian Rhapsody. Shah's last show, Control, enjoyed a critically acclaimed Fringe run, culminating in a nomination for Best Show at the 2017 Edinburgh Comedy Awards. This was followed by a UK tour, including three weeks at London's Soho Theatre. 'One of his generation’s most eloquent comic voices' **** (Telegraph). 'A scope and wit about him that is exciting to behold' **** (Times). 'Ratchets up the dismay to thermonuclear levels' **** (Guardian). **** (Sunday Times).
Artist: Soho Theatre in association with Avalon

And come to discover the story of a great Scot, the 'Godfather of Pop Art', Eduardo Paolozzi. The tour will explore more about Paolozzi and how he came to be our muse. Of course, there’s plenty of beer talk too. Our brewers will walk you through our lager-making process from blank canvas to final masterpiece. You’ll even get the chance to taste the raw ingredients and the unfiltered brew! There will also be an open question policy.
Venue description:
The Edinburgh Beer Factory is a family run, independent brewery founded in 2015 to make people think again about beer and Scotland.
Like our home city, we’re creative, inventive and outward-looking. We combine old and new ideas and techniques to create beers of beauty. It comprises of a brewery, bottle shop and Taproom - with views into the brewery and decorated with original Paolozzi artwork.

'One of the funniest and most original performers around.' (Independent). 'Fresh, funny and imaginative.' (Guardian). 'As dry as a critic’s mouth in the morning' (List).

'Full of sarcastic wit' (Time Out, Los Angeles). 'Salty-sweet, savagely honest, brutally funny' (TheSceneMagazine.com). Twangs – Malcolm Creese. Bangs – Cormac Byrne. This explosive band combines diabolical fiddle virtuosity from international star Adam Summerhayes; outrageous brilliance from world number one recorder genius, Piers Adams; horrifying high-ABV insanity from accordion master, Murray Grainger; positively feverish power from bass legend, Malcolm Creese; and dazzling bodhran playing from the king of folk percussion, Cormac Byrne.

Title: Alastair Savage and Gregor Blamey, Scotland and Beyond
Description: Alastair Savage is one of Scotland's most versatile fiddle performers. A prizewinner on traditional Scots fiddle, he has played throughout the world as a member of the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra and other leading instrumental ensembles.This exciting collaboration with pianist and accordion player Gregor Blamey of the Scottish Tango Ensemble focuses on 18th-century Scottish fiddle music by Niel Gow and Robert Mackintosh alongside melodies tracing the centuries old Scots immigration to Ireland and the American Appalachians. Alongside this, folk inspired sounds from mainland Europe including music by celebrated Hungarian composer Bela Bartok.

Description: We protested because we believe in a better country. We protested because we believe in gender equality for all. We continue to protest through performance because we believe these conversations are worth having. The March relives two friends’ journey to the Women’s March in London, while featuring the humorous and insightful experiences of other protesters and their different reasons for attending. Interspersed throughout are tales of fiercely feminist women from history, leading up to a final celebration of progress and a call for continued action. March with us!
Warnings: The March contains a scene about the experience of an illegal abortion - content is NOT graphic but may be triggering.

With male mental health being such a key issue in our culture and suicide being the biggest killer of men between 18 and 50, The Spider Glass entertains whilst inviting audiences to put a spotlight on the messages which dictate the unhealthy state of masculinity in the world, and how these stories have dramatically impacted the way we live.

Join us on this 90-minute magical mystery walking tour as we take a step back in time to Victorian Edinburgh and discover the hidden history and forgotten places where the Holmes legend really began – places unseen by most visitors and fans. Hear the incredible true story of how the world's most famous fictional detective was based on a real man who lived in Edinburgh just over 100 years ago as we follow in Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's footsteps. The game, quite literally, is afoot!

Simon Ward explores a language of ceramics that is influenced by traditional Chinese blue and white techniques. Porcelain birds are the vehicle for his expression; swarms and murmurations of individually cast birds are composed on wall based panels. Ward has received numerous awards in Japan, Korea and China. www.simonward-ceramicstudio.uk

Aunty Jee's twin from another mother twice removed is Mystic Jee – the ditsy medium who is really an extra large. Lubna's comedy style has been described as gentle, observational and perfect for Radio 4!

She’ll be drawing influence from her traditional roots as well as displaying her passion for cutting-edge contemporary music from countries such as Canada, Holland, Israel and of course, China. You will never hear the harp played like this – Sophie Rocks promises to open your ears and minds to some of the best music from around the globe!

After a decade of keeping her membership card firmly at the back of her wallet she’s fallen head over heels in love with Jeremy Corbyn and his raw communist sex appeal. Reluctantly whisked away to the bowels of Hell, everything that Bella believes in is called into question. Can she save the souls she deems worthy? Or will Lucifer drag her down to join him... Inferno is a dark comedy loosely based on Dante’s epic, exploring just what makes us so moral.
Warnings: Themes of sexual violence and suicide
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. More info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
Description: ‘I simply cannot wait to see more of their magic’ ***** (Tribe). ***** (Saint). ***** (OwlEyesMagazine.com). Look, okay. You’ve got a load of fairies, magic galore and there’s a dude that gets turned in to a donkey. So really, I feel like you need to, like, actively try to not have a good time with A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Fresh out of their international tour, join BoxedIn Theatre on an exciting romp through Shakespeare’s most magical comedy, complete with original music, silly hats and the best tent in Edinburgh.
Venue description: Another high calibre venue. A classy alternative to the Fringe norm, boasting the most comfortable seats in town! Wonderfully located in our 8 theatre central performance hub adjacent to theSpaceTriplex and theSpace @ Surgeons Hall.  A programme of music, a-capella, theatre and comedy and our very own bar & Theatre tent in the tranquil garden adjacent makes this a must for all. For more information / Show info: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Staff available to assist, full access via modern lift facilities. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. cobbled pavement

Title: The Lion and the Mouse
Description: A fun, interactive and educational classical concert for babies and toddlers where wriggling is allowed!
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Accessible entry is on the left from main doors. If not taking the ramp there are a few steps from the pavement to the main door

Title: Nancy Crook Organ Recital
Description: Experienced organ virtuoso, Nancy Crook, plays a varied programme of familiar and less well known organ masterpieces, including: Fantasia and Fugue in G minor BWV 542 by J S Bach; Recit de Tierce en Taille by Nicolas de Grigny; Piece Heroique in B minor by C Franck; Chorale Fantasias on When I survey and Old 100th by C H Parry; selection from 24 Pieces in Free Style Op 31 Book 2 by L Vierne; and Prelude for a Solemn Occasion, The Sweet Rivulet from the Hovingham Sketches and Fanfare by F Jackson.
Venue description: Modelled on Saint-Sulpice in Paris, this splendid church dates from 1875 and is in the heart of the West End. A magnificent yet intimate internal space is ideal for music concerts, featuring a fine Wells-Kennedy organ built in 1992.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Don't Be Terrible
Description: Can stand-up save your love life? Self-confessed nice guy Steve thinks so. That’s why he’s asked Alice, an up-and-coming stand-up, how to make people laugh. It’s his last-ditch attempt to distract his girlfriend from the funny guy at work. Unfortunately, misanthrope Alice believes in comedy much more than she believes in love and may not be quite the guru he was expecting. A comedy about comedy, that asks whether nice is ever funny, and whether sexy is ever nice.
Artist: Ellen Waddell and Oliver Milburn / Free Fringe
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.

Title: Ben Dali: Trance of a Lifetime
Description: Last chance to catch Edinburgh's premier hypnotist, including greatest hits plus new sketches. Expect random and unforgettable moments in Dali's most adult and groundbreaking extravaganza. The audience stars and anything goes. From simulated nudity, exploding sex-crazed aliens, world's first 5D cinema experience and hilarious scenes set at the heart of the Fringe, Trance of a Lifetime is an Edinburgh-centric blast providing all the laughs and excitement you hope for. Ben Dali has thrilled thousands at Edinburgh since 2014, and this is your final opportunity to experience his mastery of hypnosis in its natural environment.
Warnings: Hypnosis all performed by experienced, licensed and insured practitioner and is performed in accordance to the 1952 Stage Hypnosis Act. Unsuitable volunteers will be instructed not to participate. The unpredictable nature of the show means there is a potential for nudity that will not be encouraged by the hypnotist.
Venue description: Part of The Liquid Room and offering 2 fantastic separate I stage rooms and beer garden music bar. The venue can be accessed from 9 Victoria Street. The Annexe & Warehouse Rooms will feature a wide and varied selection of PBH FREE FRINGE comedy, cabaret and music acts everyday during August from 11am - 1am. Under 18's, accompanied by a responsible adult, can attend suitable shows until 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Ramp access to courtyard bar via Victoria street entrance. There is a flight of stairs down to the main performance space and a further flight of stairs to the annex.

Title: Pottervision
Description: The Potter parody show that celebrates and highlights the absurdities of those magical movies. Join us, four full-grown men pretending to be 12-year-old children, as we re-enact, recreate and celebrate the Philosopher's Stone. Suitable for the most casual potter fan but engaging enough for the most avid squib. (Sell-out 2016 and 2017 show!)
Venue description: One of Edinburgh's flagship free venues, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, there are free shows all day, and a free nightclub until 5am across our 5 floors of rooms and bars. Come an explore!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: Def Comedy Space Jam
Description: Tom Lawrinson and Josh Jones present an hour of stand-up comedy direct from outer space! Jokes that are absolutely raw and positively looney. In terms of free shows, this one is a guaranteed slam dunk! 'If you only see one comedian this month, make it Tom Lawrinson' (Skinny). 'Josh Jones has a very engaging personality, and a back-story that should keep him in routines for years to come' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items. Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are two steps up into the venue from the street. Once inside there is steps up/down into the toilet

Title: Comedy Freak Show
Description: Come one, come all to this tragic affair! Comedy Freak Show is an exhibition of comedic rarities. Typical features would be socially unusual humans, such as those uncommonly eery or unrelatable, those with both male and female secondary sexual characteristics, people with other extraordinary perspectives or paranoias, and performances that are expected to be toe-curling to the viewers. A rotating bill of five different comedians awaits you, so step right up to be blown away by those who dare call themselves 'freak'!
Venue description: The candle in the middle of two burning ends. A patchwork quilt of fair-trade coffees, 241 pizzas & magazines will get you through the day. It all begins to unravel again with a night-time tapestry of cocktails, craft beers and fine tunes - and a huge variety of free Fringe shows
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Alan Ayckbourn's Farcicals
Description: Highly acclaimed but rarely performed hilarious Ayckbourn double bill. Chloë With Love: does Teddy still love Lottie? Does Lottie still love him? Cue Penny and Reggie to the rescue. Penny weighs in to help Lottie, and Reggie resolves to help his friend resist temptation when the voluptuous Chloë puts all their plans to the test. Kidderminster Affair: sexual intrigue at Teddy’s barbecue. Will his secret liaison with neighbour Penny leak out? Will his wife Lottie discover the truth about Kidderminster? Will Penny’s husband and best friend Reggie ever resolve the mystery of the slow puncture?
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Great stylish on site bars too. For more info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Not So Secret Society
Description: From the team behind the hugely successful Bongo Club Cabaret and the UK's premier free variety night franchise, comes this epic family-friendly variety show, a generation in the making. Featuring A-list comedy and cabaret acts from across the Fringe that appeal to children and adults of all ages and persuasions. Each show will give you an unforgettable range of world-class performers and a showcase of why this is the world's greatest arts festival. Featuring magic, comedy, music and all manner of oddities, people will come back time and time again.
Warnings: While this is a family friendly cabaret show and acts without nudity or potentially offensive performances, this is still live cabaret and it can't be guaranteed that there won't be occasional swear words or mildly adult themes being discussed.
Artist: Jaggy Events / Ben Dali / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Having undergone a £1Million refurbishment Bourbon celebrates a unique bar/restaurant and nightclub space. The multi-purpose venue, open 7 days & nights a week during the Edinburgh Fringe, hosting a variety of PBH Free Fringe shows everyday.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Approx. 15 steps into the main bar. Once inside performance spaces are fully accessible

Title: Andrew Sim: You Gotta Find Joy
Description: Bringing his first solo show to the Fringe with a combination of storytelling, songs and surreal improvisations, Andrew Sim intends to liberate you from overthinking and explore the elusive subject of joy. Every day will have one of Andrew's comedy friends as an opening act before his 45 minutes of pure energy and stupidity. ‘Relentlessly self-aware... cause of genuine hilarity!’ (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘The sheer energy and pure boldness of this performer ensures the enjoyment of the audience’ (Student Newspaper).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.

Title: Paul Savage: DoGooder
Description: It's hard to do good when everything's falling apart. Paul Savage had a weird year, that really made him look inside himself. That's never a good thing. Contains great new jokes about depression, identity politics and jewel heists. 'Brave enough to be offensive, with a number of insane anecdotes. Shades of brilliance lurk here' (ThreeWeeks). Top 10 Jokes of the Fringe 2017 (Guardian, Mirror, Esquire, Shortlist, Week). 'An engaging and affable labour of love from a man determined to find comedy in the unlikeliest of places' (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Genuinely brilliant. An all round hoot' (Guardian).
Venue description: This family-run Italian restaurant on South Bridge hosts PBH Free Fringe comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am. No age restrictions before 10pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the building then performance space is down a flight of space.

Title: Peter Brush: Chasing Snails
Description: Awkward jokesmith Peter Brush takes on today’s hot topics, the Bayeux Tapestry, socks, the reason why snails move so slowly, and whether you’ll think more favourably of this show after he’s dead. ‘Compellingly hilarious... first-class gag writing... an original and achingly funny voice’ ****½ (Chortle.co.uk). 'An hour of killer gags with no let-up in quality' (Fest). www.facebook.com/peterbrushcomedy. www.peterbrush.net. www.peterbrush.podbean.com.
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Edinburgh Gin Safari
Description: Get off the tourist drag and on the gin trail! See the New Town through gin-tinted spectacles with gin cocktails, G and T marshmallows, chocolates and gin-cured salmon on this fab walking homage to gin – and you’ll discover that of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world, Edinburgh is the best. www.edinburghfoodsafari.com/about/
Warnings: Walking on sometimes uneven surfaces, stairs and there is alcohol included on tour- soft drinks can be provided
Venue description: Meeting Point

Title: The Piece
Description: The Piece is an immersive, glow-in-the-dark experience that spoofs immersive, glow-in-the-dark experiences. It's about a performer trying to put on the show of his life except something keeps getting in the way (honestly, it's probably you). Take a glowstick. Breathe. Experience The Piece. 'A terrifying, joyous funhouse ride!' (Peter Michael Marino, Show Up). 'You will be laughing with your whole freaked-out body' (Kevin Laibson, former AD at Peoples Improv Theater in New York City). 'The Piece is changing the game' (Ed Larson, Comedy Central).
Warnings: The show takes place largely in the dark in a small, attic-like space. It’s a very intense show with direct verbal interaction and, potentially, physical interaction with the performer. That said, the audience has moment-to-moment autonomy indicating (through the use of different glowsticks) whether they would like to interact with the performer.
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Evren
Description: In 2026, five explorers aboard the Evren are sent out to discover what lies within a black hole. Seventy years of secrecy later, the NARSA Space Agency will now release the findings of the Evren mission to the public. Through physical theatre, Evren displays the tensions that arise in extreme conditions of deprivation, isolation and the way relationships deteriorate. As seen in the logs recorded by the crew, audiences will witness the ephemeral movement of time and space and the lengths at which these explorers will go to discover what it takes to conquer frontiers, instead of each other.
Artist: So, That Was Fun! Theatre / YUFFA Fringe
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The pedestrian route available from the Royal Mile is wheelchair accessible

Title: Now That's Who I Call Archie Henderson
Description: On 12th November 2013, Archie Henderson accidentally reached #98 in the UK Singles Chart. It’s 2018, and this time he’s heading straight for number one. 'Immense talent' ***** (EdFestMag.com). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Radiated a delightfully daft energy' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: This popular bar hosts great PBH Free Fringe comedy in the arch cave every day during the Fringe. Between shows you can watch live big screen sports or simply enjoy the bar banter with beers from £2.80 per pint. Over 18's only.

Title: Alex Love: Stop the Press, I Want to Get Off
Description: Find out what life is really like as a local newspaper reporter in a rural town, covering hard-hitting stories such as parish council meetings, charity bike rides and dogs winning raffles. In less than a year, Alex Love was burnt out in hospital with a broken ankle and vowed to escape. This is Love’s follow-up to How To Win A Pub Quiz, sold out for 2016 and 2017. ‘A confident and relaxed performer who makes his audience feel at ease’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Alex Love is great fun’ (Copstick, the Scotsman).
Venue description: Situated at the foot of the Royal Mile, this traditional bar offers a wide selection of PBH Free Fringe shows daily. Kilderkin also boasts one of Edinburgh's finest selections of rums with over 100 to choose from. Our handmade, stone-baked pizzas are available until 2am. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Single step into the venue

Title: Amazing Bangkok Thai Street Food Cookery Workshop
Description: Amazing Bangkok street food by executive Thai chef Rujira Herd (Ru). You can eat superior Thai food and you can buy all Thai ingredients in Edinburgh or other parts of UK. Ru will reveal her best-kept trade secrets through a 100% hands-on lesson, creating three delicious traditional dishes. Something different to celebrate the Fringe. Exclusive to the Edinburgh Fringe. The school is 2.7 miles from city. Twenty minutes by bus (numbers 7,37,47,67), straight to the door. Please advice about special diets at least three days in advance. Lunch included.
Warnings: There are 4-5 steps access to the School.
Venue description:
Krua Thai is located 2.7 miles from Edinburgh Castle

Description: Saltire Sky's hit debut show is back. Follow these fearless young Scots in their quest to see their heroes lift the Scottish cup. Laughter, tears and bevy are guaranteed in this electric piece of new writing. Saltire Sky provide an access-all-areas approach to working class life, growing up Scottish and mad about football. This tale of pride, woe, defeat and victory reaches out to anyone who has dared to dream. Football is only the beginning. Football fans and theatre-goers alike, come along and be entertained by an impressive young theatre company whose voice will be heard.
Venue description:
The Wee Red Bar is a much loved Edinburgh institution, in terms of a lively and intimate venue.
Operating since the early 1980s and located in the grounds of Edinburgh College of Art via a secret, concealed entrance on Lady Lawson Street.

The venue prides itself in its excellent sound quality and puts on many, live gigs ranging from Reggae to Post-Rock, and every other genre in-between.

Title: Strauss: Four Last Songs and Schumann: Frauenliebe
Description: Susan McNaught (soprano), Taylor Wilson (mezzo) and Robert Melling (pianist) present a recital of beautiful German lieder including the Four Last Songs by Richard Strauss and Frauenliebe und Leben by Robert Schumann. 'Susan McNaught’s Ida is a vocal tour de force' (Kenneth Walton, Scotsman). 'Taylor Wilson – something really magical happens when a piece of music finds a performer whose talent matches it to perfection' (Alan Cooper, Herald). Title: Dan Kelly's Madras Years
Description: Ever tried to order a curry with all ten members of the Wu Tang Clan? Ever thought about what it all means (love/life/lager) mid downward-dog? Ever scored the winning goal in the last minute, only to have it chalked off for emotional reasons? Join Dan Kelly as he piles into the Madras Years, a medium-spicy character comedy show designed to open more cans of worms than it keeps closed. 'A particular treat' **** (Scotsman).

Title: Snowflake It 'Til You Make It
Description: Matt Duwell is a snowflake, and he is owning that label (despite thinking labels are pejorative). A show for anyone who has ever been called a snowflake, a libtard or a remoaner. Expect jokes about lighthearted subjects such as the polarisation of political discourse and the rise of nationalism as well as more serious subjects like Netflix and Angel Delight. 'Razor sharp ability... the boy's got talent' **** (MumbleComedy.net).
Venue description: As a brand new cocktail and coffee experience Harry’s Southside is the perfect place to spend a morning, afternoon or evening. A stylish and intimate bar (formally known as the Meadow Bar & Southside Social) Harry's is Edinburgh's first social enterprise bar.  So come in, pull up a chair and give back to your community and others across the globe while enjoying great free Fringe shows.

Title: The Really Terrible Orchestra
Description: The RTO has searched far and wide for music to play. European masters and music from the great plains of the USA will challenge orchestra and audience alike. Come and appreciate the excitement of the brass, the finger speed of the strings and the melodious sounds of the woodwind. You will be amazed at our courage and hard work in having the temerity to pull this one off. Join our usual sell-out audience and be prepared.

Title: Grimm Tales
Description: Carol Ann Duffy's lyrical and heartwarming adaptations of classic tales brought magically to life by a vibrantly talented young all-female cast. Tales both familiar and strange are wound together with music and dance, pathos and pandemonium. Theatre for the young at heart and the old of soul. This exciting and ambitious young company have visited the Fringe many times before to considerable acclaim. Title: A-Z of the Man With No Name
Description: A crazy alphabetical journey through the life of a modern vaudevillian loon. This man is bananas. With ukulele serenades, haiku jokes, environmentally conscious, zany short films, the man with no name will make you laugh, cry and ponder your very existence and sanity. A bananarama of lunacy, with free bananas for all! That's worth the entry alone, come on!

Title: #Hypocrisy
Description: Lost in blissful foreign travel, Imogen joyfully succumbs to the spoils of Western privilege. Returning to Scotland, a harsh society confronts her. Dangerous politicians prevail, the media sells fictions masquerading as reality, an ocean of social media sympathy pours forth for Western terror victims, yet backs turn on the migrant crisis. What staggering hypocrisy. A seamless blend of sharp spoken word poetry, dark comedy and original music, #Hypocrisy reminds us that in complacency lies the most heart-stopping terror. Be disconcerted, be cautioned. The premiere of this blistering performance will leave you questioning: why me and not them?
Venue description: Scottish Poetry Library is the nation's iconic home of poetry. Our live literature events take place in our mezzanine with a balcony for those balmy Scottish summer nights.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access from main door, venue is located on a cobbled lane

Title: Eat Sleep Shit Shag
Description: Amused Moose Comedy Award finalist, 2015, Abbie Murphy returns to the Fringe with her new show, Eat Sleep Shit Shag. Murphy has been trying to figure out what it is to be a woman. Anecdotes from the ex showgirl and her journey from corduroys and football shirts, to feathers tits and teeth. 'Murphy is sensational' ***** (EdFringeReview.com). 'Laugh aloud funny' *** (Steve Bennett, Chortle.co.uk).

With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.

Title: Scottish Folk Singer
Description: A special performance of historic and contemporary Scottish folk songs in the atmospheric Captain's Bar.

Title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
Description: Sweeney Todd returns to London having been unjustly exiled by the evil Judge Turpin. Now hailing as the Demon Barber, Sweeney swears vengeance against the Judge. Coaxed by the whispered words of the ensemble, Todd forms a sinister partnership with Mrs Lovett. Todd's thirst for blood inspires the addition of a secret ingredient into Lovett’s meat pies that has the people of London lining up for more. Inspired by Dante’s Inferno, Ethereal Theatre returns to the fringe with an iconic musical where Todd’s bloodthirsty world will come alive in a late-night spectacle.
Warnings: Contains scenes of murder/horror and references to psychiatric disorders.
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue, In another unrivaled location we present the ultimate powerhouse of live performance. Part of our 8 space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter. A pulsating programme of cross genre performance art, the festival's largest programme of new writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information . Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Daniel Downie: 2 O'Clock Gun
Description: Daniel Downie takes an irreverent look at Edinburgh’s history that’s more hysterical than historical. Why do they fire a massive cannon every day at lunchtime? Is there really a strip club named after a pair of brutal murderers? Why did they mark the spot where people were burned alive with a well? Is all of Scotland as middle class as this? The 2 O'Clock Gun is everything you needed to know about Edinburgh and everything you didn’t want to know about Daniel! 'Up-to-the-minute material that had the audience in stitches' (MumbleComedy.net).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving great food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Our two dedicated 50-seat performance spaces, presenting some of the best home-grown comedy at the Festival, are on the first and second floors.

Title: The Quest: A Fantasy Musical
Description: Questing Voles – All’s Well That Ends As You Like It, 2017: ‘a pretty anarchic hour of fun and frolics’ (FringeReview.co.uk); Piracy!, 2013: ‘recommended show’ (FringeReview.co.uk) – return with a new musical comedy set in the fantasy world of Elvenheart. Kick back as the Troll’s Trousers Tavern band whisk you off on an adventure with a ragtag fellowship, including an underachieving wizard, incompetent Elvish warriors and a ranger with a dark and silly secret. Will unlikely romance blossom? Why is the Orb so glow-y? And do any of our heroes actually know what they’re doing?
Venue description: The original Fringe venue, its unique atmosphere is known in Fringe folklore. it's worth a visit just for that! Here we present new and established work from across the globe. From mid to large scale theatre, dance, musicals, opera and music makes a daily programme of quality to enjoy. Don't miss our partner venue (V267) at the church upstairs offering a fabulous classical programme. Show info. www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Crizards Cromedy Show
Description: Crizards come to Edinburgh with some spicy cromedy concerning bronze, weevils and utility bills. Will and Eddy (the Crizard boys) are an offbeat double act specialising in bulletproof patter and groovy audiovisual happenings. Crizards were third place champions of the Leicester Square Theatre Sketch Off 2017, and are the stars and administrators of the monthly Crizards Cromedy Crub. ‘Very clever, very wry, very well performed’ (Bruce Dessau, BeyondTheJoke.co.uk).
Venue description: The iconic world famous Waverley bar has recently reopened having undergone refurbishment throughout with both the main bar and upstairs lounge restored to full glory. A must visit bar for old and new customers alike during this years fringe and beyond. A well stocked spirits gantry and selection of traditional beers and wines are available on tap, as well as light bar snacks. During this years fringe we are hosting PBH Free Fringe shows in our upstairs lounge every day.

Title: EdinBra Fringe Comedy
Description: The debut season of a revolving line-up of the best established and up-and-coming female comedians from around the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. An early evening show for all comedy fans. This show is also supporting the Against Breast Cancer charity. For full details go to overthelyne.com.
Venue description: One of Edinburgh's flagship free venues, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, there are free shows all day, and a free nightclub until 5am across our 5 floors of rooms and bars. Come an explore!

Title: Action Figure Archive With Steve McLean
Description: Steve opens his old toy box and rediscovers your faves from He-Man, Transformers, Star Wars and many more (about three more). Remember when toys were better? Your memory might be playing tricks on you. Who was the worst Decepticon? Why didn't they make a Star Wars Tarkin figure but they made one of the blue elephant trumpet player? Geeks and nerds unite in this fun show that critics are calling a good show to go to while you're waiting for another show to start. Not a children's show (but bring them if you want).
Venue description: This NEW colourful Grassmarket bar and basement lounge has the trapping of the Pacific, with a selection of freshly prepared foods, drinks, cocktails and family friendly entertainment to suit all. During the Edinburgh Fringe we host PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement lounge.

Title: A Librarian
Description: A naive librarian witnesses an incident that will change the rest of her life. ‘A rich and nuanced performance at the heart of this gripping play.’ (Paul Fowler: Guild of Drama Adjudicators chair). One week only. Experience the life of lonely spinster – Anne Poole – and re-live the ‘incident’ as she takes you on a journey, acting out episodes as she remembers them with the characters in her head coming to life before your eyes. An intense thriller, with an unexpected disclosure. #alibrarian
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. More info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Fan Girl
Description: Geraldine is a lonely young secretary living with her invalid and overbearing mother. Her only respite is a hit American television show loosely based on the life of Zenobia, a third-century Syrian Queen. Using her life savings, Geraldine attends the first International Zenobia fan event. We cheer her on through the highs, the lows, the embarrassments and her small triumphs during her weekend adventures and we learn the secret behind her obsession with Zenobia. This one-woman comic drama by Eddie Coleman, and starring the wonderfully talented Karen Whyte, follows a sell-out run at the 2017 Camden Fringe Festival.
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Great stylish on site bars too. For more info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com

Title: A Diamond Diva
Description: Miss DQ, the Diamond Diva, also happens to be the only dwarf drag act in Europe. Fresh from a three year residency at Sparkles Show Bar in Gran Canaria, the star of Channel 4's Seven Dwarves is ready to knock the Fringe for six. Big time! Randy Newman sang ‘short people got no reason to live’... well eat your words Randy, because this short person has a great reason to live. She’s got talent oozing out of every corset and don’t you know: diamond divas are forever. So come on down, you Johnnies, it’s showtime! Pow!
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue
Venue description: Venue 429 The Planet Bar is an all year round venue with entertainment most weeks and boasts cheap drinks and a friendly atmosphere.  On special nights your DJ hostess is Cilla Slack, along with her chums Scarlett Diamonte and Ginger Rodgers.  Come and be entertained.

Title: Men With Coconuts
Description: One of the UK's leading improv troupes, the award-winning Men With Coconuts are back! An hour of improvised comedy sketches and songs, culminating in a showstopping finale – an entirely improvised musical. Unplanned, unscripted, and unbelievable! Praise for Men With Coconuts: 'One of the best improv shows I've seen. Skilful and hysterical' (Jo Caulfield). Winner Spirit of the Fringe Award (Prague Fringe 2016). 'Hilarious... make sure these guys are on your list!' (pftc.cz). 'Absurdly ridiculous and downright hilarious' (TheWeeReview.com). 'Forget everything you thought you knew about improvisation... a must see show!' (EdFringeReview.com).
Artist: Men With Coconuts / PBH's Free Fringe

Under 18's, accompanied by a responsible adult, can attend suitable shows until 9pm.

Title: Ryan Ward and Joe Molander: Natural Born Performers

Title: Men With Coconuts: Improvised Bond
Description: One of the UK's leading improv troupes, the award-winning Men With Coconuts, return with their fully improvised Bond film! Expect villains, gadgets, femme fatales and sobering reflections on masculinity – all improvised live onstage! Praise for Men With Coconuts: 'One of the best improv shows I've seen. Skilful and hysterical' (Jo Caulfield). Winner: Spirit of the Fringe Award (Prague Fringe 2016). 'Hilarious... make sure these guys are on your list!' (pftc.cz). 'Absurdly ridiculous and downright hilarious' (TheWeeReview.com). 'Forget everything you thought you knew about improvisation... a must see show!' (EdFringeReview.com).

Title: Improv Cage Match
Description: Improv Cage Match pits two improv teams against each other, with the audience declaring the winner. Previous teams include Baby Wants Candy and The Free Association. Who will be declared the Fringe’s best improv team? You decide! Improv Cage Match gives you a taste of the best improv comedy the Fringe has to offer. Two teams will each have just 25 minutes to skillfully build a hilarious improv show right in front of your eyes that has never been seen before, and will never be seen again! This is an improv show you haven’t seen before.
Artist: Hat On Dog / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: The Bureau of Untold Stories
Description: In the minds of people just like you are tales of significant importance, waiting to be discovered. The inspired inspectors who uncover these fables are members of an elite unit known as The Bureau Of Untold Stories. And these are the stories you've shared. Unravel the hidden stories of the audience with our inspectors as they utilise live sound effects, improvisation and their unconventional storytelling skills to immerse you into the excitement of an old radio mystery. 'To entertain both children and parents with such brilliant improvisation is no mean feat.' (Audience review).
Venue description: Venue 444

Title: Harry De Cruz Gets His Act Together
Description: Everyone has a party trick. Harry has 374 and counting. Watch the multidisciplined master at work as he brings his hotly anticipated one-man show to the Fringe for the first time. 'The king of party tricks’ (Dynamo) shares his incredible skills, takes on challenges from the audience and pits his wits against the clock to change your perception of what one man is capable of. Performing the improbable and impossible, creating a show that can only be described as unbelievable. 'The real Harry Potter' (JK Rowling).
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with a cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy, ballroom and space 3 will be used during the festival by some of the best PBH Free Fringe performers on the cabaret and comedy circuit.

Title: Full Moon Cabaret
Description: The Full Moon Cabaret is an immersive art party with burlesque, variety and subversive surprises. Taking place on the full moon of every month in Berlin, the Full Moon Cabaret offers a cheeky exploration of a theme derived from what Native Americans called the full moon. After a year of inciting Berliners to misbehave, the Full Moon Cabaret is now off to subjugate the world to its eccentric erotica and deviant decadency. Join us for a knees-up celebrating the lunacy within us all.
Warnings: Occasional nudity and profane language.
Venue description: Situated on the bustling city centre street, at the foot of Edinburgh Castle sandwiched between the stylish West-end district and the ever popular Bruntsfield. Moriarty‘s is a place where you can relax in stylish yet homely surroundings. The carefully refurbished bar has a Sherlock Holmes theme upstairs with our focus on Craft Beers, World Lagers and Malt Whisky.

Title: The Rising – Springsteen Tribute

This dynamic seven-piece band perform with the energy and precision of the E Street Band. This show is not to be missed by fans of the Boss and of live music. Previous sell-out shows!
Venue description: Fringe venue 44

Title: Interruption Show
Description: The interactive show where Dalia Malek (CKP's Lunchtime Special, Chortle Student Comedy Award finalist, Second City Diversity in Comedy Festival, SF Sketchfest) and rotating co-hosts interrupt comedians mid-performance to ask burning questions, find out what happened next and dig into backstories of jokes. Dalia Malek started comedy in London and performed in major clubs, theatres and universities all over the country. She now lives back home in California, where she hosts Interruption Show at All Out Comedy Theatre. This will be Interruption Show's Edinburgh Fringe debut.
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, The Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11:00-02:00. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Title: Quiz in My Pants
Description: The festival's silliest panel show returns for its ninth year! With special guests every day – previous guests include Joe Lycett, Miles Jupp, Tom Green, Henning Wehn, Matt Richardson, Max and Ivan, and Noise Next Door. Features the world's longest quickfire round! 'A clever experiment which pays off... definitely funnier than any quiz show you’ll see from your sofa' (ThreeWeeks). **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Title: Arturo Tappin
Description: Internationally renowned jazz saxophonist, Arturo Tappin, ushers in carnival fever to Edinburgh once again, taking you on a rousing musical trip around the Caribbean Islands. Arturo’s esteemed career includes having performed with Roberta Flack, Luther Vandross, Eddy Grant and Maxi Priest to name a few. Arturo performs the world over, but he can most readily be seen selling out festivals in his native Barbados. As Arturo says, 'your chairs are your enemies!', because it is hard to resist getting up to dance! Don’t miss Arturo, accompanied by his Barbadian trio, raise the roof in the Outhouse's intimate setting.
Venue description: Popular and city centre bar promoting local products as well as worldwide beers, wines and cocktails in a uniquely friendly environment. Close to The Playhouse, the Outhouse is situated down a lane off Broughton Street. We boast a beer garden, quality music, reasonable prices, showing local artists and excellent shows during the Fringe. It's a hidden gem the locals want to keep to themselves! 18+ only. Dog Friendly.

Title: Kids' Birthday Bash!
Description: Is it your kid's birthday? Well it is today! Sit in on a 40-minute birthday party for all the kids in the room! Kids get to play games, win prizes and they even get to blow out the candles on the birthday cake! Family fun guaranteed at this interactive children's show! All performed by professional children's entertainer and comedian, Christian Elderfield. 'Fantastic, intimate slap-dash comedy' ****1/2 (Advertiser, Adelaide 2017).
Venue description: The recently refurbished Pear Tree offers a huge selection of free shows during the day and bands indoors at night. Through the day there's also music on the outdoor courtyard stage, in a huge courtyard with outdoor bars and barbecue to enjoy your Fringe days and nights in. The venue is also linked to the Counting House which boasts four more theatres with more free shows all day and night.

Title: The Nasty Show
Description: Offensive is the new black. The Nasty Show is a guaranteed offensive comedy showcase featuring a selection of the best comics of the festival, delivering their filthiest material. Hosted by Jez Watts. 'Electric' ****1/2 (FourthWallMedia.wordpress.com, 2018). **** (PerthHappenings.co.au, 2018). 'Not for the faint-hearted' ****(TheMusic.co.au, 2018). **** (WinningAtFailing.com, 2018).  'A masterclass in smut' **** (TheAustraliaTimes.com). With a huge drinks selection, a wide bar menu, and a courtyard full of street-food tents and cocktail huts. Shows run from 10am to 2am, with music through until 5am.

Title: #1 Comedy Great Fun Best Show Jez Watts
Description: ****1/2 (PerthHappenings.com). **** (TheMusic.com.au). West Australian stand-up comedy veteran Jez Watts has a fresh hour of material, his online search criteria covered and a loop machine. Title: Friz Frizzle: Keyboard Warrior
Description: Friz Frizzle is a songruiner. He'll take the tunes you know and love and mess around with them until you don't want to know or love them any more. It's better than it sounds. Winner of the TenFootCity Hull Comedian of the Year, finalist of the Musical Comedy Awards 2017.

Title: A Gay and a NonGay Live! – Free
Description: Prepare for the gay and straight worlds to come together, as unlikely friends James Barr and Dan Hudson bring their hugely successful podcast to Edinburgh – live! James will explore the "admin" behind gay sex, while Dan promotes his campaign for metal music fans to be recognised as a minority. Plus questions from the audience and a good chinwag about LGBT issues in what Time Out call 'a warm, funny take on love, friendship and sex', and Radio Times called 'one of the most fundamentally kind and funny podcasts in Britain'.
Warnings: Strong language, adult themes

Title: Akiko Okamoto plays Mozart and Chopin Piano Concertos
Description: This talented, international Japanese-born pianist returns to the Fringe to perform Mozart’s piano concerto No 12 and Chopin’s Piano Concerto No 1. She will be accompanied by a local string quartet and will also perform an exciting programme of solo piano music.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music - and some book discussions,  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.

The performance area and green room are not wheelchair accessible.  A ramp leads from the street up to the front portico for general access to the building. Lift access to cafe and toilets

Title: The Greatest Play in the History of the World...
Description: A love story, set on Preston Road, and also in space and in time. A man wakes in the middle of the night to discover that the world has stopped. Through the crack in his bedroom curtains, he can see no signs of life at all... other than a light in the house opposite where a woman in an over-sized Bowie t-shirt stands, looking back at him. Starring Julie Hesmondhalgh (Coronation Street, Broadchurch), The Greatest Play... is squashed full of exquisite observation and heartbreaking beauty.
Warnings: Strictly no latecomers
Artist: Tara Finney Productions in association with Royal Exchange Theatre
Venue description:
The Traverse Theatre is Scotland's new writing theatre. From its conception in 1963, it has embraced a spirit of innovation and risk-taking that has launched the careers of many of Scotland's best-known writers. With two custom-built and versatile theatre spaces, the Traverse’s home in Edinburgh’s city centre is a powerhouse of vibrant new work.
'The Traverse is the festival's most prestigious home for serious drama' ([i]New York Times[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Two wheelchairs available to borrow at the Traverse. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: James Barr: Thirst Trap! – Free
Description: Dating in 2018 is a total disaster! MTV presenter, comedian and co-host of the UK's leading LGBTQ+ award-nominated podcast A Gay And A NonGay, and tragically single James Barr unleashes a hilarious attempt to finally meet The One – and it could be you! Join him on his wedding day as he dishes the dirt on his ridiculous romantic life, and dates the audience to find his way up the aisle. A super fun and funny 60-minute make-out session, where it's time to let the crazy out!
Warnings: Strong language, adult themes
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free Venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10am to 2.30am. There's an massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food & drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Organ Recitals in the City
Description: Enjoy our popular lunchtime recitals by the next generation of organists on the fine Wells-Kennedy instrument in the Georgian splendour of St Andrew’s and St George’s West Church, George Street. Title: Jem Brookes: Schizophonic
Description: Jem Brookes: Schizophonic is a fast-paced cacophony of characters and voices that come out of one man's head. Quick-fire skits, sounds, recurring characters and topical bits all interlaced together. Imagine your favourite late-night radio show – but live. Returning favourites including Celebrity? I'm an Alcoholic, Get Me Out a Beer! and Essex girl Stacey Doolally 'taking on the wewld' for BBC!!! This show will be unlike anything you have ever heard or seen before and you will wonder how it's possible for so many different characters, accents and voices to emanate from one man's mind and mouth.

Title: The Shakuhachi Experience
Description: In this world premiere at the 2018 Edinburgh Festival Fringe, licensed master shakuhachi performer Markus Guhe takes Japan's oldest and quintessential bamboo flute on a journey from its mythical beginnings through its long and fascinating history into the 21st century. The programme features the traditional shakuhachi solo repertoire created during the Edo era by mendicant Zen monks (mysterious masterless samurai working as government spies and the only ones permitted to play the instrument), happy folk tunes, taiko (Japanese big drums; Markus is also a senior performer with Mugenkyo Taiko Drummers) and live electronics.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces we present two spaces offering an array of new and established work, from theatre to musicals, dance, music and physical work, a real feast for all . Our fabulous courtyard bar adjacent to the venue is a must for all. Show info:www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Adventures in Dementia: Steve Day
Description: Steve's dad has Alzheimers. There's nothing he can do about it except remember the way he was. Steve has also been deaf since his teens but has new hearing aids so now he's gone through all the music of his youth. It reminds him of his dad. There's nothing else for it but to defy dementia, with music, songs and laughter. Laugh, cry, sing along if you want. If you like bittersweet comedy about deafness and memory loss then this is the show for you. Previous shows were rated ***** (Chortle.co.uk) and **** (Scotsman).

Title: Everything Wrong With You Is Beautiful
Description: Poet and raconteur Tina Sederholm has long been an adult, but still feels like a problem child. As her father is consumed by Alzheimer’s, Tina tries to uncover the facts behind a family story that never rang true. But as telling stories becomes her career, she discovers that 'what really happened' is not always simple to define. Inspired by Tina’s recently published book, Everything Wrong With You Is Beautiful is a funny and poignant meditation on the nature of memory, truth and lies. 'Completely spell-binding' ***** (EdFringeReview.com). 'Superbly realised story' **** (SabotageReviews.com).

In a Cornell University study women rated fictional female peer, Joan, as emotionally unstable and less competent because she was sexually promiscuous. If Joan wasn't fictional her name would be Harriet Kemsley and in this deeply personal show Harriet delves into her sexual history. Star of Bobby and Harriet Get Married, Comedy Central’s Roast Battle and Katherine Ryan Tour support. 'A quirky, refreshingly charming comedian at the dawn of her TV career' (Radio Times). 'Joyful’ **** (Scotsman). ‘Effervescent’ **** (EdFestMag.com).
Warnings: Sensitive content

A show cognisant of human patterns, taking ownership of my own hypocrisy and realising that we become who we judge. It’s only funny because it’s true. www.imranyusuf.com

Set sail on a surreal journey – sometimes poignant, always funny and ultimately uplifting. With biscuits. Of course. 'Terrific deadpan delivery of material… topical and relevant. Audiences loved it!' (Alexa Kelly, Pulse Ensemble Theatre). Razor-sharp wit laced with a touch of the surreal' **** (Fest). 'A character so defined and well realised that the room is instantly on board with his quite unique critique of modern life' **** (TheWeeReview.com).
