Title: Limmy’s Vines
Description: Limmy is perhaps best known for BBC Scotland’s Limmy’s Show, but when that came to an end, Limmy turned to Vine. With a lot of time on his hands, he spent most of 2013 on his phone, recording six second video after six second video. When Vine came to an end, Limmy had created over an hours' worth of nightmarish nonsense, improvised characters and the one with the spider crawling out his mouth. Join Limmy as he introduces a screening of the Vines, followed by an audience Q&A where you can ask him how, what and why.

How do we think others see us? And does it matter?!

Description: Comedy legend Tony Slattery reveals all in conversation with comedy-historian Robert Ross. After playing to packed houses last year, with a return to his greatest triumph Whose Line Is It Anyway?, Tony Slattery is back with a no-holds-barred reflection on his life and work. From the Cambridge Footlights to the demons that have consistently dogged his success. As you would expect of the king of improvisation, this is an unstructured and unpredictable gallop through several lifetimes’ worth of poignant and hilarious anecdotes. Anything can happen, and it probably will...

Title: Buddhist Meditation
Description: People attending the workshop will have the option of either meditating on chairs or on cushions on the floor. Some instruction on posture will be given. The main practice we teach involves focusing on the breath to help develop concentration and general awareness of body and mind. We will also make suggestions to encourage healthy emotions such as kindness and contentment. The participants should feel some immediate benefits in calmness, clarity and a more confident perspective and should also be able to practise the simple methods by themselves in the future.
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 349, The Healthy Life Centre is conveniently situated near Lothian Road and offers a diverse programme of therapies, classes and workshops, conducive to mental and physical well-being.

Title: Phantasmagorical
Description: The merrily macabre Sylvia Sceptre presents Phantasmagorical, a show of spooky mind reading and Victorian spirit theatre. This is as close as you will get to experiencing the thrills of the golden age of spiritualism. You will witness a supernatural spectacle of stories and magic, swirling with dark whimsy. Sylvia Sceptre is a character devised by Careena Fenton. She blends storytelling, drama and magic ensuring this powerful piece of theatre resonates in the minds of the audience long after the performance is over. 'Timeless, elegant and beautifully Victorian. Brilliant!' (Reece Shearsmith, writer of Inside No. 9).
Warnings: Themes of death and life beyond the grave.

Title: John Lynn: Addiction Diction
Description: John Lynn is not a drug fiend. He doesn’t have a (serious) gambling problem. He’s not even that fond of coffee. However, like all of us, John has many addictions in his life. Addiction is defined as a chronic, relapsing brain disease, considered so because drugs alter the brain. This is also true of music, dancing, a walk in the park, sex, sobriety, religion, meditation, booze, exercise, smoking, playing the victim, gossiping, social media, Netflix, making money, losing money. Perhaps happiness is becoming friends with your addictions? We all have vices but John likes his.

Description: Edinburgh's biggest comedy event returns. Always a complete sell-out so book early to avoid disappointment. 2018 marks the 11th year of partnership between Off The Kerb Productions Ltd and Waverley Care, Scotland’s biggest charity providing care and support to those living with HIV and Hepatitis C. All proceeds raised from the Edinburgh Comedy Gala go straight to supporting the life-changing work of the charity. Since its launch in 2003, the now annual event has raised almost £450,000 with this year’s event looking set to topple the £500,000 mark.

Title: Nàdar / Prakriti
Description:
Nàdar / Prakriti is the first solo UK exhibition by Indian artist Ravi Agarwal. Through new print commissions, Agarwal responds to current
conversations about rural and urban sustainability and the various challenges posed to nature in Scotland and India. His work examines community-led attempts to 're-wild' or 'take back' nature in rural and urban contexts. Agarwal has a diverse and interdisciplinary practice as an artist, environmental activist, writer and curator. He works primarily with photographs, video, installations and public art. This project is
supported by the British Council and Creative Scotland, with partnership support from the John Muir Trust.

Getting far more than he bargained for, he travels through the dark heart of Europe's past towards the present day. Four actors portray Adam Smith, David Hume, Jean Jacques Rousseau, Voltaire, Robert Burns and Margaret Smith. The Scottish Enlightenment and the impact of the French Revolution form the background to the emergence of Adam Smith's two great books, The Wealth of Nations and The Theory of Moral Sentiments.

Description: A new translation of the scandalous Austrian play from 1903 unveils intimate conversations between people before and after they have sex. A prostitute meets a soldier on the street, the soldier seduces a housemaid and so on, until in the final scene a noble Count meets with the prostitute and everything goes full circle. The characters and relationships are startlingly contemporary and socio-critical, and just as real as they were 100 years ago. Confrontational, physical and funny, this play dissects the relentless mechanics of desire, gender roles and power imbalances that still exist today.

Title: Sisterhood
Description: A fearless adventure into the dark heart of a paradigm shift... Three women, aged 20, 40 and 60 (but not a virgin, mother or hag in sight), set about unpicking the fine weave of existence, re-examining with fresh and furious eyes, threads such as gender, fertility, sexual assault and the state of feminism today. 'Their style is stiletto sharp, their diction perfect as they race through their complex rhymes' (Evening Standard). Winner – Best Musical Act (Leicester Comedy Festival 2018). Winner – Best Music and Variety Act (Chortle Awards 2018).
Warnings: This show contains swearing and adult themes

With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman). Open until 3am.

Title: Songlines
Description: ‘She’s scared of what I might get up to out here in the countryside. Keeps giving me lectures on barn-bonking. I’m going to die of boredom just to make her feel bad.’ Stevie is sent to Suffolk – the home of doggers, folklore and Stan. The course of teenage love never did run smooth. When Stevie bumps into Stan again, she has a chance to make things right. Title: Sparks
Description: 'Fall in love in my early 20s, get married in my late 20s, have at least one child by the time I'm 30. F*ck!' Life is hard to navigate when you've got so many questions. Can I put this jumper in the washing machine? Do you have my birth certificate? Where did you find love? How did you do it? How do you survive? A story of a kamikaze love affair with unexpected consequences. Hilarious and heartbreaking, written and performed by Jessica Butcher and Anoushka Lucas. Sparks is a two-hander musical about the brain's response to grief.

Title: No Kids
Description: No Kids explores the personal journey that real-life couple Nir and George embarked upon when they asked the question: as a gay couple, should we go out of our way to have children? Gender-bending musical cabaret and verbatim theatre marry to conceive a distinctly queer piece that asks: should we be making more babies in an increasingly overpopulated world? And is our society truly open to the idea of two dads? Title: Unspoken
Description: From the team who brought you the winner of the Amnesty International Freedom of Expression Award for the groundbreaking The Two Worlds of Charlie F, Bravo 22 Company's new drama, Unspoken, brings to light the lives interrupted and forever changed by war, on a heart-wrenching and hilarious journey of love, loss, loneliness and hope, performed by ex-Service personnel. Title: No One Is Coming to Save You
Description: Climate change, nuclear war, radicalism: we live in a culture of suspense. Humanity is moving so unstoppably towards the edge, that you might imagine we were enjoying the violence of our slow decline. This is a play about that impulse. No One is Coming to Save You takes place in the minds of two young people who can’t sleep. She is staring at a glass. He is watching TV in a foreign language. David Lynch meets Danny DeVito’s Matilda in this new play about being young during the slow cancellation of the future.
Warnings: Sensitive content: descriptions of violence, descriptions of suicide, swearing, and descriptions of mental illness.

To be a professional footballer, to play at the highest level, to represent his country and to usurp the crown of his school’s greatest hero: Leeds United and Scotland footballer Billy Bremner. The schoolboy was comedian Phil Differ and his dream came with a plan – to get into the school team, to impress with every game and to eclipse Bremner’s incredible career through his own spectacular achievements. Only one thing stands in Phil’s way – mediocrity. Discover the fruits of Phil’s failure in this autobiographical one-man show.

We all know the classic tale of two star-crossed lovers, but seriously weren’t there, like, a thousand ways it could have worked out for them? Maybe she follows him to Mantua. We invite you to read our minds, to listen to our secrets, to watch us dance, hear our songs and our spoken word. Together, let's laugh hysterically and share a serious case of the feels. In a forest where time moves as it wants, nine women, all accused of some form of defiance, come forward to tell their truths. From an 11th-century baker murdered by a mob, to a 21st-century award-winning actress who finally tells the truth and brings down an empire, their stories are about the fear of saying nothing and the courage to say 'no more'.

Chiaroscuro tells the story of both Winton’s remarkable and selfless act of heroism and the extraordinary journey of one particular group of children he saved.
Warnings: The play depicts traumatic events that were experienced by children in pre-World War II Czechoslovakia. No bad language, but some events depicted will suggest and/or describe violent events.
Venue description: Central Hall

Founded by women, for women, this all-girls school centered itself around four values: social justice, spirituality, community, and service. Today, the young women who walk the hallways of Mercy Academy are hell-bent on carrying on this tradition and their sights are set on tackling today’s toughest, messiest, and most ridiculous issues, those straight from today’s headlines. And, for the first time, they’re taking their story and stance directly to the stage. Join us.

Dionysos weaves his spell in the land of Thebes, seeking revenge on those who refuse to honor him. A cappella four-part harmony singing punctuates text in this living version of ancient myth, as the house of Pentheus falls. These interactions between humans, the god Dionysos, and the Bakkhai, with their connection to the Mother, bring up questions of humanity and our place in the spiritual realm.

Title: Dr Korczak's Example
Description: Dr Korczak was a Polish doctor and writer, who passionately championed every child’s right to freedom, respect and love. Dr Korczak’s Example is set in 1942 in the final days of an orphanage in the Jewish ghetto of Warsaw, where food is scarce, tempers rise and everyone wants to survive. Award-winning playwright David Greig tells this powerful tale of Korczak's refusal to abandon the young people in his care, and focuses on the human need for respect and hope, even in the face of injustice.

Title: Rembrandt: Britain's Discovery of the Master
Description: This exclusive new exhibition, which will only be shown in Edinburgh, reveals how the taste for Rembrandt’s work in Britain evolved over the past 400 years. From early beginnings around 1630, it grew into a mania that gripped collectors and art lovers across the country, reaching a fever pitch in the late 18th century. The exhibition also reveals the profound impact of Rembrandt’s art on the British imagination, by exploring the wide range of native artists whose work has been inspired by the Dutch master, over four centuries, right up to the present day.

Megan’s ‘Bloody Mary’ of a foof, is flowing free and she is imprisoned in the loo with a toilet attendant who charges £2.50 per tampon. Ever wondered what happens in the Ladies Loos? Join us round the U-bend!
Warnings: Contains strong language and adult humour.

Title: Contractions
Description: Staging of the famous play – Mike Bartlett's Contractions by St Petersburg A.A. Bryantsev Youth Theatre. This ink-black satire features a series of short interviews between the human resources manager of a multinational company and a young woman working in the sales division. Mike Bartlett, who was thrilled, by his own words, that Contractions was having its premiere production in Russia, said that the message he wanted to translate to the viewers is 'the importance of humanity versus faceless authority, and the necessity of frailty, emotion and above all, play.'
Artist: St.Petersburg State A.A. Bryantsev Youth Theatre, Russian Federation

The combination of the two voices in close harmony in songs, whether traditional or contemporary, interspersed with anecdotes and a touch of humour has received much praise from both audiences and organisers. A concert with The Quiggs is a chance to hear folk song in its simple yet highly expressive form, including beautiful harmonies and songs that seek the audience's participation.

Title: Festival Lights – The Songs of Nick Keir
Description: Nick Keir, the Edinburgh folksinger and songwriter, left us too early in 2013. However, he left a great legacy of his own lovely songs. At tonight's concert some of his folk friends will gather in his memory to sing Nick's songs – including Dick Gaughan, Sangsters and The Quiggs. The whole night is being produced by Nick's best mate, Alastair. All the proceeds from what promises to be a terrific show will be donated to Cancer Research.

Title: Charlie Caper – Artifice Intelligence
Description: Advanced technology indistinguishable from magic! Robots of varying complexity, from AI research platforms to homemade junkbots, interact with international magician Charlie Caper in experimental high-tech wizardry. 'Wubalubadubdub" (Roy Batty). Charlie Caper has performed in 50 countries using seven languages. He is the winner of Sweden's Got Talent, has received the Mandrake's D'Or (the Oscar of magic) and a very small share of an Olivier Award (as part of La Soirée). His last show Minor Miracles, with Malin Nilsson, won the Adelaide Fringe Best Magic Award 2016. 'Goodness!" (Stephen Fry, tweet about Charlie's video).
Venue description: Part of The Liquid Room and offering 2 fantastic separate I stage rooms and beer garden music bar. The venue can be accessed from 9 Victoria Street. Title: Hatty's Last Stand
Description: Harriet Stand (Hatty to her friends) is auditioning for a part in the critically acclaimed play Life. Harriet’s dilemma is to find the right role to audition for. We follow her trials and smiles in this relentless pursuit of a role. Hatty's Last Stand is a one-woman show written and performed by Sarah Grace. It is 20 years since Hatty first came crashing onto the scene back in 1998, and to mark this anniversary she is treading the boards once more. Hatty's Last Stand is returning to cause humorous havoc in 2018 through a familiar story.

Title: In Conversation With... Arnold Brown
Description: Arnold Brown first came to prominence in the early 1980s at Soho's Comedy Store and later, at the Comic Strip live show, with Alexei Sayle, Rik Mayall and French and Saunders et al. In 1987, he was the first stand-up comedian to win the prestigious Perrier Award – and in 1990, Frank Sinatra described Arnold's support appearance at Ibrox Park as being 'the highlight of my career'. He is currently the comedy consultant on the podcast Are You Feeling Funny? with leading comedians such as Paul Merton, Stewart Lee and Helen Lederer.

Title: In Conversation With... Barbara Dickson
Description: Scotland's top-selling female album artist of all time, Barbara Dickson has had a fifty-year life in music, telling stories through song and performance in the theatre and continuing to tour to this day. In conversation with Graham Spiers, Barbara traces her career from the late-1960s Fife folk circuit to chart-topping success and prime time TV, the theatre and a 2002 OBE. Described by Aly Bain as having the best female voice ever to come out of Scotland, Billy Connolly says simply: 'her voice just nails me to the wall. She's a one-off'.

Title: In Conversation With... Judy Murray
Description: Former Scottish tennis international with 64 national title successes, Judy was appointed Scottish National coach in 1995, becoming the first woman to pass the LTA's Performance Coach Award. She initiated the Scottish Development School, producing four Davis Cup players and one Fed Cup player, including her Grand Slam-winning sons, Jamie and Andy. Judy has pioneered initiatives to grow the profile and numbers in women’s tennis, including Miss-Hits, for girls age five to eight; Tennis on the Road, taking tennis into remote and deprived areas; and She Rallies, to encourage Scottish women and girls into tennis.

Description: A show that makes smack talk an art form. Comedy Roast Battle Edinburgh puts two comedians head to head in a battle of wit and put-downs. Each comic gets five jokes to roast their opponent. The opponent can respond with an off-the-cuff rebuttal. Ultimately the winner is decided by a guest panel of audacious judges, choosing to compliment the winner or make it worse for the loser. Come and join us for one of the funnest shows you'll ever see. Title: In Conversation With... Ruby Wax
Description: A much-loved comedian for over 25 years, at the peak of her success Ruby bizarrely jumped ship to gain a master's degree from Oxford in mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, then produced two best-selling books – Sane New World and A Mindfulness Guide for the Frazzled. An unspeakably brilliant one-woman show and world tour followed. In 2015, she received an OBE for services to mental health. Her 2018 best-seller, How to be Human: The Manual, written with a little help from a monk and neuroscientist, is the subject of a new show touring from September.

Description: Debut performance by brand-new band, BrÒg, featuring legendary piper Gary West on pipes, whistles, vocals and guitar; virtuoso fiddler Greg Borland on fiddle and bass, and the sensational Sandy Brechin on accordion. Jigs, reels, airs and Scottish songs. Gary West is one of the country's top pipers, currently with Glasgow City Police Pipe Band and the famous Atholl Highlanders, ex Ceolbeg, Caledon and Clan Alba. Greg Borland plays with Other Roads, Burach, ex Caledon and the Kathryn Tickell Band. Description: A selling exhibition celebrating centuries of Iranian culture, cuisine and craftsmanship. Featuring traditional pottery from Hamadan, hand-painted tiles from Isfahan and introducing the culinary heritage of this ancient land. Join us in an exploration of the rich culture of this cradle of civilisation. Enjoy an evening of poetry, study the cuisine with cookery demonstrations and partake in a Persian feast with us. Traditional craft items and ceramics will be available to purchase.

Title: Caledonia: Spirit of Place
Description: Ian Scott Massie has fond childhood memories of Scotland. Subsequently, he has come back for many sketching and painting visits. Ian’s atmospheric watercolours and original screen prints capture the spirit of Scotland: the skylines of town and cities, mesmerising vivid colours at sunset and the subtle greys of rainy days. Julia Linstead, an artist from the Scottish Borders, sandblasts original designs on glass. Julia’s unique etchings mostly focus on floral patterns that are carefully selected according to the shape and colour of vessels and vases hand-blown by Jane Charles, with whom Julia collaborates.

Title: Theatre Uncut: Women on Power
Description: The multi award-winning political agitators are back at the Traverse with a morning of outstanding new writing and fiery debate. Join the Theatre Uncut team as they present their brand-new collection of plays by some of the UK's most dynamic female playwrights exploring the theme of power. They will also be joined by inspiring guests from across the festival to discuss this historic moment in gender politics as the Women's Marches, #timesupnow and #metoo rock the world.
Warnings: Strong language
Venue description:
The Traverse Theatre is Scotland's new writing theatre. From its conception in 1963, it has embraced a spirit of innovation and risk-taking that has launched the careers of many of Scotland's best-known writers. With two custom-built and versatile theatre spaces, the Traverse’s home in Edinburgh’s city centre is a powerhouse of vibrant new work.

Owen Jones described it as a 'challenging book that takes on not only the Right, but also the Left in the balance between social justice and personal responsibility'. It shouts out that women are sick of being whistled and shouted at on the street and fed up of being treated as though they won’t mind. Flattered invites you to look at a collage of these thoughts, worries and aggressions that many women have using physical theatre, sound and music; telling a story, lived out by many, heard by few.

All the therapists she’s sacked said it’s because of 'abandonment issues', but it’s actually because she didn’t blow out any candles on a cake. A darkly comic show about life’s stumbling blocks and scrambling over them. ‘Brutally funny’ (Guardian). ‘Get out of my house’ (Mother-in-law).

Description: We're hosting drop-in screenings of Festival in Edinburgh (1955) and Edinburgh on Parade (1970). Watch these fascinating records of previous Edinburgh festivals from Scotland’s Moving Image Archive. The films last 14 minutes and run consecutively. Scotland’s Moving Image Archive collects and preserves thousands of film treasures. Our screening gives you a taste of what is available. Festival in Edinburgh is a stylish documentary about the 1954 festivals and Edinburgh on Parade brings the 1969 festivals to life in impressionistic observation.

Title: In Conversation With... Paddy Hill
Description: One of the so-called Birmingham Six, wrongfully convicted of the Birmingham pub bombings in 1974, at that time the worst terrorist atrocity in mainland Britain. Along with the fight to free Mandela, the campaign to free the Six became one of the biggest human rights campaigns in the world, finally resulting in the quashing of their convictions in 1991. Since then Paddy Joe has campaigned tirelessly on behalf of fellow falsely-imprisoned inmates. In 2001 he set up the Miscarriages of Justice Organisation, which continues to provide legal support for those who claim factual innocence.

Title: In Conversation With... Richard Leonard
Description: A proud socialist and trade unionist, elected Scottish Labour Party leader in 2017 on a radical programme of change. He is committed to a programme to make public services, including buses and rail, work in the interests of the public and not private shareholders.

Title: Sad Clowns
Description: Can you decide how you're remembered? Would you want to? Would you leave a video behind just in case? Two people on stage. One person has hit the record button. What ensues is a cabaret of various ways in which one can attempt to preserve their memory, from a death tango to a reality TV skit. Partly naturalistic, partly absurd and all-round darkly comical, Sad Clowns is an exploration of subjectivity and the remoteness of truth in humanity under capitalism and its constructs.

Social media feeds are filled with people ticking events off the list, yet you feel you that you’ve not even made it to the shops! Her is twentysomething, she has a five-year plan in place but life events put a spanner in the works. Our inclusive non-auditioning choir comprises people with varying mental health backgrounds. We are still enjoying our weekly rehearsals and even wrote our own song together. We'll have a few surprise guests with us on stage to show you what the joy of music is all about! All profits to mental health charities.

Just explores these issues by creating safe spaces for dialogue and exchange between affected groups.

Title: Emil Nolde: Colour Is Life

Title: Abolish Childhood!
Description: Childhood is an injustice. Childhood infantilises, exploits, and oppresses children. Dr Philip Cook (University of Edinburgh) argues that justice demands we abolish childhood. But how can we abolish childhood? And would abolishing childhood harm children? Philip explains how society creates childhood through its laws. These laws aim to protect children, but they end up disempowering them. Children should be treated as equals, entitled to make their own choices about their lives. Treating children as equals might seem shocking, but abolishing childhood is the best thing we can do if we truly care about our children.

Title: Doing Drugs (Policy) / Take More Drugs
Description: Discussions about drug use and drug policy often involve stories – personal experience combined with knowledge gleamed from the media and other sources. But how are these stories translated into policy, and what validity should we give to personal experience in drug policy decisions? Using interview data and background experience, researcher Anna Ross (The University of Edinburgh) will be exploring personal narratives on drugs policy in Scotland. In particular, she looks at how stories can help us feel empathy and understanding and create policy built on compassion and individual rights opposed to retribution.

And yet we rarely take the time to question it. So join researcher David Mountain (The University of Edinburgh) as he explores the many problems with patriotism. Bringing together evidence and arguments from science, philosophy and politics, he'll reveal why patriotism is illogical, dangerous and a complete waste of time.

The Bugle has been entertaining and misinformatising hundreds of thousands of weekly listeners since 2007. Until 2015, The Bugle featured Andy alongside his long-term collaborator John Oliver. Since its 2016 relaunch, a worldwide cast of guest co-hosts has brought new life to one of the most enduringly successful comedy podcasts in the known universe. Warning: may contain puns. www.thebuglepodcast.com @hellobuglers
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Andy Zatzman / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Under new direction, New Town Theatre is heralding in a new Fringe age of outstanding Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Music and Interactive Game Play in the New Town area! Situated in the beautiful Freemasons' Hall, built in 1913 (on elegant George Street, between Assembly Rooms and the Edinburgh International Book Festival), the New Town Theatre is a must visit destination. A beautiful Fringe venue with well-equipped and comfortable theatre spaces.

All venue spaces: 1 wheelchair per venue space, per production. Staff are happy to assist if appropriate. Regretfully, staff are unable to assist electric wheelchairs. Title: Musical Comedy Guide Showcase
Description: Free daily hour-long showcase of the best musical comedy at this year's Edinburgh Festival, courtesy of the Musical Comedy Guide website (check for full listings). Come along each evening to see a hand-picked selection of live comedy using music – funny songs, satirical parodies and more. So if you're a fan of Flight Of The Conchords, Victoria Wood, Bill Bailey, The Axis Of Awesome, Rachel Parris, Abandoman, Tim Minchin, Flo & Joan, Mitch Benn, Jonny & The Baptists, Jess Robinson, David O'Doherty, Frisky & Mannish, Jollyboat, Fascinating Aïda, Rob Deering etc, you'll know what to expect!
Artist: Dave Nattriss's Musical Comedy Guide / PBH’s Free Fringe

Title: Kevin Matviw: Self Defence for Cowards
Description: Canadian comedy veteran and perpetual white belt Kevin Matviw (The Second City) returns to the Fringe with an unhinged solo sketch show filled with improv, “karate” and hilarious characters that will leave you laughing and feeling almost empowered! 'Saturday Night Live worthy' (Globe and Mail). 'Hilarious… You just have to watch and see for yourself!' (The Insider, CBS Television).
Venue description: Home to Fringe shows in the past, this is the first year of free Fringe Festival shows at The Place Hotel, a luxury four star boutique hotel, situated on York Place, close to The Stand, Playhouse and St Andrew Square. With a bar, covered outdoor terrace and free shows all day, this is the perfect place to enjoy the Fringe in the New Town, and relax between shows.

Title: Death Ray Cabaret
Description: After performing to sold out crowds in Toronto, Death Ray Cabaret returns to the Edinburgh Fringe with more fast-paced songs and break-neck banter. Silly, dark and delightful, come celebrate human life as we knew it with hilarious songs and characters. You'll leave the theatre with a smile on your face and a skip in your step as you head towards your impending doom!
Venue description: Home to Fringe shows in the past, this is the first year of free Fringe Festival shows at The Place Hotel, a luxury four star boutique hotel, situated on York Place, close to The Stand, Playhouse and St Andrew Square. Title: Risk
Description: 'Free copy of Risk magazine with chocolate biscuits' shout Gabby and Matt at South Kensington Tube station. They also, of course, like chocolate biscuits (who doesn't?!) and intend to keep some for themselves. They don't know if their boss and/or the client are going to be checking up on them, photograph them, or worse, find their hidden biscuits! They also don't know if bloke-in-van over there is the agency driver checking up on them or just some bloke leering at them! So please, take a magazine, but I'm afraid we are all out of biscuits...
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, The Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11:00-02:00. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: CROW
Description: CROW is the genre-defying new stage show and new album by vocalist Bird Radio – 'folk-horror of the darkest hue' (fRootsMag.com) – based on poetry from Ted Hughes’ 1970 masterpiece on grief, Crow: From The Life And Songs Of The Crow. It is a unique collaboration with a band featuring sonic duo Pig7 that works with live processing, found sound and synthesis to create powerful atmospheres, providing an immersive and otherworldly sonic terrain for Bird Radio to channel, through his voice, the spirit of the ultimate trickster, Crow. Poetry, songwriting and performance like you have never seen or heard.

Title: Creative Project: An Afternoon With Wendy and Friends – Road to Meikle Seggie
Description: Creative Projects: An afternoon with Wendy and friends at Greyfriars Kirk. 24 August 2018 13:30. Free, includes reception and discussion. The afternoon is a collection of songs, poems, art, orchestral poems, dialogues and connections inspired by Richard DeMarco’s Road to Meikle Seggie. Opening remarks by Richard DeMarco. 'To travel the road to Meikle Seggie is to undertake any journey which offers unexpected opportunities for intellectual growth and self-discovery.' We each have our own Road to Meikle Seggie to travel and explore. Come join us.
Artist: Wendy Kaiser and friends, including special guest, Richard DeMarco
Venue description: Founded in 1620, Greyfriars Kirk is an iconic building situated in the heart of Scotland's capital.  Also at the centre of the Fringe Festival venues, it is a beautiful and atmospheric space for worship. With a magnificent acoustic the Kirk is often host to many performing arts events including orchestral and choral concerts and organ recitals. The Kirk and museum are open to visitors from Spring to autumn.

Title: Connected Lives
Description: Baz, Muyemba and Poppy are isolated and feel alone – in a city of half a million people. How is this possible? What has caused this isolation? How and where can they make connections again? In partnership with The Bethany Christian Trust, The Alma Project and Shakti Women's Aid, Connected Lives explores the complex reasons that people become isolated including addiction, domestic violence, mental health difficulties and homelessness. The performance invites the audience to respond with suggestions for possible ways forward.

Title: Beta Test
Description: This show will be hilarious and moving and energetic and tearjerking and heartwarming and most of all: made up completely on the spot! We are an improv group from Stanford University in California!
Venue description: This NEW colourful Grassmarket bar and basement lounge has the trapping of the Pacific, with a selection of freshly prepared foods, drinks, cocktails and family friendly entertainment to suit all. During the Edinburgh Fringe we host PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement lounge.

Title: Alistair Barrie – The InternationAL
Description: Alistair Barrie headlines comedy clubs all over the world and is a BBC Scotland Breaking the News regular. He has been nominated for Best Show at the Fringe twice and lost both times. This year he is going for the hat-trick. The InternationAL is his eighth solo show, which means five of the others haven't been up to scratch either. 'Properly smart comedy for grown-ups, by a properly smart comic' **** (Scotsman). 'No one does righteous indignation with the same brio as Barrie' (Guardian).
Venue description: Part of The Liquid Room and offering 2 fantastic separate I stage rooms and beer garden music bar. The venue can be accessed from 9 Victoria Street. The Annexe & Warehouse Rooms will feature a wide and varied selection of PBH FREE FRINGE comedy, cabaret and music acts everyday during August from 11am - 1am. Under 18's, accompanied by a responsible adult, can attend suitable shows until 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Ramp access to courtyard bar via Victoria street entrance. There is a flight of stairs down to the main performance space and a further flight of stairs to the annex.

Title: Henry
Description: Kirsten Brown and Guy Woodhouse present the show Henry. A 50-minute shared stand-up show that is their first. Of all the Henrys history has to offer, who is the best? Ford, the VIII, or the Hoover? Don't expect any scientific experiments to prove this, but do expect to hear some dodgy sonnets, and a complaint letter to God. You will laugh a lot, or at the very least sympathise with Guy and Kirsten's situation. Kirsten Brown: 'Neatly off-kilter' (Bruce Dessau, BeyondTheJoke.co.uk). Guy Woodhouse: 'Unique relaxing energy, like jazz' (Barry Ferns).
Artist: Brown and Woodhouse / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.

Title: Luke Wright, Poet Laureate
Description: The campaign to make Luke Wright the new Poet Laureate starts here. All new material from 'the best performance poet around' (Observer). ***** (Scotsman, List, ExeuntMagazine.com, Herald, ThreeWeeks, BroadwayBaby.com). **** (Guardian, Telegraph, Mirror).
Warnings: There is some swearing.
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). Title: We Are
Description: A high-octane hour of drumming, singing, storytelling and dance. Los Angeles all-woman band Adaawe premiere their new show, bouncing hip multiculturalism off their own ethnic roots from Africa to the Middle East to Morocco to Panama to the USA. Inspired by, and dedicated to, the women of Ghana, West Africa, who gather under the full moon to tell stories of sorrow and joy. We Are shares stories of women of many cultures who have inspired, changed, and healed our world. Skin on skin. Wood on wood. Voices on air. The first heartbeat. Put your ear to the earth and listen!

Description: 21 August 2018, 10:00-13:00, The Space @ Jury’s Inn. Workshop: exploring your place relationships, connecting with circles of support and your artistic inspiration from your individual sense of home, in a collaging workshop. Come explore your artistic voice, resources and action plan in this free workshop with snacks and supplies provided.
Artist: Wendy Kaiser and Marna Hauk, PhD

Title: Marjolein Robertson: It's Time
Description: Shetland comedian Marjolein Robertson weaves through time with jokes, anecdotes and storytelling. Intertwining her own life with a traditional Shetland folk tale. 'Marjolein Robertson is a highly promising and delightfully original act' (Jay Richardson, Scotsman). 'Her performance was easygoing, charming, and disarmingly frank, reducing the audience to quivering puddles of laughter constantly, with stories of romantic failures and drunken shenanigans' (Alex Garrick-Wright, Shetland News, 2017). 'Marjolein Robertson's stage presence and narrative style is informal and charming' (Kenza Marland, List, 2017). 'Charming, intelligent, and self-deprecating in the best way' (Catherine Hart, ArtMurmurs.nz, 2017).

Hear again pop and folk hits like Putting on the Style, Amazing Grace, My Old Man's a Dustman, Wild Rover, Hello Mary Lou, Nobody's Child, Singing the Blues, Tom Dooley, Freight Train, Does Your Chewing Gum Lose It's Flavour, Heartaches by the Number and many more.

Title: In the Glare of the Neon Yak
Description: Cult comedy spoken word artist Robert Garnham returns to the fringe. A late-night sleeper service, a train full of circus folk, a mysterious apparition in the fog... Comedy and poetry collide in this new show from the Professor of Whimsy.
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). Title: Norman Maclean
Description: After successes at the Edinburgh Fringe with the Soft Shoe Skiffle Band, here’s another trip down memory lane with some fun and pop and folk songs like – Wild Mountain Thyme, Streets of London, Last Thing on My Mind, Don’t Think Twice It’s Alright, Dark as a Dungeon, The Boxer, Winterwood, Dirty Old Town, The Leaving of Liverpool and more.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Accessible entry is on the left from main doors. If not taking the ramp there are a few steps from the pavement to the main door

Title: Steve Richards Presents Rock'n'Roll Politics 2018
Description: In a different show every day the audience has the chance to seize back control of Rock'n'Roll Politics as broadcaster and author Steve Richards conducts a tour of the latest seismic political dramas – from Trump to Corbyn to Sturgeon, May and Brexit, discover why we are almost getting used to expecting the unexpected. In the Brexit era the audience will decide what form each show will take leaving the performer on stage to follow its instructions powerlessly. Politics even more shook up than the last year.
Venue description: Another high calibre venue. A classy alternative to the Fringe norm, boasting the most comfortable seats in town! Wonderfully located in our 8 theatre central performance hub adjacent to theSpaceTriplex and theSpace @ Surgeons Hall.  A programme of music, a-capella, theatre and comedy and our very own bar & Theatre tent in the tranquil garden adjacent makes this a must for all. For more information / Show info: www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Nick Hall: Peninsula
Description: No man is an island. But Nick Hall might be a peninsula. Hilarious and inventive stand-up, as seen and heard on BBC Two, BBC Three and BBC Radio 4. 'Brilliant' (Times). ‘Crackingly original’ **** (List). ‘One not to miss’ **** (Skinny).
Venue description: This family-run Italian restaurant on South Bridge hosts PBH Free Fringe comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am. No age restrictions before 10pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the building then performance space is down a flight of space.

Title: The Butcher, the Brewer, the Baker... and Merryn Somerset Webb
Description: Confused about money? Concerned about the economy? Join editor-in-chief of Moneyweek and FT columnist Merryn Somerset Webb as she interviews, talks over and argues with a well-known group of economics, politics and finance gurus (with a few comedians chucked in for fun). Got a burning question on anything discussed? Audience participation will be very welcome.
Venue description: Panmure House, the final home of Adam Smith, is a Category-A listed building of national cultural significance to Scotland and globally. Edinburgh Business School have restored Panmure House as a place for economic, social and moral debate and the latest academic thinking.
Venue accessibility: Please feel free to call 0131 451 3090 if you have any  questions regarding accessibility. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Panmure House is located on Lochend Close and can be accessed via the Royal Mile and/or Calton Road. There is a slight incline if approaching from Calton Road side

Title: Captain 'The Butcher' Reality
Description: Former superstar Captain 'The Butcher’ Reality returns after a 15-year absence. Has it been all nearly naked parties and B-movies or has he discovered new hobbies to deal with his rage? Wrestling meets poetry meets pain in the new play from twice Great Yorkshire Show-Off winner and multiple poetry slam winner. ‘Witty, engaging and very entertaining’ (BroadwayBaby.com, for My Wrestle Mania).
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: Three's Company, Where's Our Crowd? An Improvised Show
Description: Three wise men followed a star to Edinburgh to bring you frankincense, myrrh and comedy gold. Back for their third year, Beard of Zeus is bringing the funny in three different sizes with their brand-spanking new improv show. A show made up entirely on the spot, we threw the scripts out along with our dignity for your entertainment. It’s different every night so come back for another tasty slice of improv pie. Previous acclaim for BoZ: 'Distinguish themselves on sheer talent' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'A great find!' (Marco Polo).
Warnings: May contain strong language or themes of an adult nature
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Great stylish on site bars too. For more info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Ania and Riss Are Trying Their Hardest
Description: Funny Women regional finalist Ania Magliano and Cambridge Footlight Riss Obolensky have joined forces after two successful runs at the Edinburgh Fringe: The Footlights International Tour Show (Pleasance Dome) and Switch: A Sketch Show (Underbelly Med Quad). They are no strangers to trying to fix themselves and the world around them. They’re also no strangers to failure. They’ve tried therapy, arts and crafts, lying down, play fighting and actual fighting – but to no avail. Instead, they’ll try their hardest to make you chuckle. Join them in their debut split bill of stand-up.
Artist: Ania Magliano and Riss Obolensky / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new venue for PBH Free Fringe 2018. A wide selection of shows, including comedy, cabaret, spoken word, theatre and others, will be on tap every day in 6 stages over 2 floors. The main bar and 2 courtyard bars will be open from 11am-3am every day during August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible. Level access to ground floor and 2 courtyards. Room 1 & 6 fully wheelchair accessible. other room on first floor about 10 steps to the space

Title: That's So GCSE
Description: Blackouts. Chair duets. Overacting. Brecht. Watch these students navigate the GCSE Theatre curriculum to perform a stunning show of their combined pubescent talents, in this hilarious new comedy, showcasing the fond memory of amateur and GCSE Theatre.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. More info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: KEITH. Presents KEVIN.
Description: 'Unbeatable comedic timing' ***** (DurhamStudentTheatre.org). 'KEITH. is shaking up the status quo with a mirth that is hard to match' **** (Palatinate). After bringing a hot slice of off-beat funk comedy to the Yorkshire countryside, KEITH. is now in the big 'Burgh. With surreal, high-energy sketches and original tunes spanning from awkward game shows to Tesco's love songs, here's a show that might promise to change your entire life for an hour. Maybe.
Venue description: Home to Fringe shows in the past, this is the first year of free Fringe Festival shows at The Place Hotel, a luxury four star boutique hotel, situated on York Place, close to The Stand, Playhouse and St Andrew Square. With a bar, covered outdoor terrace and free shows all day, this is the perfect place to enjoy the Fringe in the New Town, and relax between shows.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. 3 Steps to door/bar, stairs to performance space

Title: Fright Bus Service
Description: A theatrical sightseeing tour onboard a classic 1960s Routemaster bus, taking you on a journey around the darker side of Europe’s most haunted city. Join your creepy conductor and a peculiar psychic investigator on a hilarious trip around the ancient city’s sites of murder, torture, execution and paranormal activity. From the makers of the Edinburgh Ghost Bus Tours comes this comedy horror show you’ll never forget as you travel around the city and discover its dark and unusual secrets. 'Far better than much of the Fringe' (Edinburgh-Reviews.co.uk).
Warnings: There is some walking involved during the tour, and due to the classic design of the bus itself it is not wheelchair accessible unless the wheelchair can be folded and kept close to the audience member as they're sitting on the bus.
Venue description: A black classic 1960s Routemaster bus transformed into a theatre space, with cameras, screens, audio/visual capabilities and seating for up to 64 audience members. Beautiful interior.
Venue accessibility: Due to the classic design of the bus itself it is not wheelchair accessible unless the wheelchair can be folded and kept close to the audience member as they're sitting on the bus. Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Upper deck. The black bus is situated on Waverley Bridge

Title: Umbrella Man
Description: Teuchter Company, Scotland’s twice award-nominated Fringe favourites, are back with Umbrella Man, the tragicomic story of a sandwich artist who attempts to prove that the earth is flat. Using poetry, storytelling and improvised piano to take the audience on a journey to the limits of common sense, Umbrella Man is a Don Quixote for the millennial generation: a daft, moving, unmissable show. Umbrella Man is written and performed by poet, pianist, founder of Teuchter Company and member of Men With Coconuts, Colin Bramwell. 'Bramwell held a commanding presence as storyteller... his natural musicality is something to behold' (EdFringeReview.com).
Venue description: Scottish Poetry Library is the nation's iconic home of poetry. Our live literature events take place in our mezzanine with a balcony for those balmy Scottish summer nights.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access from main door, venue is located on a cobbled lane

Title: Artist – Jennifer Thomson
Description: Admirers of Jennifer Thomson's cityscapes and seascapes will be intrigued to discover a different focus in her work this year. This series of smaller, mainly figurative paintings celebrates those simple, heartwarming moments in life that make you smile. Jennifer's paintings can be found in various prestigious art collections (e.g. City Art Centre, Royal Bank of Scotland, British Golf Museum) and are regularly being shipped to clients worldwide. Some of Jennifer's Edinburgh and East Neuk paintings, plus her cards, prints and other gifts, will also be on display. Escape the city crowds at our picturesque seaside gallery.
Venue description: The Blue Easel gallery first opened it's bright blue door in April 2017. It is owned and run by resident artists Jennifer Thomson and Ruth Farquhar. The gallery is set in the heart of the beautiful, historic village of Cramond just a stones throw from the beach. There is ample parking and a choice of lovely cafes nearby. The 41 bus will bring you to Cramond from the city centre.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are two rooms in the gallery - one is on street level and fully accessible the other room is down 5 stairs

Title: Losing My Mindfulness
Description: Do you want to feel calmer, more focused and relaxed? Imagine a life where daily stress just floats by like a cloud in the sky, not a rain cloud, a nice one, a fluffy one. Yeah, do you want that? You know you do, don’t you? Join me at my mindfulness workshop where we can leave our baggage behind and be in the moment, even if that moment is not quite what you thought it would be, cos hey, what is?! Sometimes that moment is f*cking terrible. I’m joking. See, mindfulness can be fun. Fun and calm.
Venue description: Cafe and health food store offering freshly prepared vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, Scottish food and drink on the menu from 9am daily. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement function room. No age restrictions.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the shop. The performance space is down a flight of stairs

Title: The Boy With the Pearl Necklace
Description: From the creator of Will He Bonk You in the Chocolate Factory and Fridged Moan's Diary comes a new stand-up comedy spectacular! An evening of music and comedy about being young and reckless and how you too could be the owner of a pearl necklace...

Hosted by comedy historian Robert Ross.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Tony Slattery / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Scotland's original and world famous purpose-built comedy club, The Stand, is not only at the heart of the Fringe, but open 361 days per year. Playing host again to impressive comedy bills, it's not to be missed. The atmosphere is relaxed and informal, with cabaret-style seating and standing room. All seating is unreserved and first come, first served.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Stand 1 is in a basement. Access by stairs at the front of the building from the pavement of York Place. Stairs are well lit and in good condition. Steven steps down, turn 90 degrees, then two more to gain access. Staff always available to assist where appropriate. Regretfully, staff are unable to assist electric wheelchairs

Title: An Imp-Revised History of the World
Description: Ever wondered what might happen if Queen Victoria met Genghis Khan? In this totally improvised comedy, the audience choose which chapters of history they want to see rewritten. After two years of full-house performances at the Fringe, Edinburgh's own Smoky Monkeys are back again demonstrating that everything you thought you knew about history is in fact completely wrong. Prepare for inaccurate historical knowledge and made-up musical numbers! Tell your grandchildren that you saw history made up before your very eyes. 'Funny and enjoyable' (TheWeeReview.com). 'Exactly what an improv group should be' (EdFringeReview.com).
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: One of Them, One of Us
Description: Caught between Berlin and New York, Daniel Louis Vezza explores and takes on the differences between these two cities and the lifestyles that come with them, in an hour of observational and biographical stand-up.
Venue description: Home to Fringe shows in the past, this is the first year of free Fringe Festival shows at The Place Hotel, a luxury four star boutique hotel, situated on York Place, close to The Stand, Playhouse and St Andrew Square. With a bar, covered outdoor terrace and free shows all day, this is the perfect place to enjoy the Fringe in the New Town, and relax between shows.

Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Description: Join us for a postmodern take on popular songs from the past decade as well as standards by the likes of Gershwin, Berlin, and Ellington. An intimate evening of cabaret in the heart of the New Town.
Artist: Caitlin McGillivray, Jamie Lang and Friends
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music - and some book discussions,  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.

Artist: Free Festival Music / The Golf Tavern

Title: Love Like 90s R'n'B
Description: A rump-shaking stand-up comedy hour of phat beats, funky rhythms, ukulele and fun. Larissa grew up in the 90s and, just like any teenager, growing up had its difficulties – but it was OK because "mentors" like TLC helped her deal with the scrubs while Boyz II Men helped her at the end of the road. Join Larissa for fun and games as she remixes and imparts some of R'n'B’s timeless wisdom. Can you dig it? We can dig it! No diggity, no doubt!
Venue description: A brand new music and performance venue, comprising four grand arches with an inviting yard out front. Furnished with curiosities and a roaring fire at night, Fireside hosts an eclectic roster of acts alongside great beer, cocktails and street food from around the world.

Title: Dome Nights: Dark Side of the Moon – Inspired by the Music of Pink Floyd
Description: Inspired by the music of Pink Floyd, this dome spectacular features the 1973 album The Dark Side of the Moon in explosive surround sound. With spellbinding abstract projections on the dome, audiences will be surrounded to create a truly astonishing experience.
Venue description: A visit to Dynamic Earth is like nothing else on Earth. It’s a chance to experience the primeval forces of nature as they shaped our planet, to journey through space and time and even go on a 4DVENTURE around the world. You’ll be embarking on the interactive adventure of a lifetime – the lifetime of our planet. Throughout the year we offer a range of family friendly drop in events.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, On street blue badge parking

Description: Enjoy a showcase of the best comedy talent to kick-start your day with our hand-picked selection – and watch what you should be seeing more of from around the city. Great fun, great value! What's not to like? At just £6 a ticket – it's sure to be a hit! Different line-up daily – check our website for more information.
Warnings: May contain swearing. All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Title: Barry's Fringe Audio Walking Tour
Description: An immersive, downloadable, free, 45-minute audio tour of the Festival Fringe – featuring interviews about its history with many Fringe comedy legends as you walk through the chaos and fun of the 2018 Fringe. Find out where Simon Munnery got arrested, where Arthur Smith freed Nelson Mandela, where Tony Law almost got busted and many, many more interesting and location-based curios. Download the walking tour any time this August at: barryferns.com
Warnings: This walking tour is a 45-minute long downloadable audio file, which can be done at any time during the month of August.
Venue description: Outside the Tron - Hunter Square
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No wheelchair accessible toilet, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Tree
Description: Tree is a folk-rock guitarist and vocalist, originating from Belfast who with this show makes her Edinburgh Festival Fringe debut at AMC. Tree signed to MAS Records after her first ever centre-stage performance at O2 Academy Leeds, Tree invites you to an encapsulating performance and Fringe experience. Upcoming on the Leeds (UK) alternative scene, Tree is set to break into the commercial industry with newly-formed ideas and melodies. Influenced mainly by the likes of Blind Melon, Eluveitie and Avenged Sevenfold, Tree's expanding musical desires need to be heard and expressed; you will be touched in an unexpected way.

The all-day dining & drinking venue pays homage to the hustle and bustle of the former advertising room, where journos and quick witted wordsmiths would rub shoulders.

Description: Scotland! Famous for hills and of course mountains. Breathtaking, but when things go wrong, we rely on mountain rescue (mostly run by volunteers). A night of comedy hosted by The Stand Comedy Club – let's help and support this fantastic cause so that everyone can enjoy Scotland's natural majesty as safely as possible. With a stellar line-up of comics! Check the website for full line-up details.

Description: Hungry Wolf VYT return to Edinburgh Fringe with another original piece of cutting-edge theatre. Goodbye Rosetta is a fast-paced and warm-hearted tale of a group of teens coming of age. Keisha and Mo are foster sisters, they are also the misfits. When Mo’s depression makes the ground give way from under her, Keisha struggles to understand the illness that seems to be devastating the lives of the people she loves. They are forced to navigate their new reality and find their way with the guidance of the stars.
Warnings: Use of explicit language

Title: Harry Cullen
Description: Harry has been a stalwart of the Edinburgh folk scene since the early 70s and as a member of The Garvies, Town Choice and the Kinsmen he performed throughout Scotland. Eventually, Harry decided to come off the road and get a "proper job" so some may know him better as the "friendly" landlord of The Oxford Bar. There he dispenses the odd insult but loves entertaining his regulars and visitors with spontaneous Monday afternoon jamming sessions. So he's never really stopped singing and today his live performances are a great combination of traditional and contemporary music.

Title: Live Before You Die
Description: What do you do when you have a best mate who's so sad he might die? Especially since your friendship is built around a mutual appreciation of 90s hip hop, borderline alcoholism and finding creative ways to call each other dickhead. Byron is bipolar and a successful performer and writer, Dave only communicates in insults. Together they must find a way to fix Byron's broken soul before it's too late. Funny, tragic and shockingly honest, this is a true story of a friendship fighting against tragedy, told by two men on a desperate quest for happiness.
Warnings: Themes include mental health, suicide and depression. Bad language.
Artist: Byron Vincent and Dave McGinn / PBH's Free Fringe

Title: Hive Mind
Description: A series of (eight) mannequin heads are transformed by the insertion of thousands of metal pins and the application of mobile SIM cards, inviting us to question where humanity ends and technology begins. Hive Mind addresses those questions fundamentally asking what it means to be human in the digital era, posing a number of questions about identity, technology and isolation/connection stemming from our hyper connected lives.
Venue description: Open plan art gallery with dedicated access, alarm, office, kitchen, bathroom. Year-round exhibition programme. Fringe venue 256.

Title: Tales of the Unacceptable
Description: In the wake of #MeToo and #TimesUp Sameena Zehra and Seymour Mace set out to examine UK comedy. Come along and find out what happened next. We're on a mission to make the UK comedy industry a place where people can spend their time creating and facilitating art rather than wasting their time fashioning poisoned darts (both literal and metaphorical) to fend off all the f*ckwits. There'll be a Q&A at the end and all profits will be donated to Rape Crisis Scotland.

There will be char and maybe some Cher – why have a nap when you can have a nip? Join in the fun with everyone’s favourite nun-entity.

In the evening the venue transforms into a great party space with live DJs and a late licence. Check out our Rocky Horror Night and our Karaoke Sundays... and £3 Jagerbombs seven days/week and £4 cocktails Monday – Wednesday.

Title: The Orchestra of the Canongait
Description: Technically brilliant, thrillingly passionate and globally in demand, Finnish violin soloist Anna-Liisa Bezrodny is 'a real and true musician... and plays at white heat' (Jessica Duchen). Bezrodny showcases Tchaikovsky's Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 35, one of the most important works for the instrument in the history of romantic music. The entirely Tchaikovsky programme includes the familiar, beautiful, love-themed Romeo and Juliet (overture-fantasia) and Symphony No. 5 in E minor, Opus 64. First performed in 1888 following almost a decade of soul searching, the piece emphasises the composer's melodic gifts both subtle and spectacular.
Artist: The Orchestra of the Canongait, Robert Dick, conductor
Venue description: Founded in 1620, Greyfriars Kirk is an iconic building situated in the heart of Scotland's capital.  Also at the centre of the Fringe Festival venues, it is a beautiful and atmospheric space for worship. With a magnificent acoustic the Kirk is often host to many performing arts events including orchestral and choral concerts and organ recitals. The Kirk and museum are open to visitors from Spring to autumn.

Title: Shady With a Chance of Sunburn
Description: Dana Alexander offers her unique and irreverent perspective in an industry that is dominated by the privileged and homogeneous – a purple sheep in a group of black sheep. This is her funny, fresh and alternative perspective on our cultural shift which challenges the status quo because you can't be 'woke' if you were never asleep. In a world of constant surveillance and social media, there is nowhere to hide. New voices have been amplified and we are starting to question everything. How do you discover a country that already has people in it?

Title: Criminal
Description: Welcome to Criminal, an anarchic improv night in which four comedians have an hour to solve a grisly murder. With a different line-up every night, one detective and three suspects will investigate a mysterious case armed only with the power of improvisation. Who's innocent? Who's guilty? What's really happened? How can you kill a man with a rocking horse? At least some of these questions will be answered in front of your very eyes. A podcast and monthly gig in London, Criminal has hosted a wealth of performers including Marcus Brigstocke, Josie Lawrence, Deborah Frances-White and Miles Jupp.

Title: Elise
Description: New York, 1962. Beat poet Elise Cowen commits suicide and her family incinerates all but eighty-three of her poems. Dixie Fried Theatre's moving piece of new writing brings to light the life and legacy of a woman shrouded in Allen Ginsberg's shadow. Terry Johnson returns to the boards with his interrupted monologue KEN: a freewheeling reminiscence of his turbulent and inspiring relationship with the truly original and unclassifiable theatre maverick Ken Campbell. Milligan – a man of great sensitivity, insight and comedic invention – redefined the landscape of British comedy on stage, TV and radio. In the year of Spike’s 100th birthday, Stockwell and Larner sift through the madness and find only more of it. Playing Spike and those who surrounded him, they explore his invention, delight in his influence and look to discover what made him tick. Some nonsense here to cure a crazy world.
Warnings: Mild Swearing
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. Served with huge servings of sauce, you can consider your bouche well and truly amused. 'Imaginative, brilliant and ever-so-slightly risqué' (Scotsman).
Artist: Jo Frank and Louise Leigh / PBH's Free Fringe

Think of it as watching a DVD of Phill with a shoddy memory, and the commentary track on all the time. So you definitely get the song about Owls being bastards and that Coldplay parody. Also the chips cheese and curry sauce bit, and the bit about Puffins which is now more elaborate as he has been doing it on tour. So for a free show, it’s quite busy. You should totally bring badges to swap.
Venue description: Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. With live music six nights a week, and a host of other events constantly on the go, it's proved a firm favorite with locals and tourists for many years now. Open from 12:00-01:00 every day, apart from Sundays when we open at 12:30. No under 18's. www.bannermanslive.co.uk

Let’s just say that since Nevermind the Buzzcocks was cancelled, the scales have shifted in poetry’s favour. There will be new works, evergreen favourites and some occasional guests. Phill will also have his badge-swap buckets on site. So, you should totally bring badges to swap with him.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with a cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. Venue description: A visit to Dynamic Earth is like nothing else on Earth. It’s a chance to experience the primeval forces of nature as they shaped our planet, to journey through space and time and even go on a 4DVENTURE around the world. In the words of perhaps the most revered cartoon Caribbean crab maestro in history: 'darling it's better down where it's wetter, take it from me'. Why not come aboard and take it from us, too. 'Awesome originality! A unique voice, miles ahead of the hacks and the pretenders. Off-kilter genius!' (BBC Radio Newcastle). @johnwhalecomedy @KieranFRafferty
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Kieran and The Whale / The Stand Comedy Club

Moran will offer his unique take on love, politics, misery and the everyday absurdities of life, all served with poetical panache from one of the finest comedians of his generation. 'High-octane riffs from Irish master of grumpiness... spellbinding' **** (Evening Standard). 'Funny and fascinating, and utterly deserving of his place in the modern classics' **** (Times).
Warnings: Show may contain strong language and adult content.
Venue description: Scotland's original and world famous purpose-built comedy club, The Stand, is not only at the heart of the Fringe, but open 361 days per year. All seating is unreserved and first come, first served.

Glasgow's Chris Thorburn is back with his least personal hour yet! It’s a comedy show all about films. Good films, bad films, happy films, sad films, films you secretly love, and the films you’ve never seen but you know you’re supposed to so when someone asks if you’ve seen it you say 'of course' and while they talk at length about it you just keep nodding and going 'oh yeah', hoping they won’t realise what a fraud you are.
'Superbly comedic look at cinema with a personal touch... Genuinely hilarious' ***** (TheWeeReview.com).
Venue description: Cosy upstairs venue in the heart of the Fringe, bringing you some of the best comedians on the circuit

Warnings: Adult themes, strong language

Title: Grace Notes
Description: Meet Grace Miller. Gobby, brash and a talented pianist. Just out of prison, she is determined to get her broken life back together. A convicted killer, Gracie still has old wounds to heal and bitter scores to settle. Becky Williams plays Grace, addressing her audience with candour as she battles the demons of addiction, violence and music. Grace Notes asks the question: what does it take to get a second chance in life? A powerful and gripping one-woman show, written and performed by Becky Williams.
Warnings: Adult themes, language, partial nudity.

Title: Sheraz Yousaf: The Pursuit of Manly-ness
Description: What if you were taught how to be a man but you weren’t yet a man? So you un-taught yourself and then you learned again from someone else and they were also wrong. So you decided to read a book about it. And then looked on the internet. And then went to something where there were other men. And they told you how to be a man. What kind of man would you be?

Georgia shakes up the traditional character comedy formula and uses it to explore the way she sees the world through colours, and how she approaches both comedy and songwriting. Expect to have an absolute bleedin' laugh, basically. 'Nothing short of sublime' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Each show sees three volunteers adopt characters in a narrative of the audience's making and embarking on an epic quest. Usually for something quite silly. Assemble ye nerds and rejoice! Best Improv Show nominee, Leicester Comedy Festival 2018. Outstanding Contribution winner, VAULT Festival 2017. Festival Spirit winner, VAULT Festival 2016.
Warnings: Occasional swearing due to the improvised nature. Never vulgar

Description: As a kid you’re told you know nothing. As a teen you’re told you think you know everything. As an adult you find out you have no idea whatsoever. Join this newly minted adult and up-and-coming Australian comic, as he tackles the big questions of love, peace and oversized burgers, armed with all he has learnt in his 24 years. Title: Australia: Origin of F*cked
Description: Since 2013, Australia is the origin of racist, science denying, sexist lying thugs getting elected Prime Minister. Trump is a shitty cover band. Brexit is a tribute act. Now, we’re all probably f*cked! Fringe veteran and Australian satirist, Kieran Butler, returns for a fifth year of his sold out cult hit. Defamed by feminists and blacklisted by the director of the Australian #MICF, Butler is the enfant terrible of Australian comedy. 'One of my top ten comedians in the world' (‘Irish’ Rob Halkett from legendary band The Exploited). 'Damn good' **** (Evening News). **** (Scotsman).

Title: Shouting 'Action' at a Distance: Collaborative Productions Beyond Borders
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme, for Fringe participants. The internet has accelerated the flow of creativity across borders, but many obstacles still remain. Overcoming linguistic barriers, cultural differences, and time zones is the task of the current generation of artists. This seminar will feature excerpts of CollabFeature's "Train Station", a film produced by 40 contributors in 25 countries, each with a voice and a vote in every creative decision. A panel discussion with members of CollabFeature about the future of global filmmaking will follow.

Title: Sam Campbell: The Trough
Description: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe (often referred to as simply The Fringe) is the world's largest arts festival, which in 2017 spanned 25 days and featured 53,232 performances of 3,398 shows in 300 venues. Established in 1947 as an alternative to the Edinburgh International Festival, it takes place annually in Edinburgh, Scotland, in the month of August. I am looking forward to coming over to perform! The show is at midnight so it should be outrageous.

Title: Bastille
Description: British indie-rockers Bastille will take to Edinburgh Summer Sessions for their festival debut, after an electric eight years in the industry seeing them sell over four million albums and 11 million singles around the world. Bastille will bring their energetic, electric live set to Scotland’s capital for an unrivalled summer show on 9th August 2018.

So much so, that she wants to share her perfectly, pert pearls of wisdom with you lucky darlings… Come and celebrate all things fabulous and shimmy those blues away at a self-help, cabaret seminar like no other! An Edinburgh debut from actress and cabaret performer Jo Calderwood (Burlesque Idol, runner-up 2017 and Spare Rib Superstar, winner 2017). Expect burlesque, songs and a sassy philosophy from a true force of (enhanced) nature… Let's have a Kiki!

Title: Pigeon Man Apocalypse
Description: William Whitehurst's savage and unflinching examination of abuse and isolation is given wings in the shape of Arthur Cork, performed by the award-winning Corin Rhys Jones. Arthur has walled himself up in an abandoned warehouse, existing on a diet of pigeons and rainwater. But his isolation is about to be rudely shattered – and the demons from his past are about to be revealed. This unflinching, darkly humorous story of betrayal, murder, madness and liberation explores not only the devastating consequences of child abuse, but asks us some uncomfortable questions in the process.
Warnings: Themes of violence and child abuse.

Australian comedian Nat Harris takes you on a rollercoaster ride through the five stages of grief in 50 minutes: denial, anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance. 'She unleashes a mix of hilarious tales and heartfelt childhood reflections with a deadpan, perfectly paced delivery and dry, ballsy demeanour that is a joy' (Chortle). 'It’s safe to say that Natalie Harris’s secret is out – and a pleasure to share' (Herald Sun).

But power is addictive, and goaded by the words of some mysterious drunkards on a dark night, and her bullying husband, her mission to prove her worth turns bloody. In a society where places for women at the top are few, what lengths would you consider to break that glass ceiling? A timeless story of ruthless ambition reimagined through a female lens, yt2’s Macbeth will bring humour and a modern energy to Shakespeare’s classic.

The concert is given in aid of Peacebuilding UK which supports and implements a number of peacemaking projects with local groups and individuals in the North Caucasus region and Ukraine. An opportunity to participate in discussion with both artists will follow the concert.
