Title: A Verbal Tightrope Walk
Description: There's a fine line between the sublime and the ridiculous. Jack has no idea where it is but enjoys finding out with puns, wordplay and nonsense teetering on the border between daft and dafter, constantly testing your sense of silly and the constraints of the one-liner form. Will he go overboard with the puns or break out from the form altogether? 'Superbly formulated and consistently funny one-liners' (Back Street Heroes). 'Left me with an aching side' (NottsComedyReview.wordpress.com). 'A host of inventive gags doused in wordplay and performed with aplomb' (Stagefright Comedy).
Warnings: Adult themes, puns.
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: Stella Graham: Uncivilized
Description: Stella vs Nature, like Man vs Food, without the quadruple cheeseburgers. Warning: May contain girl going nuts and high risk of a rage infused heart attack. 'If you're a TV executive, drop what you're doing and go see her now' (Skinny). **** (FringeGuru.com).
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: Modern Horror Stories
Description: An anthology horror show featuring nine modern day tales of terror, death and the supernatural. From online paranoia and ghost hunting, to the perils of dating after the zombie apocalypse. You'll laugh, you'll scream, you'll love it. Black comedy with adult themes and not for the easily offended. Written by David Bourn and Alasdair Buddington, with James Wordsworth.
Warnings: Profanity and adult themes.
Artist: Modern Horror Stories / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new venue for PBH Free Fringe 2018. A wide selection of shows, including comedy, cabaret, spoken word, theatre and others, will be on tap every day in 6 stages over 2 floors. The main bar and 2 courtyard bars will be open from 11am-3am every day during August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible. Level access to ground floor and 2 courtyards. Room 1 & 6 fully wheelchair accessible. other room on first floor about 10 steps to the space

Title: Touring South Korea With Mid – Small Productions
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme, for Fringe participants. Did you know you should not write a name using red ink in Korea? This session will offer a frank and informative discussion about touring in South Korea, one of the major markets for international work. It will introduce South Korean theatre industry, culture and taboos to companies considering touring in the thriving Korean theatre landscape. Following the presentation, there will be Q&A and 1:1 consultation with Korean producers and international touring experts.
Warnings: Those with Fringe participant pass will be given priority access
Venue address: Appleton Tower, Corner of Windmill and Chapel Streets
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.
Venue accessibility:
Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is level access throughout Fringe Central from Chapel Street. There is a lift to the ground floor reception, first floor event spaces and Fringe offices.

Title: Babes Against Bullshit
Description: Women have claimed intellectual and economic power for themselves, culture has simply found new ways to make us inferior. A patchwork of stories tackling the identity and experiences of young women, relaying the often overlooked and dismissed realities that affect women through both a black and white cultural lens. This piece explores both the flaws and relatable realisms of womanhood, challenging gender codes yet keeping it funny! Created and performed by Camille Bell and Dona Adwera.
Artist: Camille Bell and Dona Adwera in association with yt2 Theatre
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all, the ultimate location for a Fringe venue! Seconds from the Royal Mile stages and part of our 10 theatre strong Royal Mile hub. Three spaces offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, a-capella, comedy, sketch and cabaret. A global feast for all. Lovely on site bars too. More info/Show info see: www.thespaceuk.com
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Pee Paper Pizza
Description: Wouldn’t it be great if we had superpowers that could get us out of hopeless situations? Or a hero or heroine who stands by our side? Brand-new international ensemble Donkey for Nights remind us of our inner superheroes – the ones that we sometimes can't or don't want to see. Two young women use super shero paper to come up with more and more superpowers. They remember their own childhoods, and show us that a hero doesn't always have to be perfect.
Artist: Donkey for Nights / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: The iconic world famous Waverley bar has recently reopened having undergone refurbishment throughout with both the main bar and upstairs lounge restored to full glory. A must visit bar for old and new customers alike during this years fringe and beyond. A well stocked spirits gantry and selection of traditional beers and wines are available on tap, as well as light bar snacks. During this years fringe we are hosting PBH Free Fringe shows in our upstairs lounge every day.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There is Level access from the main entrance into the bar. Ladies toilets are up a flight of stairs (15 steps).

Title: A Political Breakfast
Description: Chris O'Neill and four comics will talk about the news and be amusing while being awake! They will be joined by insomniacs in search of laughter.
Venue description: Cafe and health food store offering freshly prepared vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, Scottish food and drink on the menu from 9am daily. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement function room. No age restrictions.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the shop. The performance space is down a flight of stairs

Title: Take Refuge Under My Shade
Description: This contemporary dance piece performed by Claire Henderson Davis and Bettina Carpi follows the interweaving stories of three pregnant women: a Syrian woman refugee  journeying to the UK, a British woman describing her struggle with poverty, and the biblical story of Mary visiting Elizabeth to share her good news. The dance piece explores themes of loss, endurance and new beginnings through a female lens, not in a linear or literal way but through evoking the inner, emotional journey of the women –piecing together the fragments of lives radically changed. Soundtrack by composer Gary Lloyd.
Artist: Claire Henderson Davis and Bettina Carpi
Venue description: Just Festival events aim to challenge perceptions, celebrate differences and promote respectful dialogue. The conversations, talks, exhibitions and performances which constitute Just’s annual programme are designed to engage with topical local, national and international questions of social justice, equality and identity, including prejudice against race, ethnicity, class and economic status. Just explores these issues by creating safe spaces for dialogue and exchange between affected groups.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Absolutely (Not) Free – An Evening of Zappa – Special Extra Show
Description: Special additional show featuring former Zappa Plays Zappa vocalist/instrumentalist Ben Thomas, who will be opening the show with his own material and then joining the band for... a smorgasbord of Frank Zappa classics hand-delivered by those finest purveyours of conceptual continuity, Pygmy Twylyte! Expect pickles, poodles, dental floss, muffins, snowballs and stinky feet!
Venue description: Central, intimate basement venue with a grass roots feeling hosting a varied programme of live music, comedy and clubs 7 nights a week. Bar open until late at night. With flexible seating arrangements and an informal small dancefloor, Henry's is equally suited for live music, nightclubs, comedy and other types of performance. Strictly 18+, photo ID required
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Basement venue accessed by stairs

Title: Phil Zimmerman – Sixty-Seven Arseholes (Free)
Description: Off-the-wall stand-up with sausage. Phil’s take on the new insanity as normality. It’s bonkers! He mocks the establishment as he seeks out the world’s biggest arseholes and invites you to make nominations, throw things and sing along to anarchic punk rock. Joyful, furious and provocative. And about to hit Hollywood... See Phil in a tiny venue before he becomes too big for his underwear in Tim Burton’s epic Dumbo, coming to cinemas in March. 'Genius' (Omid Djalilli). 'F*cking wonderful' (Daniel Kitson). 'I’d rather eat my own ovaries' (Kate Copstick).
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a section of free Fringe shows in the multiple downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity right in the middle of town.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: Robbie McShane and Mary Flanigan: One of Us Is a Robot
Description: One is a comedian doing relatable stand-up, the other is a robot programmed to do relatable stand-up. Can you save humanity and spot the AI? Both Mary and Robbie think they’re the human but only one of them is right. Put on trial kangaroo-court style, Robbie and Mary will each do half an hour of their most relatable material to prove they are in fact human. The audience will then vote, and watch their choice be terminated on stage. The only Fringe Show flexible on murder!
Artist: Robbie McShane and Mary Flanigan / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: Look, it's Tom Little, Alright?
Description:
Tom Little won the Leicester Mercury Comedian of the Year 2015, was a BBC Radio New Comedy Award 2014 finalist, and appeared in both Pleasance Comedy Reserve and Big Value showcases so, you know, be impressed.
This show is about toothpaste, crisps, Austria, prawns, chicken, The Beatles, two different musicals, physical violence, sausage, regret and dogs. And at least five other things. Unless he forgets a large, important chunk of it. ‘Brilliant, loudly awkward… completely inventive’ (GiggleBeats.co.uk). ‘Hilarious' ***** (Mirror). ‘Gut-wrenchingly funny... truthfully, an hour with Tom Little almost isn’t enough’ (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: A new venue for PBH Free Fringe 2018. A wide selection of shows, including comedy, cabaret, spoken word, theatre and others, will be on tap every day in 6 stages over 2 floors. The main bar and 2 courtyard bars will be open from 11am-3am every day during August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible. Level access to ground floor and 2 courtyards. Room 1 & 6 fully wheelchair accessible. other room on first floor about 10 steps to the space

Title: Universal Dad: Searching for Pop
Description: PJ Landers brings his new story Searching for Pop to Edinburgh for the first time. It's the story of a young man's quest to find the father he never knew, met or even saw a picture of. After having a child of his own he had an overwhelming yearning to find this man. From the streets of Queens, NY to a movie set in Yonkers, NY then on an emotional cross-country journey that changes his life forever. Its about sacrifice, redemption, forgiveness and above all love. A heartfelt, funny and engaging dramatic memoir.
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: Hurricane Vs Robot
Description: Strap in for a strikingly alternative show from deadpan character act, 'The Robot' Nicholas Everritt and nutbag improviser extraordinairé Pete 'The Hurricane' Nash. 'This guy is brilliant!' (Dustin Cardinal Burns). 'Watch this space, he’s something else' (Tom Parry). 'Almost' (Gaulier). 'One of the funniest minds I've ever met' (Graham, Austentatious). 'Leaves your face hurting from laughing' (Ross Smith). 'Floods my eyes with tears every time!' (Akin Omobitan). 'Seriously funny' (Dan Audritt). 'Comedy genius or mad' (Sikisa Bostwick-Barnes). 'Comedy genius' (Valerio Sarà). 'Revolutionary' (Pedja Pavlicic). 'He's my spirit animal' (Sally Foster). 'Funniest thing I've ever seen' (Will Roden).
Artist: Peter Nash and Nick Everritt / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new venue for PBH Free Fringe 2018. A wide selection of shows, including comedy, cabaret, spoken word, theatre and others, will be on tap every day in 6 stages over 2 floors. The main bar and 2 courtyard bars will be open from 11am-3am every day during August.

Title: Is This the Worst Quiz / Game Show Ever? (Edinburgh Regional Championships) Hosted by Yianni Agisilaou
Description: A cross between Mastermind, Ultimate Cage Fighting, and the Royal Variety Hour in a bar off Cowgate. Come watch guest comedians battle it out on stage in the ultimate comedy quiz/game show. In a series of increasingly-challenging questions and potentially life-threatening tasks, there will be one, maybe two winner/s. May contain traces of stand-up, cabaret and sketch. Hosted by Yianni Agisilaou, 'stunningly good' **** (Scotsman).
Venue description: Sneaky Pete's is a one room club located on the Cowgate, with guest DJs playing throughout the week as well as at weekends. Sneaky Pete's has a full schedule of PBH Free Fringe comedy every day during the Fringe from 12noon-11pm. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible

Title: Professor Novak Presents: Cabinet – A Victorian Séance
Description: Past secrets remain hidden, not by the sinister or well-meant, but from fear. Fear of the veil and what lies beyond. Aided by Elizabeth and the Davenport's spirit cabinet, Professor Novak offers an invitation of enlightenment. To learn the secrets of the departed, pulling back the shroud that protects the living from the dead. Come peek behind the curtain. It may be your only chance. A Victorian ghost story.
Warnings: Periods of total darkness.  Adult disturbing themes.
Venue description: A new venue for PBH Free Fringe 2018. A wide selection of shows, including comedy, cabaret, spoken word, theatre and others, will be on tap every day in 6 stages over 2 floors. The main bar and 2 courtyard bars will be open from 11am-3am every day during August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible. Level access to ground floor and 2 courtyards. Room 1 & 6 fully wheelchair accessible. other room on first floor about 10 steps to the space

Title: Clicking Comedians
Description: For over 25 years, Steve Best had been delighting audiences around the world with his particularly silly brand of stand-up comedy. Then, one day, backstage at a gig, he took a blurry photo of Ross Noble and there began the start of a whole other career. Since then, Steve has used his unique, exclusive 'behind the scenes' access to take thousands of photos of comedians at work and at play. Everyone from the very new to the downright famous has been clicked (please watch the video). This photographic exhibition shows off some of his best work. www.stevebest.com
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night. Open until 5am.
Venue accessibility: All performance spaces are accessible. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Customers with access requirements are encouraged to contact the venue in advance and to make themselves known to a member of the team upon arrival to access lifts

Title: Kerry Godliman: Work in Progress
Description: Kerry Godliman is back in Edinburgh to try out material she's never said out loud before. Both an incredibly talented comedian and a phenomenal actor, Kerry is best known for her appearances on BBC's Live at the Apollo, Mock the Week, Jack Dee's Referendum HelpDesk, ITV's Bad Move, Sky Atlantic's Save Me and Channel 4's Derek. Kerry is also a regular on Radio 4 with appearances on the esteemed News Quiz, The Now Show and Just a Minute, The Wilsons Save The World as well as her own series Kerry's List. **** (Sunday Times).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman). Open until 3am.
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Pleasance Courtyard is located uphill when accessing the venue from Cowgate. The outdoor spaces of the venue are a mix of cobblestones and tarmacked surfaces

Title: Scottish Landscapes
Description: Tommy Fitchet's exhibition of unique Scottish landscape paintings from his travels around Scotland.
Venue description: Saorsa Art Gallery is located in Stockbridge, Edinburgh.

Title: Reuben Hunter – The Hoard
Description: Stand-up comedy all about mess, junk and baggage – the stuff we hold on to, and the reasons why. Stacked to the ceiling with stories, jokes and observations from comedian and self-confessed hoarder, Reuben Hunter. This show promises big things, or at least a lot of them. 'A unique and touching performance' *** (EdFestMag.com). 'It’s quirky stuff, but so damn funny!' **** (TheFourthWallMedia.wordpress.com).
Warnings: References to suicide
Venue description: A new Free Fringe comedy venue situated in the heart of the Royal Mile. Every day (12noon-Midnight) during the Edinburgh Fringe Free Fringe shows will be performed on 2 stages. On tap will be a wide selection of drinks and covered courtyard seating area.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Museum of Lies
Description: Lying. We all do it. In a ten-minute conversation with a stranger, we humans tell an average of three lies. Is lying one of humanity’s fatal flaws? Can lying ever be okay? Is lying (sometimes) as funny as all get out? Fun Club Theatre Company presents The Museum of Lies, a timely theatrical interrogation of lying, lies and liars. Five eccentric tour guides deliver, for your entertainment and illumination, a hilarious, poignant exposé of all manner of deceit – including little white lies and great big whoppers.
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The pedestrian route available from the Royal Mile is wheelchair accessible

Title: Old Jewish Jokes
Description: Sixth year of the UK's most successful ever Jewish comedy. The traditional flavour of Jewish humour plus a satirical look at the life of the modern Jewish comic. For brief video clip see oldjewishjokes.co.uk. ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). **** (Scotsman, Mirror, ThreeWeeks). Admission free, gentiles half price.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere music venue, at the heart of town just off of the Royal Mile hosts free festival shows during the day, and live music in the evenings - with a wide offering of drinks available all day!
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is one small step into the venue

Title: Eleanor Westbrook: Big Berg
Description: Let the 'Queen of silliness (***** BroadwayBaby.com). Eleanor Westbrook take you on an adventure to the South Pole, inspired by the journals, ambitions and adventures of Ernest Shackleton and Robert Scott. Why do people take great risks, to do things that no-one has done before? Expect silver onesies, existential crises and emperor penguins in a dark basement.
Venue description: Just of Princes Street Club La Vida will be hosting Free Fringe shows everyday during the Edinburgh Fringe in 2 performance rooms. Under 18's, accompanied by a responsible adult, can attend suitable shows until 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There is a flight of steps down into venue, level access once inside

Title: Akbayan
Description: Akbayan is a beautiful folk legend that is performed by the spectacular Kazakh Theatre of Drama and Music Kyzylorda and directed by the esteemed Hussein Amir Temir. This will be a European premiere and suitable for all audiences. Bayan and Kozy are the main characters in this legend and they both bring to life the history, romance and tradition of Kazakhstan. The beautiful Bayan is promised in marriage to Kozy as a young child and while Kozy always remains besotted by the idea of Bayan, she forgets him, and his wooing of her becomes the stuff of legends!
Artist: Kyzylorda Theatre of Music and Drama, Kazakhstan
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Accessible entry is on the left from main doors. If not taking the ramp there are a few steps from the pavement to the main door

Title: A Dangerous Woman
Description: Fringe First and DarkChat Best Director winner Renny Krupinski's new one-woman play is funny, poignant, touching and disturbing. When a woman’s perfect marriage descends into a mixture of apathy, rage and enforced dependency, the reality of losing everything brings about a completely unexpected, unimaginable career change. Preview quote: 'Amazing, take it to Edinburgh' (Audience review). Previous critiques: Bare: 'In this play, written, directed and choreographed by Renny Krupinski, a world dripping with testosterone is brought home with the punch, slap and crack of an adrenaline-soaked fight' (Scotsman). The Alphabet Girl: 'Renny Krupinski’s script is a marvel' (UpstagedManchester.com).
Venue description: Located seconds from the Royal Mile and part of our 10 space strong Royal Mile performance hub. Two intimate spaces host an array of new and established work from small scale theatre to spoken word, sketch, stand-up and chat. Also the home of 'YourSpace' the festivals very own production house for performers.  For more info on Shows and YourSpace see : www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Lia Hatzakis – Onion Gum
Description: Lia Hatzakis delivers a multi-character show, playing every member of the Onion family. Hatzakis’s one-woman comedy drama is multilayered and filled with depth, heartbreak and hilarity. 'The female Derek' (Luke Barnes, award-winning writer). 'Lia Hatzakis is fantastic to watch' **** (LondonTheatre1.com).

Title: Dave Maher Coma Show
Description: Dave Maher was almost unplugged from life support during a month-long coma. He was eulogised on Facebook. Then he woke up. The Chicago stand-up comedian told the story on This American Life. He brings his 'carefully observed, discomfitingly intimate, disarmingly funny monologue' (Chicago Reader) to the Fringe for its international debut.
Warnings: Sexual content, medical content, bodily humor.

Title: Malicious Mischief? Women's Suffrage in Scotland
Description: Marking the centenary of women getting the vote, this exhibition displays together for the first time records of the Scottish authorities and their dealings with the Suffragettes. Protests and arrests, hunger strikes and force-feeding are all starkly revealed in the official records. Many contemporaries regarded the Suffragettes as violent troublemakers. The Scottish authorities often charged them with ‘Malicious Mischief’, but were they just criminals? Did the Suffragettes’ actions help or hinder the cause? Discover the stirring story of the struggle for the vote in Scotland by peaceful and violent means.
Venue description: National Records of Scotland

Title: No Success Like Failure
Description: How do we define success? Is failure ever an option? Is a teasmade an appropriate 60th birthday gift? Does anyone really know what is going on at all, ever? Expect beguiling stories and big belly laughs as Jake attempts to answer these questions and more. 'Definitely endearing' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Imaginative and original’ (Scotsman). BBC New Comedy Award nominee (2015, 2017 and 2018)

Title: Harmon Leon's American Horror Story
Description:
NY comedian and Vice contributor Harmon has made a career infiltrating extremist groups. A multimedia journey into such Trump America entities as Hell House, a Christian haunted house where they scare the Jesus into you...literally, a staring cult, and crazy cat ladies. An international hit. Complete sell-out fringe ‘17. 'Leon’s hilarious subterfuge of a collapsed system makes us laugh as we slowly swirl down the muddy toilet' (Doug Stanhope). 'A stand-up version of Louie Theroux' (BroadwayBaby.com).
'I was reminded of Spalding Gray presenting his great work' (NewYorkTheaterGuide). 'Cross between Michael Moore and South Park' (Melbourne Age).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com

Title: Daniel Nicholas: Travaux En Cours
Description: If you remember MSN, getting your first DVD player and video game soundtracks from the 90s, then you won’t forget this show. Whilst longing to be a teenager again (life was better back then right?) 'Prince of Peculiar' (GreatCentral.org.uk) Daniel Nicholas, presents an alternative political game show that investigates communications between different fractions of society. Whoa! Sounds serious, doesn’t it? It really isn’t. It’s more like stand-up comedy with some party games. ‘Someone as inventive as this should have a future in comedy.' (Chortle.co.uk).
Warnings: Very interactive / audience participation
Venue description: Having undergone a £1Million refurbishment Bourbon celebrates a unique bar/restaurant and nightclub space. The multi-purpose venue, open 7 days & nights a week during the Edinburgh Fringe, hosting a variety of PBH Free Fringe shows everyday.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Approx. 15 steps into the main bar. Once inside performance spaces are fully accessible

Title: Fagin and the Star City Rebels
Description: Fagin and the Star City Rebels welcome you to the stargate, a portal to strange and mysterious worlds. Come meet the good, the bad, the twisted, and the downright dangerous. The Theatre of the Wild, Beautiful and Damned is a carnival of delights leading somewhere you don’t want to go. Somewhere dark and cold, filled with the damp ambiguous shapes of things you’d hoped were forgotten. The company is the creation of Lee Mark Jones. 'I love Lee, he’s dangerous and doesn't give a f*ck and I love that' (Chris Thorpe).
Warnings: Contains simulated violence, nudity and very strong language.
Artist: Theatre of the Wild, Beautiful and Damned
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue, In another unrivaled location we present the ultimate powerhouse of live performance. Part of our 8 space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter. A pulsating programme of cross genre performance art, the festival's largest programme of new writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information . Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Three ground floor theatres, lift to Grand Theatre. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. On approach there are ramps to the venue box office

Title: Church of Phil
Description: Join award-winning oddballs Fire Donkey as they blur the lines between fiction and reality in this interactive madcap comedy seminar about their imagined experience of living with a cult on a caravan holiday park in Wales. Expect silliness, dance, obscure 90s camping nostalgia, a psychotic chimp, and just the right amount of blood sacrifice to keep it tasteful. Winner of Best Original Show at Swindon Fringe 2017. 'Gleeful absurdity' **** (Buzz Magazine). 'Appealing grubby anarchy' (TheSwindonian.co.uk). 'One to keep an eye on' (LondonPubTheatres.com). And one woman just wished us 'good luck'.
Artist: Fire Donkey Productions / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new Free Fringe comedy venue situated in the heart of the Royal Mile. Every day (12noon-Midnight) during the Edinburgh Fringe Free Fringe shows will be performed on 2 stages. On tap will be a wide selection of drinks and covered courtyard seating area.

Title: Brown Guys, Grey Skies
Description: An outsider perspective to life in Europe. Part observational humor, part cathartic revelation, the show zigzags through hilarious childhood stories from India and how it ricochets in present day Europe. 'Original and refreshing' (Luxembourg Times). 'The storytelling is what makes this show fabulous' (CitySavvy.com).
Artist: Sundeep Bhardwaj and Deepu Dileepan / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A new Free Fringe comedy venue situated in the heart of the Royal Mile. Every day (12noon-Midnight) during the Edinburgh Fringe Free Fringe shows will be performed on 2 stages. On tap will be a wide selection of drinks and covered courtyard seating area.

Title: SHAnd Up Comedy
Description: Join us for an hour of fabulous comedy as part of the Fringe Free Festival. We’re in the third year of SHAnd Up Comedy and it just keeps getting better! Check out performances from some of the Fringe's funniest comedians who have all very generously donated their time to SHAnd Up Comedy! All donations at this event will go straight to Scottish Huntington’s Association (SHA) to support families living with cruel neurological condition Huntington’s disease (HD). Comedians include: the wonderful Taylor Graham, the incredible Katie Maria and the fantastic Ifrah Qureshi. (Not even exaggerating with those adjectives).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue with five rooms of free shows running throughout the day and night, all located around a vibrant and buzzing courtyard in the middle of Cowgate. With a huge drinks selection, a wide bar menu, and a courtyard full of street-food tents and cocktail huts. Shows run from 10am to 2am, with music through until 5am.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Paul Wade: Mortal
Description: Do you struggle to fit in in an ever-changing world? Does the speed of change make you feel old before your time? Then you know how Paul feels. Join him as he exposes his thoughts, fears and vulnerabilities and makes everyone feel a bit better about just being themselves. 'One of the most promising new comedians around' (The Herts and Essex Observer).
Venue description: The Phoenix Bar & Kitchen is a family friendly bar serving food until midnight daily, with a daily selection of free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival from midday until midnight each day of the Fringe in the basement room. To add to this there's also Sky Sports shown on the big screens upstairs.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Post-Coital Risotto
Description: A mix of stand-up, musical comedy, and unusual surnames from two local Edinburgh comedians. Bryan Ghosh – whose writing is 'mind-blowingly brilliant' (ThreeWeeks) and Chris Iskander – 'a doubly-talented man' (Skinny) – know full well you won’t have heard of them, so will spare you phrases like 'up-and-coming' and 'rising stars' and just promise it’ll be funny.
Artist: Bryan Ghosh and Chris Iskander / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Located in the old Clydesdale Bank building on Lothian Rd Festival Square. During the Edinburgh Fringe we will be providing Free Fringe shows everyday, 25 taps of craft beers, amazing menu, outside seating area and integrated BottleDog!
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Wheelchair lift from bar to upper level lounge and function room (The Garage). If not taking the lift there are 5 steps into the performance space

Title: Tygers Of Pan Tang – Edinburgh Festival Fringe
Description: In the May 1979 issue of Sounds magazine the term ‘New Wave of British Heavy Metal’ was used to describe a second wave of heavy metal bands that emerged in the late 1970’s. It was an era considered to be a major foundation stone for many metal genres. The pioneers of NWOBHM who have had a major influence with their musical style include Iron Maiden, Motörhead, Saxon, Diamond Head and … Tygers of Pan Tang.
Venue description: Stramash is a 900 capacity Live Music Venue in a converted church in Edinburgh's historic Old Town.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Wheelchair access to ground level with accessible toilets

Title: Well, It's Woody – Free
Description: In association with PBH's Free Fringe, veteran chanteuse Woodstock Taylor and her band of aging gits, Dai Lowe, Bev Wright and Max Scratchmann, bring their mixed bag of songs, poems and tales to the centre of things. Standards, originals and parodies, with an ever-changing array of guest talent, means it's never the same show twice. 'That's the most entertained I've been in ages!' (Audience member at The Street, 2016). 'You really should get out more' (Us, in reply).
Warnings: Strong language possible, sad songs likely, silliness probable.
Artist: Woodstock Taylor and Friends / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of FREE comedy shows and live music.

Title: Peatbog Faeries – Edinburgh Festival Fringe
Description: Hailing from the Isle of Skye, the legendary Scottish trailblazers have created a glorious mixture of traditional sounds and dance floor grooves that have been embraced worldwide. Drawing upon a dazzling myriad of influences from jigs and reels through dance music, jazz, African, and more; they bring the sound of Scotland fresh-faced and breathless to new audiences from around the world. Their mainly instrumental music allows the band to develop exciting themes and soundscapes, as well as locking into their trademark hypnotic ‘Celtic Dance’ sound that no-one can resist moving to!
Venue description: Stramash is a 900 capacity Live Music Venue in a converted church in Edinburgh's historic Old Town.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Wheelchair access to ground level with accessible toilets

Title: Zach Zimmerman: Started as a Bottom, Now I'm Here
Description: Queer NYC comedian Zach Zimmerman (The Second City, The New Yorker) attacks conservative Christian parents, contemporary gay culture, and hunts for a husband in this provocative and hilarious stand-up Fringe debut. TimeOut NY described Zach as a 'hyper-prolific, wickedly-funny stand-up' and the Chicago Reader called him 'a world class comic' which are both very nice things to say. More info on Instagram @zzdoublezz
Venue description: A brand new music and performance venue, comprising four grand arches with an inviting yard out front. Furnished with curiosities and a roaring fire at night, Fireside hosts an eclectic roster of acts alongside great beer, cocktails and street food from around the world.

Title: Book Shambles Live at the Fringe with Robin Ince
Description: The acclaimed hit podcast Book Shambles, recorded in front of a live audience! Hosted by Robin Ince who‘ll be joined by a different amazing guest each show. Using books as a springboard into shambolic, often ludicrous and always passionate conversations into literature, science, philosophy, comedy, politics and, well, everything and anything. Part of the PBH Free Fringe
Artist: The Cosmic Shambles Network / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. With live music six nights a week, and a host of other events constantly on the go, it's proved a firm favorite with locals and tourists for many years now. Open from 12:00-01:00 every day, apart from Sundays when we open at 12:30. No under 18's. www.bannermanslive.co.uk
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No reserved accessible parking. entrance to the venue is fully level, however there is a single step into the toilets

Title: Jim Swann: The Man With No Vaginas
Description: Somewhere between who he is, who he thinks he is, who he wants to be, who he wishes he wasn’t and who he suspects people want him to think he is… you’ll find the child in adult’s clothing struggling to hide the fact that he has absolutely no idea what the bloody hell he’s doing.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with a cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy, ballroom and space 3 will be used during the festival by some of the best PBH Free Fringe performers on the cabaret and comedy circuit.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: The Police Sting Show
Description: The Police Sting Show in concert: Re-worked, fresh versions of all the iconic Police and Sting solo album songs in a 70-minute show featuring an acoustic Sting section. Performed totally live with the voice timbre and range of the original. Hits include: Roxanne, Fields of Gold, Every Breath You Take, Englishman in New York. Message in a bottle and more. The debut shows at Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2016 all sold out! 'Power, passion, top drawer musicians with THE voice – what a show' (Audience Review from The Police Sting Show in concert).
Venue description: Stramash is a 900 capacity Live Music Venue in a converted church in Edinburgh's historic Old Town.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Wheelchair access to ground level with accessible toilets

Title: The Good Life
Description: Welcome to the Good Life! A split-bill stand-up comedy show from two fun-loving, good-time-having, honest to goodness proper cute comedy lads. Join Steph Browne (‘one to watch’ (Funny Women) and first runner-up Southend Comedy Festival, New Act) and Rob Copland, an enigmatic, silly, performer, bringing off-kilter stand-up comedy to the people. Come and enjoy two half-hour servings of the good stuff with us.
Artist: Rob Copland and Steph Browne / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: 7+ Stages and 2 bars (Cowshed Bar & Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH FREE FRINGE shows and music EVERYDAY (Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Cabaret, Live Music). Title: A Contemporary Perspective
Description: international artists and emerging local talent. Included in this exhibition of highlights you will find detailed photographs by Freddy Fabris (USA), optical illusions by Jolanda Spagno (Italy), abstract works by Natasha Barnes (South Africa), jigsaw pieces by Keymi (France), bronze sculptures by Matt Duke (UK), charcoal drawings by Patsy McArthur (UK) and thoughtful paintings by Frank Schroeder (France) among many others.
Venue description: Urbane Art Gallery is a contemporary art gallery located in the heart of the Scottish capital city just off the Royal Mile. The gallery exhibits internationally acclaimed and award-winning artists from around the world.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Alpha Art Highlights
Description: Alpha Art is delighted to present a vibrant collection of works by local and international artists. This exhibition features well-known Scottish artist Ron Lawson's distinctive representations of the Scottish Islands and Highlands, as well as paintings by iconic British artist Jack Frame, revered for his cherry blossoms on gold leaf. Further, the mixed exhibition will include glass works by Robert Ryan and Nick Giles, landscapes by Talia Lehavi, Rosie Playfair and Elena Guillaumin; sculptures by Pauline Montgomery, Steve Yeates and Michael Disley; and seascapes by Clodagh Meiklejohn and Senja Brendon.
Venue description:
Alpha Art is one of Scotland's leading contemporary art galleries. Since being established in 2006, the gallery has built an enviable reputation due to the exceptional quality of the work exhibited.
The gallery offers a unique and diverse selection of artworks by local and international artists, both established and emerging. It also manages an ambitious programme of events throughout the year, including exhibitions and art fairs.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Marc Jennings:  Jokes 'N' That
Description: Scottish Comedian of the Year finalist and regular panelist on BBC Scotland‘s Breaking the News, Marc Jennings comes to the Edinburgh Fringe using his 'caustic wit' (Scotsman) to give his take on the world from his perspective as a young working-class Glaswegian with an intellectual bent.  Exploring his true feelings on everything from politics and sex to sexual politics, this is the most authentic and revealing show yet from one of the country's most exciting up-and-coming talents. 'An astute observer who's accomplished at channeling his frustrations into a wider social critique' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: COMMON: GROUND – Barriers to Staging Work at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe as a Working-Class Artist
Description: COMMON: GROUND is an initiative developed by COMMON, an arts organisation who exist to support the UK theatre industry in achieving greater socio-economic diversity, delivered with support from leading theatres across the country. COMMON: GROUND is an inclusive discussion exclusively aimed at artists who self-identify as working-class. This COMMON: GROUND event will offer a platform for working-class artists to share barriers they face when bringing work to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, specifically related to their class status.
Artist: COMMON, Pleasance Theatre Trust Ltd and Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society
Venue address: Appleton Tower, Corner of Windmill and Chapel Streets

Description: COMMON is an arts organisation which exists to support the UK theatre industry in achieving greater socio-economic diversity, and help working-class artists build sustainable careers in theatre. Title: Who's the Daddy Pig?
Description: Before starting stand-up comedy, Philip Simon was an actor, and the fact you didn't know that is testament to how successful he was! He eventually took on the prized role of Daddy Pig in the UK tour and West End run of Peppa Pig’s Party. A few years later another Daddy role came his way when his first son was born. But would parenting be as easy as Daddy Pig makes it look? Could everything really be resolved by jumping in muddy puddles? Come along and find out in Philip's new work-in-progress show.
Venue description: This family-run Italian restaurant on South Bridge hosts PBH Free Fringe comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am. No age restrictions before 10pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the building then performance space is down a flight of space.

Title: Stephen Buchanan: Purpleberry
Description:
Scottish Comedian of the Year runner-up 2017, Stephen Buchanan, comes to the Fringe with his debut solo show. Expect 45 minutes of sharp wit and offbeat observations as he explores his darkest fears, from commitment to dead-end jobs to children's literature. 'Skillful, personal and pitch perfect stand-up' (TheWeeReview.com). 'His material was tight and assuredly delivered' (Scotsman).
'His career's going places' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue description: A new PBH Free Fringe venue for 2018. 6 performance rooms with a wide selection of shows everyday. Bar and lounge open from 11am-1am.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Level access into the bar and performance spaces are up a flight of stairs (approx. 20+ stairs)

Title: Scotland Through the BeverAGES
Description: A boozy history of Scotland held on the most unique of venue – on board The Lochrin Belle canal boat. Join Greg and Joey, our resident drinks geeks, on an immersive journey into Scotland’s historic relationship with 'the water of life'. Prepare yourself for seven unique drinking experiences, each reflecting on an important age in Scotland’s past and how they made the Scotland of the present. From ancient ale to tomorrow’s tipples, we will delve into how each shaped the historic and social culture in Scotland, adrift on Edinburgh’s Union Canal. PS It’s on a boat.
Venue description: Fringe venue 508

Title: Flesh and Bone
Description:
Winner: The Pleasance's Charlie Hartill Award. Winner: Fringe First 2017.
Winner: Holden Street Theatre's Award. Feast your eyes upon the depravity, triumphs and utter hilarity of the underprivileged in a vivid and fast-paced ride through a working class estate which fuses Shakespeare-inspired lyricism with cockney accents. Award-winning Unpolished Theatre will thrust you into their stories, hold you by the scruff of the neck, and make you listen. Winner: Adelaide Critics’ Circle Award 2018. Winner: Bank SA Best Theatre Award – Adelaide Fringe 2018. Winner: Overall Best Theatre Award – Adelaide Fringe 2018. Sell-out show: Edinburgh Fringe 2017.
Warnings: Swearing, scenes of a sexual nature, violence, strobe lighting.
Artist: Unpolished Theatre in association with Eastlake Productions
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night. Open until 5am.

A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Title: Leith Brewing Heritage Tour with Tastings
Description: Escape the crowds and explore Leith with a local through its beer scene, past and present. Setting off from Customs Wharf, you’ll hear stories of Leith’s gritty past as a busy port and source of fortunes that built Edinburgh's stunning skyline. You'll discover today's vibrant arts, food and drink scene and visit local gems to sample award-winning beer from Leith’s exciting craft breweries. For history lovers or beer lovers, you’ll discover the authentic story of Leith while experiencing its exciting craft beer scene. Beer included. Non-beer and alcohol options available.
Warnings: Accessibility requirements should be advised in advance.
Venue description: Customs Wharf is a small street next to Customs House by the shore in Leith
Venue accessibility: Accessibility requirements should be advised in advance. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Cobbled street

Title: Comedy Car ft. Andrew Maxwell
Description: Uber is launching the most intimate travelling venue at Fringe, hosting a series of Andrew Maxwell comedy performances for absolutely free, from the back of a car. The Comedy Car gigs will last for 15 minutes, giving passengers an uproarious taste of Andrew’s cutting-edge observational comedy and acerbic social commentary while taking in the sights of the Scottish capital.
Warnings:
Guests will meet at the Comedy Car meeting point then be directed to the Uber car for the comedy show. 
Please do call 07791144243 once you get to the meeting point or if you're struggling to find it.
Venue description: Uber

Title: sick advice™ surgery
Description:
What’s your problem?! Drop in to our pop-up surgery for your very own tailor-made one-to-one comedy therapy session, guaranteed to solve your most pressing personal problem with the sickest advice in town! Founded in 1977, ill!™ specialises in providing badass assistance with sass, helping you access your inner insanity by injecting you with a healthy dose of sick solutions to alleviate all your worldly woes.
Couples and threesomes welcome during Happy Half-Hour! Claim your crackpot discount with proof of diagnosis if you’re a certified nutter! No advance booking necessary. Free to enter, pay negotiable consultation fee to leave!
Venue description: Recreational Vehicles repurposed for static fun. Museum, theatre, shopping and site seeing all catered for plus a well engineered catering galley servicing both wet and dry journeys.

Title: Vaudeville and Vice
Description: Swoon into the arms of the Roaring 20s with Vaudeville and Vice! Born in America, raised on the road – a classy coterie of dancing, singing circus swingers conjure an early-evening revue in the intimate Last Arch Theatre. We've got acrobatics, burlesque, hula hoops, aerial dance and more in the fast-talking sharp-dressed style of the Jazz Age! Cabaret duo Askew and Tracy are the centre of the show, with beloved artists like Russell Brunner and Ms Eliza joining them for guest appearances.
Warnings: Nudity, adult language, and playfully sexual material abounds.
Venue description: A brand new music and performance venue, comprising four grand arches with an inviting yard out front. Furnished with curiosities and a roaring fire at night, Fireside hosts an eclectic roster of acts alongside great beer, cocktails and street food from around the world.

Title: Chris Laker is Dead – Free
Description: Hi! I’m American comedian Chris Laker. I’m obsessed with my upcoming death and want to talk to you about it. My life too. It’s in joke/story form but it’s the life of a straight white man, you get it. It's free, so that pretty good.

Title: Does That Mean We're Not Going Bowling?
Description: Does That Mean We’re Not Going Bowling? may be the best debut comedy show at the Fringe this year. Telling a tale of painfully embarrassing experiences with a poignant conclusion, Simon Fraser will leave you laughing, amazed and most definitely not jealous. From a divorce in a Chinese restaurant to an ill-fated two days at a Sri Lankan drone company to an umbrella that just wouldn’t close, the stories in the poorly-acronymed DTMWNGB are sure to amuse, as are the sharp one-liners and hilarious protestations at occurrences in daily life. Not to miss.

Description: One of London’s hottest improv teams returns to the Fringe to bring you an hour of comedy inspired by music. Every show, we invite a guest musician to perform their hits, then Geraldyne take to the stage to turn those songs into improvised hilarity. From bluegrass to opera and folk music to heavy metal, come and delight in the unexpected at this made-up melodic extravaganza.

Title: Daddy Long Legs
Description: Join Jem (Best Newcomer Midlands Awards 2018), Joe (Chortle finalist 2015) and Horatio (Chortle semi-finalist 2018) for an absurd hour of stand-up about dads, insects, long hairy legs and dads. The three young comedians are well behaved, clean boys who bonded through a joint passion of building good relationships with their friend's mothers and solvent abuse. 'Wonderfully offbeat material' (Peter Fox, NottsComedyReview.wordpress.com).
Artist: Horatio Gould, Joe Bowley, Jem Braithwaite / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A friendly neighbourhood bar with a great choice of craft, cask beers, wines and spirits, friendly staff and a delicious new menu. Last orders during Fringe 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-Midnight.

Title: Women for Trump
Description: A verbatim play created from interviews conducted across America in late 2016, Women for Trump explores why five women were, or were not, persuaded to vote for Donald Trump. The play examines why such a vast number of women chose to vote for him, despite many considering him deeply misogynistic, and considers the long-term social and political factors which may have led to this. Combining analysis with humour and raw personal testimony, the play offers a powerful look at gender in the modern American political landscape, as well as in wider American society.
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival and part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces here we present three smart theatres offering a selection of small to mid scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, Acapella, music and cabaret. Description: Did you know that Edinburgh has a thriving comedy scene all year? Well now you do! Join Matt Duwell, as he presents the best of Edinburgh's comedy heroes and the pick of the scene's up-and-comers. Everybody performing is either from, or lives in, Edinburgh or the surrounding areas. Come and share the joy of the only performers on the Fringe who aren't being bankrupted by accommodation costs.
Venue description: A brand new music and performance venue, comprising four grand arches with an inviting yard out front. Furnished with curiosities and a roaring fire at night, Fireside hosts an eclectic roster of acts alongside great beer, cocktails and street food from around the world.

Become a Confident Profiler.

Andrew’s unique blend of mindreading creates an interactive experience that is

Description: Al Lubel also considered Mean Jewish Boy and Boy of Inaction as titles. He now realises that he should have chosen one of them. But he is still not sure which one. Venue description: This family-run Italian restaurant on South Bridge hosts PBH Free Fringe comedy in the basement from 1pm until midnight every day of the Fringe. Upstairs the freshest Italian cuisine is available 10am until 1am. No age restrictions before 10pm.

Title: DC's Marvels of Comedy
Description: DC's Marvels of Comedy is a stand-up compilation show with a difference. Each day Dan Cadey will host a mighty handful of comic marvels who will each put their powers to the test to be crowned DC's Ultimate Marvel of Comedy... and walk away with some trinket or other. Every hero has to start somewhere.

Nestled under the beautiful Georgian buildings on Dublin Street, it is a bar, eatery and late night den that coins its name from the infamous window tax era. We will be hosting a vast array of PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement lounge during the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There are 5 steps into the main body of the bar. There is a flight of stairs down into the performance area

Title: The Good, The Bad and The Irish
Description: In association with Bar Brig, and after four sold out tours in Europe, The Good The Bad and The Irish return to the festival for our eighth year! Join host Michael Porter as we showcase the best comedy talent from all over the world. 'Energetic and cocky' (The Stand Comedy Club). 'Damn funny!' (Culch.ie). 'Highly recommended' (BroadwayBaby.com).
Warnings: Strong language
Venue description: Brig Below, established in 2017 in the heart of Leith, is a brand new cellar venue available for live music, comedy, private functions and more. Brig Below can accommodate up to 80 people and customers have enjoyed its ripped-back interior and relaxed atmosphere hidden under our sister bar, Bar Brig at the bottom of Leith Walk.

Description: Gethin Alderman presents his new show all about limes. And sometimes other things. Join him for a fast-paced, physical 45-minute show of surreal character comedy and clown. It’s fun, it’s silly, it may contain facts. It definitely contains citrus fruit. You’ve probably seen him before, you just haven’t realised it yet. Come see him again. Praise for previous work: 'impeccable comic timing' (Campaign/Thinkbox).
Venue description: Hispaniola Restaurant, previously The Old Rutherford's Bar, Robert Louis Stevenson's favorite drinking haunt, has been converted into a beautiful homage to the famous Scots authors most renowned novel – Treasure Island. During the Fringe you can also watch a wide selection of family friendly PBH Free Fringe shows.

Artist: The Unmistakable Scent of Leopard (USOL) / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Located in the old Clydesdale Bank building on Lothian Rd Festival Square. During the Edinburgh Fringe we will be providing Free Fringe shows everyday, 25 taps of craft beers, amazing menu, outside seating area and integrated BottleDog!

Description: An interactive night of comedy organised by activist collective Pink Protest to raise money for Help Refugees. A guaranteed wild night that will actually make you feel good about yourself this Fringe.

Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving great food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Our two dedicated 50-seat performance spaces, presenting some of the best home-grown comedy at the Festival, are on the first and second floors.

Title: Marc Burrows – Mind Your Head
Description: Journalist, musician and stand-up Marc Burrows presents a surprisingly silly trek through psychiatric wards, suicide attempts, depression and bipolar diagnosis. With jokes. Lots of them. Relaxing smooth vocals, keys and sax deliver a sumptuous array from the great artists such as Nina Simone, Ray Charles, Ella Fitzgerald, Caro Emerald, Adele, Carole King, Frank Sinatra and Elvis.

Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Title: Pilgrim Comedy and Spoken Word
Description: Fantastic free comedy and spoken word at this established pub in the heart of the Old Town.

Description: In November 2010, Chris Larner accompanied his chronically ill ex-wife to Dignitas in Switzerland. He returned home with an empty wheelchair and a story to tell…This extraordinary one-man theatrical event has been acclaimed by press and public alike. Powerfully moving, gripping, poetic, by turns funny and heart-rending, Larner’s brilliant script and performance draws us inexorably into the haunting, human story of a woman making the ultimate decision about her own life. With footage from real indigenous Indians of the Amazonian rainforest we share what happens to the people living with the oil exploration and the illegal logging on an everyday basis. On screen they interact with the students giving a real insight into how they live.

'Truly excellent' ***** (FringeReview.co.uk). 'Literally made me gasp out loud' ***** (FringeGuru.com). 'Breathtaking' ***** (List). 'Deeply moving' ***** (Advertiser, Adelaide). 'One of the most heartfelt shows I've seen' ***** (Rip it Up). 'Uniquely delightful' ***** (West Australian). 'Beautifully delivered tale of friendship' ***** (Herald Sun). 'A must see!' ***** (Hairline.org.uk).

Description: When the Uber driver pulls up and asks if Terra is Hung, 'so hung' is usually the response. She use to meditate a lot. She was in a meditation group/cult. She had a guru. Title: Don Paterson

Teaser: Ulrike Almut Sandig’s translator Karen Leeder described Sandig as ‘one of the most exciting voices of her generation’, placing her somewhere between the oblique otherworldliness of Alice Oswald and the energy of Kate Tempest. Thick of It is...

Thick of It is Sandig’s first volume to appear in English. Here she and her translator combine to perform the German poet’s mesmerising work. Introduced by Daniel Hahn.

Title: #Jollyboat: Bards Against Humanity
Description: Fringe legends Jollyboat play their new comedy songs, following a sell-out national tour and the first JollyCon fan convention. Come see what all the buzz is about. ***** (ThreeWeeks). ***** (GeekChocolate.co.uk). ***** (InformedCities.co.uk).
Venue description: Part of The Liquid Room and offering 2 fantastic separate I stage rooms and beer garden music bar. The venue can be accessed from 9 Victoria Street. The Annexe & Warehouse Rooms will feature a wide and varied selection of PBH FREE FRINGE comedy, cabaret and music acts everyday during August from 11am - 1am. Five floors of pure performance. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. Eclectic electric entertainment. The spectacular Virgin Money Fireworks Concert brings together unforgettable orchestral classics from Edinburgh’s own Scottish Chamber Orchestra, and awe-inspiring fireworks, specially choreographed by international fireworks artists Pyrovision to enhance your musical experience – all set against the magnificent, historic backdrop of Edinburgh Castle.
Join the city of Edinburgh for this joyous celebration of summer festivals, inspirational music and breathtaking fireworks – marking the resplendent conclusion to the 2018 Edinburgh International Festival. Conducted by Clark Rundell, the Scottish Chamber Orchestra celebrates the centenary of the birth of Leonard Bernstein with a specially chosen selection of his foot-tapping, flamboyant music from West Side Story – with special guest artists Nicky Spence and Lucy Crowe.
After the interval, join the Orchestra for a mind-expanding journey into deepest space, with music from Gustav Holst’s visionary The Planets – from the overwhelming power of ‘Mars’ to the eerie beauty of ‘Venus’; from the seething energy of ‘Saturn’ to the majestic grandeur of ‘Jupiter’. All accompanied by a jaw-dropping display of fireworks from the Edinburgh Castle ramparts.
Over 400,000 fireworks launched from Edinburgh’s imposing Castle make this one of the biggest fireworks concerts in the world. Around a quarter of a million people gather across the city and beyond to share in this annual grand International Festival finale.

Returning to the International Festival after her serene but powerful debut Wind Resistance sold out in 2016, this year’s Scottish Songbook will breathe fresh meaning and life into folk songs that have been around for centuries. Karine will dig into her all-time favourite Scottish pop songs from the past fifty years, and explore the special musical landscape that she grew up in. From childhood memories of her mum’s Donovan and Gerry Rafferty LPs, through her young love of Big Country, Annie Lennox and The Blue Nile, she’ll also revisit maverick innovators like Bert Jansch and John Martyn, and celebrate current bands like Frightened Rabbit and Chvrches. Karine is joined onstage by a brilliant 6-piece band featuring Admiral Fallow’s lead singer and guitarist, Louis Abbott for a joyful evening of Scottish music gems.

Title: The Crooners
Description: An hour of non-stop, razor-sharp, unadulterated show business. Comedy, crooning, cocktails and class from critically acclaimed character comedians, Brendan Murphy and Kiell Smith-Bynoe (stars of BBC Radio 1's improvised comedy show BattleActs!). Frankie Paradise and Louie Valentine know all the hits! Join them on a journey through the golden age of crooners. A stupid, surreal and really really good looking musical comedy with live piano. 'Flamboyantly juicy' (Times). 'Fantastical, riotously funny characters' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'Had the audience wailing with laughter' **** (Skinny).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. Title: Looking for Lightning
Description: An inspirational story of courage, caution and perseverance and humor. Facing a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis head on, McLean takes us on a journey from the fast-paced life of Hollywood to Canada to India and the feet of yoga master BKS Iyengar. McLean’s journey is transformational for all. Looking for Lightning honours the legacy of BKS Iyengar as part of global celebrations marking the 100th anniversary of Iyengar’s birth and profound contribution to humanity. This piece has been created to raise awareness and provide hope of living well with multiple sclerosis.
Venue address: Royal Society of Edinburgh, 22 George Street
Venue description: C royale is our New Town hub, at the Royal Society of Edinburgh on George Street. Multiple smaller performance studios and larger theatres on one site, located close to the Mound and Princes Street. Also houses our pay what you think programme and film season. Part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 28th year at the Fringe.

Title: Sheeps: Live and Loud Selfie Sex Harry Potter
Description: Everything is going well in the wider world. No crises on the horizon. Seeing that the coast is finally clear, the Sheeps three are reuniting, despite never having broken up. It will be lots of new sketches and no old sketches. So if you mainly like our older stuff then this one’s not for you. But if you want to see new (wiser) sketches from some old masters (Time Out’s ‘Ones To Watch, 2011') then see it. ‘Clever, arch and multi-layered… hilarious’ (Guardian). ‘The future of British comedy’ (Skinny).
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night. Open until 5am.

Title: Foxdog Studios: Robot Chef
Description: After a year building an invoicing system in Stoke, rock and roll IT consultants Pete and Lloyd are having a party celebrating the end of dBASE IV. Returning with more music, characters, and baffling tech – including an augmented reality world and an audience controlled robot chef – this is their most ambitious show yet. As heard on BBC Radio 4 Extra. Nominated for the Chortle Award for Innovation and two Malcolm Hardee Awards in 2016. ***** (Skinny). **** (List). **** (Time Out).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.

Title: Andrew White: Coming of Age
Description: In 2017, Andrew White debuted his first solo show, It Was Funnier in My Head, unable to legally drink, have debt, or even get into some venues he was set to perform in! But this year, he's back and ready to do it all again with a new-found sense of adulthood... Now 18, I embark on a brand-new show, exploring what it means to be an adult and the world I am "grown-up" in. Through stand-up, poetry, and even experimental mime, I'll discuss every aspect of life for a teenager facing the "real world"...
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue
Venue description: PQA VENUES is located right at the heart of the Fringe in a prime position along the Royal Mile and housed inside Riddle's Court, a beautiful £5m refurbished Grade-II listed building. All three studios have comfortable seating and excellent audience facilities including a modern bar area and secluded court yard. A Destination Venue for theatre, stand-up, music and live music. Lifts make the building accessible to all.

John Lenahan has performed around the world as well as appearing in television shows for the BBC and ITV including: Stuff the White Rabbit, Secrets of Magic, Hoaxbusters and Red Dwarf. 'If there is a better sleight-of-hand merchant than this politely sardonic Philadelphian, I’ve yet to encounter them' (London Evening Standard). 'The mascot of a magical renaissance' (Guardian).

Title: Working Together: How Can Freelancers and Venues Work Effectively Together?
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme for Fringe participants. A practical workshop bringing together freelancers and venues to discuss what they need from each other before, during and after a contract. We will use case studies to highlight a variety of perspectives and facilitate discussion. You will leave with practical ideas that you can use to support positive, constructive working relationships. Contributors to be announced on Twitter through @FringeCentral.

Title: Pigs in Blankets
Description: ADAM, or Autocrats Destiny Altering Machine, is an absurd government that rules over its empire with an iron fist. On the single day of public holiday that they allow their subjects, a few miserable sods hatch a plan to overthrow them during their annual Associates Associate Association Meeting. The show is suited both to the politically minded who are concerned for the future of humanity, and to those who are looking to have a laugh at an alternate reality that is perhaps not so different to our own.
Warnings: Contains strong language.
Venue description: Paradise Green is at the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: Death Ray Cabaret
Description: After performing to sold out crowds in Toronto, Death Ray Cabaret returns to the Edinburgh Fringe with more fast-paced songs and break-neck banter. Silly, dark and delightful, come celebrate human life as we knew it with hilarious songs and characters. You'll leave the theatre with a smile on your face and a skip in your step as you head towards your impending doom!

Title: Swallow The Sea Caravan Theatre
Description: A converted 1960s caravan hosting installations both insightful and absurd, poetry, puppets and music... rotating shows touching on themes such as home, compass points and the agrarian industry. 'Total imagination immersion!' (Audience review, Edinburgh Fringe 2017). Check out swallowthesea.com/where--when for a changing daily programme. Non-ticketed, but suggested donation of £5 goes to the artists.
Venue description: Recreational Vehicles repurposed for static fun. Museum, theatre, shopping and site seeing all catered for plus a well engineered catering galley servicing both wet and dry journeys.

Title: The Tumbling Lassie
Description: A Fringe premiere performed together with Fergus of Galloway: two Scottish operas by Alexander McCall Smith set to music by Tom Cunningham, with a cast of singers, instrumentalists and a real acrobat! The Tumbling Lassie tells the true story of an acrobat in a circus in 17th-century Edinburgh and her escape from slavery with the help of a Borders family. Fergus of Galloway relates the exploits of a 12th-century knight as he puts himself through various challenges in order to win the hand of the beautiful Galiene, ruler of Lothian.
Venue description: Venue 41
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: Yes, That Nick Page, Apparently. Winner of English Comedian 2017
Description: Nick Page has had an interesting year, he won English Comedian of the year after coming second the previous year and being really grumpy about it. He had sell-out shows at the Perth and Adelaide Comedy festivals and he's appeared on Britain's Got Talent. This show doesn't have a theme, or a powerpoint, or a sad bit at 42 minutes followed by a redemptive bit at 52 minutes. It'll just be about 50 minutes of stories and jokes. Proper funny stuff, because he's a comic. Hope that's OK.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 288

Title: Joanne McNally: Wine Tamer
Description: Star and writer of Sky TV's Baby Hater and Ireland's brightest new comic, Joanne McNally returns to Edinburgh after her sell-out debut Bite Me last year, with her hysterical and whipsmart look on life, love and lies we tell ourselves. 'Fresh, bold and brazen, the sky is the limit for Joanne McNally' (Mirror). McNally has an excellent dose of 20th-century ennui and a true gift for storytelling.
Artist: Lisa Richards by arrangement with Off The Kerb
Venue description: Assembly George Square Studios are located opposite the entrance to Assembly George Square Gardens and next to Assembly George Square Theatre. The Studios have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe. All five Studios have comfortable modern seating, and the modern indoor Studios Bar has plenty of sofas, a much used piano and serves freshly prepared hot and cold meals.

Title: Penguinpig
Description: Sophie reads about an exciting creature called a Penguinpig on the internet. Filled with delight and intrigue she sets off alone on an adventure to find the adorable creature, leading her to the zoo. But what will she find inside? A fun-filled cautionary tale told through puppetry, that is both educational and highly entertaining. A story that is accessible on many levels, Penguinpig has plenty of engaging charm whilst carrying an important message for older children to consider with their grown-ups. 'The perfect outing for children' (Horncastle News). 'I've been humming Penguinpig songs to myself since' (Uttoxeter Advertiser).
Venue description: Assembly Roxy is a beautifully converted former church in Edinburgh's Old Town. The venue has two fully licensed indoor bars and the street outside has a pop up garden and bar during the Festival.

Title: Fronting
Description: Following its award-winning run at the Dublin International Gay Theatre Festival in 2017, Yellowbird Theatre are excited to present Fronting as their Edinburgh Festival Fringe debut. David is a young man, recently diagnosed with HIV, and anger and rage seem destined to consume him. However the arrival of Will in David's life could change everything for the better. If David lets it.

Title: Ahir Shah: Duffer
Description: Ahir Shah returns to Edinburgh with a new hour of stand-up about life and what comes after, death and what comes before, and Bohemian Rhapsody. Shah's last show, Control, enjoyed a critically acclaimed Fringe run, culminating in a nomination for Best Show at the 2017 Edinburgh Comedy Awards. This was followed by a UK tour, including three weeks at London's Soho Theatre. 'One of his generation’s most eloquent comic voices' **** (Telegraph). 'A scope and wit about him that is exciting to behold' **** (Times). 'Ratchets up the dismay to thermonuclear levels' **** (Guardian).
Artist: Soho Theatre in association with Avalon
